short_description.id: Långben Rese adalah raksasa mitologis (mytologisk jätte) dalam lagu-lagu rakyat Nordik, yang terkenal karena duelnya dengan pahlawan Vidrik Verlandsson.
short_description.en: Långben Rese is a mythological giant (mytologisk jätte) of Nordic folk ballads, best known for his duel with the hero Vidrik Verlandsson.

long_description.id: Långben Rese adalah raksasa mitologis (mytologisk jätte) dalam lagu-lagu rakyat (folkvisor) Nordik. Menurut tradisi, ia tinggal di Skottfjället dekat Brattön di paroki Bro, Bohuslän. Ia paling dikenal karena duelnya dengan pahlawan cerita Denmark (danska) Vidrik Verlandsson, yang berakhir dengan kemenangan Vidrik dan dipenggalnya kepala sang raksasa. Dalam Didrikssagan, raksasa ini disebut Etgeir.
long_description.en: Långben Rese is a mythological giant (mytologisk jätte) of Nordic folk ballads (folkvisor). According to tradition he lived at Skottfjället near Brattön in Bro parish, Bohuslän. He is best known for his duel with the Danish (danska) saga hero Vidrik Verlandsson, which ended with Vidrik winning and cutting off the giant's head. In the Didrikssagan the giant is called Etgeir.

long_description.id: Konon, setelah dipenggal, raksasa itu berlari tanpa kepala ke pertanian Bjälkebräcka di Hallinden, dan di sana tubuhnya dikuburkan dalam susunan batu berbentuk tiga cabang. Kepalanya dikatakan dikubur di sebuah ladang batu bulat zaman es yang di daerah itu disebut "Långbene rös". Vidrik Verlandsson sendiri adalah pahlawan dalam beberapa lagu rakyat Nordik, salah satu pejuang Didrik av Bern, yang menjadi termasyhur berkat kemenangannya atas raksasa ini.
long_description.en: After the beheading, the giant is said to have run headless to the farm Bjälkebräcka in Hallinden, where his headless body was buried in a three-pointed stone setting. His head is said to lie in an ice-age field of rounded stones known locally as "Långbene rös". Vidrik Verlandsson himself is the hero of several Nordic ballads, one of the warriors of Didrik av Bern, who became famous for his victory over this giant.

who.en: A giant of Nordic folk ballads.

role.en: Beheaded by Vidrik Verlandsson.

famous_for.id: Dalam Didrikssagan disebut Etgeir.
famous_for.en: Called Etgeir in the Didrikssagan.

did_you_know.id: Menurut tradisi Bohuslän, Långben Rese masih berlari tanpa kepala setelah dipenggal, dan tubuh serta kepalanya dikubur di dua tempat berbeda.
did_you_know.en: Bohuslän tradition says Långben Rese still ran headless after being beheaded, and his body and head were buried in two separate places.

description.id: Gunung tempat Långben Rese konon tinggal, dekat Brattön di Bro, Bohuslän.
description.en: Mountain where Långben Rese reputedly lived, near Brattön in Bro, Bohuslän.

description.id: Ladang batu tempat kepala raksasa itu konon dikubur.
description.en: Stone field where the giant's head is said to be buried.

note.id: Pahlawan yang mengalahkan dan memenggal Långben Rese.
note.en: The hero who defeated and beheaded Långben Rese.

claims.quote: Långben Rese är en mytologisk jätte i nordiska folkvisor.

statement.id: Långben Rese adalah raksasa mitologis (mytologisk jätte) dalam lagu rakyat Nordik (nordiska folkvisor).
statement.en: Långben Rese is a mythological giant (mytologisk jätte) in Nordic folk ballads (nordiska folkvisor).

claims.quote: Enligt traditionen skall han ha hållit till i Skottfjället nära Brattön i Bro socken i Bohuslän.

statement.id: Menurut tradisi (traditionen), ia tinggal di Skottfjället dekat Brattön di paroki (socken) Bro, Bohuslän.
statement.en: According to tradition (traditionen) he lived at Skottfjället near Brattön in Bro parish (socken), Bohuslän.

claims.quote: Han är mest känd för sin tvekamp med den danska sagohjälten Vidrik Verlandsson, som resulterade till att Vidrik segrar och hugger huvudet av jätten.

statement.id: Ia terkenal karena duelnya (tvekamp) dengan pahlawan Denmark (danska sagohjälten) Vidrik Verlandsson, yang menang dan memenggal kepala (huvudet) sang raksasa (jätten).
statement.en: He is best known for his duel (tvekamp) with the Danish saga hero (danska sagohjälten) Vidrik Verlandsson, who won and cut off the giant's (jätten) head (huvudet).

claims.quote: Resen skall då ha, huvudlöst, sprungit ner till gården Bjälkebräcka i Hallinden, och där fått sin huvudlösa kropp begraven i en treuddsformad stensättning.

statement.id: Raksasa itu konon berlari tanpa kepala (huvudlöst) ke pertanian (gården) Bjälkebräcka di Hallinden, dan tubuhnya (kropp) dikubur dalam susunan batu (stensättning) bercabang tiga.
statement.en: The giant reputedly ran headless (huvudlöst) to the farm (gården) Bjälkebräcka in Hallinden, where his body (kropp) was buried in a three-pointed stone setting (stensättning).

claims.quote: Huvudet skall ha begravts i ett istida klapperstensfält, som i bygden kallas för "Långbene rös".

statement.id: Kepalanya (huvudet) konon dikubur di ladang batu bulat zaman es (istida klapperstensfält) yang disebut "Långbene rös".
statement.en: His head (huvudet) is said to be buried in an ice-age field of rounded stones (istida klapperstensfält) called "Långbene rös".

claims.quote: Han är enligt dessa en av kämparna hos Didrik av Bern i Didrikssagan och blev hos denne särskilt ryktbar genom sin segerrika tvekamp med jätten Långben Rese (Didrikssagans Etgeir).

statement.id: Vidrik adalah salah satu pejuang (kämparna) Didrik av Bern dalam Didrikssagan, termasyhur (ryktbar) karena duelnya (tvekamp) dengan raksasa (jätten) Långben Rese, yang dalam Didrikssagan disebut Etgeir.
statement.en: Vidrik is one of the warriors (kämparna) of Didrik av Bern in the Didrikssagan, famous (ryktbar) for his duel (tvekamp) with the giant (jätten) Långben Rese, called Etgeir in the Didrikssagan.

short_description.id: Hippogryph (Pferdegreif dalam heraldik) adalah makhluk dongeng campuran, separuh griffin dan separuh kuda, yang muncul dalam epos kesatria Italia.
short_description.en: The hippogryph (Pferdegreif in heraldry) is a fabulous hybrid, half griffin and half horse, that appears in Italian chivalric epics.

long_description.id: Hippogryph (dari bahasa Italia ippogrifo, gabungan hippos, "kuda", dan kata Italia grifo, "griffin") adalah makhluk dongeng campuran yang separuh griffin dan separuh kuda. Menurut artikel de, istilah ini adalah ciptaan Matteo Maria Boiardo, yang menampilkan makhluk yang luar biasa cepat ini pada 1486 dalam L'Orlando Innamorato; pada 1532 Ariost mengambilnya ke dalam epos lanjutan Der rasende Roland. Artikel en justru menyebut makhluk ini ciptaan Ludovico Ariosto dalam Orlando Furioso pada awal abad ke-16, dengan bagian depan elang dan bagian belakang kuda.
long_description.en: The hippogryph (from Italian ippogrifo, combining hippos, "horse", and Italian grifo, "griffin") is a fabulous hybrid that is half griffin and half horse. According to the de article, the term was invented by Matteo Maria Boiardo, who featured this astonishingly fast creature in 1486 in L'Orlando Innamorato; in 1532 Ariost took it into his sequel epic Der rasende Roland. The en article instead credits Ludovico Ariosto's Orlando Furioso, early in the 16th century, picturing an eagle in front and a horse behind.

long_description.id: Gagasan makhluk ini berasal dari ungkapan terpelajar bahwa persilangan griffin dan kuda adalah hal yang mustahil; Boiardo kemungkinan terilhami Eclogae karya Vergil, yang memakai perkawinan semacam itu sebagai kiasan pernikahan yang absurd. Dalam syair Ariosto, hippogryph lahir dari kuda betina dan griffin, sangat cepat, dan dapat terbang mengelilingi dunia hingga ke Bulan. Roger (Ruggiero) menyelamatkan putri Angelica dari monster laut dengan menungganginya, dan Astolfo terbang ke Bulan untuk mencari akal Roland yang hilang.
long_description.en: The idea comes from a learned saying that crossing a griffin with a horse is impossible; Boiardo was probably inspired by Vergil's Eclogae, which use such a pairing as a metaphor for an absurd marriage. In Ariosto's poem the hippogryph is born of a mare and a griffin, is extremely fast, and can fly around the world and to the Moon. Roger (Ruggiero) rescues princess Angelica from a sea monster riding it, and Astolfo flies to the Moon to find Roland's lost wits.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah-kisah kemudian, misalnya Oberon karya Christoph Martin Wieland, hippogryph sering menjadi sinonim Pegasus. Ia juga muncul dalam fantasi modern seperti Dungeons & Dragons dan seri Harry Potter, dengan hippogreif Seidenschnabel yang berperan penting dalam buku ketiga. Dalam heraldik, motif ini dikenal sebagai Pferdegreif.
long_description.en: In later tales, such as Christoph Martin Wieland's Oberon, the hippogryph often stands for Pegasus. It also appears in modern fantasy such as Dungeons & Dragons and the Harry Potter series, where the hippogreif Seidenschnabel plays a key role in the third book. In heraldry the motif is known as the Pferdegreif.

who.en: Half griffin, half horse.

origin.id: Berasal dari epos Italia tentang Roland.

role.id: Sangat cepat dan dapat terbang ke Bulan.
role.en: Extremely fast and able to fly to the Moon.

famous_for.id: Dalam heraldik disebut Pferdegreif.
famous_for.en: Called Pferdegreif in heraldry.

did_you_know.id: Gagasan hippogryph lahir dari pepatah lama bahwa griffin dan kuda mustahil dikawinkan.
did_you_know.en: The hippogryph grew out of an old saying that a griffin and a horse could never be crossed.

note.en: Often a synonym for Pegasus in later tales.

claims.quote: Der Hippogryph (re-gräzisierte Form des italienischen ippogrifo, Zusammensetzung aus altgriechisch ἵππος hippos „Pferd“ und italienisch grifo „Greif“, dies aus lateinisch gryphus, dies wiederum aus altgriechisch γρύψ gryps) ist ein Fabelwesen im Sinne eines Mischwesens, das zur Hälfte Greif und zur anderen Hälfte Pferd ist.

statement.id: Hippogryph, dari ippogrifo (hippos, kuda/Pferd, dan grifo, griffin/Greif), adalah makhluk dongeng campuran (Mischwesen), separuh griffin dan separuh kuda.
statement.en: The hippogryph, from ippogrifo (hippos, horse/Pferd, and grifo, griffin/Greif), is a fabulous hybrid (Mischwesen), half griffin and half horse.

claims.quote: Der aus dem Griechischen gebildete Begriff ist eine Erfindung von Matteo Maria Boiardo, der das unglaublich schnell rasende Fabelwesen 1486 in seinem Roman „Der verliebte Roland“ (L’Orlando Innamorato) auftreten ließ. 1532 übernahm Ariost den „Ross-Greif“ in sein Fortsetzungs-Epos „Der rasende Roland“.

statement.id: Istilah ini ciptaan (Erfindung) Matteo Maria Boiardo dalam L'Orlando Innamorato (1486); pada 1532 Ariost mengambil "Ross-Greif" dalam Der rasende Roland.
statement.en: The term is an invention (Erfindung) of Matteo Maria Boiardo in L'Orlando Innamorato (1486); in 1532 Ariost took the "Ross-Greif" into Der rasende Roland.

claims.quote: Die Idee zu dem Mischwesen basiert auf einer gelehrten Redewendung, wonach eine Kreuzung zwischen einem Greif und einem Pferd ein Ding der Unmöglichkeit sei. Vermutlich wurde Boiardo von einer Stelle in den Eclogae des Vergil inspiriert

statement.id: Gagasan (Idee) makhluk ini berasal dari ungkapan (Redewendung) bahwa persilangan griffin (Greif) dan kuda (Pferd) mustahil; Boiardo mungkin terilhami Eclogae karya Vergil.
statement.en: The idea (Idee) rests on a saying (Redewendung) that crossing a griffin (Greif) and a horse (Pferd) is impossible; Boiardo was probably inspired by Vergil's Eclogae.

claims.quote: Roger (Ruggiero) rettet mit seiner Hilfe die schöne Prinzessin Angelica vor einem Meeresungeheuer, und der englische Prinz Astolfo fliegt auf dem Hippogryphen sogar zum Mond, um dort Rolands verlorenen Verstand wiederzufinden.

statement.id: Roger (Ruggiero) menyelamatkan putri (Prinzessin) Angelica dari monster laut (Meeresungeheuer), dan Astolfo terbang ke Bulan (Mond) untuk mencari akal Roland.
statement.en: Roger (Ruggiero) rescues princess (Prinzessin) Angelica from a sea monster (Meeresungeheuer), and Astolfo flies to the Moon (Mond) to find Roland's wits.

claims.quote: The hippogriff (Italian: ippogrifo ) or hippogryph is a legendary creature with the front half of an eagle and the hind half of a horse.

statement.id: Hippogriff (Italia: ippogrifo, Italian) adalah makhluk legenda berbagian depan elang dan belakang kuda.
statement.en: The hippogriff (Italian: ippogrifo) is a legendary creature with an eagle's front half and a horse's hind half.

claims.quote: It was invented at the beginning of the 16th century by Ludovico Ariosto in his Orlando Furioso. Within the poem, the hippogriff is a steed born of a mare and a griffin—something considered impossible. It is extremely fast and is presented as being able to fly around the world and to the Moon.

statement.id: Makhluk ini diciptakan Ludovico Ariosto dalam Orlando Furioso pada awal abad ke-16; lahir dari kuda betina dan griffin, sangat cepat, terbang mengelilingi dunia dan ke Bulan (Moon).
statement.en: It was invented by Ludovico Ariosto in Orlando Furioso early in the 16th century; born of a mare and a griffin, extremely fast, able to fly around the world and to the Moon.

claims.quote: In späteren Erzählungen, z. B. bei dem deutschen Dichter Christoph Martin Wieland (Oberon), taucht der Hippogryph oft als Synonym für Pegasus auf.

statement.id: Dalam kisah kemudian, misalnya Oberon karya Christoph Martin Wieland, hippogryph sering menjadi sinonim (Synonym) Pegasus.
statement.en: In later tales, e.g. Christoph Martin Wieland's Oberon, the hippogryph is often a synonym (Synonym) for Pegasus.

claims.quote: In der deutschen Übersetzung der Harry-Potter-Romane von Joanne K. Rowling wird die Form „Hippogreif“ verwendet, die aber den in anderen Sprachen üblichen Bezeichnungen näher kommt. Im Englischen werden sowohl hippogriff (so bei Rowling) als auch hippogryph verwendet. Der Hippogreif Seidenschnabel spielt eine Schlüsselrolle im dritten Band

statement.id: Terjemahan Jerman (deutschen) novel Harry Potter karya Joanne K. Rowling memakai bentuk Hippogreif; Seidenschnabel adalah hippogreif dalam buku ketiga.
statement.en: The German (deutschen) translation of Joanne K. Rowling's Harry Potter novels uses the form Hippogreif; Seidenschnabel is a hippogreif in the third book.

claims.quote: In der Heraldik ist das Motiv unter der Bezeichnung Pferdegreif bekannt.

statement.id: Dalam heraldik (Heraldik) motif ini dikenal sebagai Pferdegreif.
statement.en: In heraldry (Heraldik) the motif is known as the Pferdegreif.

claims.quote: For him a filly to griffin bore; Hight hippogryph. In wings and beak and crest, Formed like his sire, as in the feet before; But like the mare, his dam, in all the rest. Such on Riphaean hills, though rarely found,

statement.id: Syair Orlando furioso: anak kuda betina dari griffin, bernama hippogryph, bersayap dan berparuh seperti ayahnya, selebihnya seperti induknya; jarang ditemukan di pegunungan Riphaean (Riphaean hills).
statement.en: Orlando furioso verse: a filly bore him to a griffin, hight hippogryph, with wings and beak like his sire, the rest like the mare; rarely found on the Riphaean hills.

claims.quote: Gelegentlich taucht der Hippogryph in der modernen Fantasy auf, so unter anderem in Eric Rücker Eddisons Der Wurm Ouroboros (1922) und im Rollenspiel Dungeons & Dragons.

statement.id: Hippogryph kadang muncul dalam fantasi modern (modernen Fantasy), antara lain dalam Der Wurm Ouroboros karya Eric Rücker Eddison (1922) dan permainan peran Dungeons & Dragons.
statement.en: The hippogryph sometimes appears in modern fantasy (modernen Fantasy), including Eric Rücker Eddison's Der Wurm Ouroboros (1922) and the role-playing game Dungeons & Dragons.

claims.quote: The word hippogriff was adopted into English shortly before 1615; prior to this, John Harington's 1591 translation of Orlando furioso called the creature a "Griffith horse."

statement.id: Kata hippogriff masuk ke bahasa Inggris (English) menjelang 1615; terjemahan John Harington (1591) menyebutnya "Griffith horse".
statement.en: The word hippogriff entered English shortly before 1615; John Harington's 1591 translation called it a "Griffith horse".

short_description.id: Black Dog of Newgate adalah legenda hantu anjing hitam raksasa yang menghantui bekas Penjara Newgate, London, dan dikaitkan dengan kisah penyihir yang dibunuh narapidana saat kelaparan.
short_description.en: The Black Dog of Newgate is a legend of a monstrous black dog haunting the former Newgate Prison in London, tied to the story of a sorcerer killed by inmates during a famine.

long_description.id: Black Dog of Newgate adalah legenda tentang hantu di bekas Penjara Newgate, London, yang terletak di sebelah Old Bailey. Kisah ini contoh kategori Black Dog Inggris, yaitu anjing pemburu hantu pertanda buruk atau berniat jahat. Catatan tertuanya berasal dari 1596 dan dikreditkan kepada narapidana bernama Luke Hutton.
long_description.en: The Black Dog of Newgate is a legend about a haunting at the former Newgate Prison in London, which stood beside the Old Bailey. It is an example of the English Black Dog type, a spectral hound of ill omen or malicious intent. The earliest recorded account dates from 1596 and is credited to an inmate named Luke Hutton.

long_description.id: Dalam ceritanya, saat kelaparan pada masa Raja Henry III dari Inggris, seorang cendekiawan yang dikenal sebagai penyihir dipenjara di Newgate. Para narapidana, yang sudah beralih ke kanibalisme, memakannya. Tak lama kemudian mereka konon melihat anjing hitam raksasa yang dianggap arwah sang penyihir; ia membunuh dan memakan para pelaku satu per satu sampai penyintas terakhir kabur dari penjara.
long_description.en: The tale is set during a famine under England's King Henry III, when a scholar reputed to be a sorcerer was locked up in Newgate. The prisoners, who had already turned to cannibalism, ate him. Soon afterwards they reportedly saw a monstrous black dog taken to be the sorcerer's spirit; it killed and ate those responsible one by one until the last survivors broke out of the prison.

long_description.id: Menjelang akhir narasi, orang asing tak bernama itu mengaku kisah anjing roh tidak benar dan satu-satunya Black Dog yang ia dengar adalah batu hitam besar di ruang bawah tanah. Kisah ini dimaksudkan sebagai cerita moral melawan hidup nista para narapidana.
long_description.en: Towards the end of the narrative the unnamed stranger says the spirit-dog tale is untrue and the only Black Dog he has heard of is a great black stone in the dungeon. The story was meant as a morality tale against the base living of the inmates.

long_description.id: Ada spekulasi bahwa hantu ini berkaitan dengan Amen Court di dekatnya. Menurut sumber kedua, hantunya muncul sebagai bentuk hitam tak berbentuk yang menyelinap di sepanjang dinding dan mengeluarkan bau menjijikkan, disertai bunyi langkah diseret.
long_description.en: There is speculation that the haunting is linked with nearby Amen Court. The second source reports a ghost in the form of a formless black shape that creeps along walls, gives off a foul smell, and is accompanied by the sound of dragging footsteps.

short_description.id: Barak adalah anjing suci dalam mitologi Turk: anjing legendaris yang dianggap bukan anjing biasa, yang dalam sebagian legenda menetas dari telur burung Kerkes dan ditunggangi para dukun menuju langit.
short_description.en: Barak is the sacred dog of Turkic mythology: a legendary hound held to be no ordinary dog, which in some legends hatches from an egg of the bird Kerkes and is ridden by shamans up to the sky.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Turk, Barak dikenal sebagai anjing suci. Kedua sumber menyebutnya jenis anjing legendaris yang tidak dianggap anjing biasa, melainkan makhluk yang diberkati. Di Anadolu, nama yang sama juga dipakai untuk anjing pemburu yang berbulu lebat dan sangat cepat larinya.
long_description.en: In Turkic mythology Barak is known as the sacred dog. Both sources describe it as a legendary kind of dog that is not regarded as an ordinary animal but as a blessed being. In Anadolu the same name is also used for shaggy hunting dogs that run very fast.

long_description.id: Menurut sebagian legenda, ketika burung Kerkes menjadi tua ia meninggalkan dua telur: dari salah satunya lahir Barak, dari yang lain seekor anak burung. Para dukun dipercaya naik ke langit dengan menunggangi Barak dan konon mengenakan lambang-lambangnya di leher mereka.
long_description.en: According to some legends, when the bird Kerkes grows old it leaves two eggs: Barak emerges from one of them and a chick from the other. Shamans are believed to rise to the sky mounted on Barak and are said to wear its symbols around their necks.

long_description.id: Nama Barak juga dikenakan pada manusia berkepala anjing dalam legenda. Artikel pertama mencatat bahwa adanya seorang wali bernama Barak Ata atau Barak Baba di Anadolu tidak dianggap kebetulan.
long_description.en: The name Barak is also applied to legendary dog-headed people. The first article notes that the presence of a saint called Barak Ata or Barak Baba in Anadolu is not regarded as a coincidence.

literal_meaning.id: Akar Bar memuat makna sukacita dan kebanggaan; dalam bahasa Mongol Bar berarti harimau dan Barah berarti perdamaian.
literal_meaning.en: The root Bar carries meanings of joy and pride; in Mongolian Bar means tiger and Barah means peace.

statement.en: It is believed that shamans (şamanlar) ascend to the sky (göğe çıktıkları) riding Barak, and they are said to wear its symbols (simgelerini) on their necks.

claims.quote: Anadolu'da Barak Ata (Barak Baba) adlı bir evliyanın yer alması tesadüfi değildir.

statement.id: Keberadaan seorang wali (evliya) bernama Barak Ata (Barak Baba) di Anadolu dianggap bukan kebetulan.
statement.en: The presence in Anadolu of a saint (evliya) named Barak Ata (Barak Baba) is said to be no coincidence (tesadüfi değildir).

claims.quote: Efsânevî köpek başlı insanlara da Barak adı verilir.

statement.id: Nama Barak juga diberikan kepada manusia berkepala anjing dalam legenda.
statement.en: The name Barak is also given to legendary dog-headed people (köpek başlı insanlara).

claims.quote: Anlam: (Bar/Var). Eski Türkçe ve eski Altayca'da Bar kökü sevinç ve gurur gibi içeriklere sâhiptir.

statement.id: Nama ini berasal dari akar Bar/Var; dalam bahasa Turk Kuno dan Altai Kuno akar Bar memuat makna sukacita dan kebanggaan.
statement.en: The name is from the root Bar/Var; in Old Turkic (Eski Türkçe) and Old Altaic (eski Altayca) the root Bar carries meanings such as joy and pride (sevinç ve gurur).

claims.quote: Moğolca'da Barah sözcüğü ateşkes, barış gibi anlamlar taşır. Bar ise kaplan demektir.

statement.id: Dalam bahasa Mongol kata Barah bermakna gencatan senjata dan perdamaian, sedangkan Bar berarti harimau.
statement.en: In Mongolian (Moğolcada) the word Barah means truce and peace (ateşkes, barış), while Bar means tiger (kaplan).

short_description.id: Beast of Bodmin adalah hewan mirip kucing besar yang konon terlihat di Bodmin Moor, Cornwall, Inggris, dan dianggap sebagai salah satu "British big cats".
short_description.en: The Beast of Bodmin is a big-cat-like animal reportedly seen on Bodmin Moor in Cornwall, England, counted among the 'British big cats'.

long_description.id: Beast of Bodmin (atau Beast of Bodmin Moor) adalah salah satu kucing besar Britania (British big cats) yang paling terkenal, yang dituduh membunuh ternak. Menurut artikel ru, hewan mirip kucing besar ini terlihat lebih dari 60 kali sejak 1983 di Bodmin Moor, Cornwall, Inggris, dan diduga panther atau puma yang lepas dari kebun binatang atau koleksi pribadi. Penyelidikan pemerintah pada 1995 tidak menemukan bukti keberadaan hewan semacam itu, meski laporan penampakan terus berlanjut. Menurut artikel it, makhluk itu konon mirip puma berwarna abu-abu gelap hingga hitam dan juga terlihat di Devon dan Somerset.
long_description.en: The Beast of Bodmin (or Beast of Bodmin Moor) is one of the best-known British big cats, blamed for killing livestock. According to the ru article this big-cat-like animal has been seen more than 60 times since 1983 on Bodmin Moor in Cornwall, England, and is thought to be a panther or puma escaped from a zoo or private collection. A government inquiry in 1995 found no evidence of such animals, though sightings continued. According to the it article it is said to look like a puma, dark grey to black, and has also been reported in Devon and Somerset.

long_description.id: Ketika sebuah tengkorak yang ditemukan di Sungai Fowey diserahkan kepada Natural History Museum sebagai bukti keberadaannya, tengkorak itu ternyata dipotong dari permadani kulit macan tutul. Menurut artikel ru, tengkorak yang ditemukan pada 1995 itu memang milik macan tutul jantan muda, tetapi hewan itu tidak dibunuh di Inggris. Para ilmuwan menyatakan laporan semacam itu biasanya tidak dapat dipercaya, karena kelangsungan populasi memerlukan jumlah individu yang tak masuk akal, sedangkan iklim dan sulitnya mencari makan membuat hewan yang lepas sulit bertahan.
long_description.en: When a skull found in the River Fowey was offered to the Natural History Museum as proof of the beast, it turned out to have been cut from a leopard-skin rug. According to the ru article that skull, found in 1995, did belong to a young male leopard, but the animal had not been killed in England. Scientists say such reports are usually unreliable, since a lasting population would need an implausible number of animals, while the climate and scarce prey make survival of escaped cats unlikely.

short_description.id: Beast of Exmoor adalah kucing besar misterius yang dilaporkan berkeliaran di Exmoor, Devon dan Somerset, dan terkenal sejak pembantaian domba tahun 1983.
short_description.en: The Beast of Exmoor is a mysterious big cat reported to roam Exmoor in Devon and Somerset, famous since the sheep killings of 1983.

long_description.id: Beast of Exmoor adalah salah satu kisah kucing besar Britania yang paling terkenal: kucing kriptozoologi berbulu abu-abu gelap atau hitam yang dilaporkan berkeliaran di pedesaan Exmoor, terutama Devon dan Somerset. Penampakan dilaporkan sejak 1970, dan kisahnya menjadi berita nasional pada 1983 ketika lebih dari seratus domba mati dengan leher terkoyak di South Molton.
long_description.en: The Beast of Exmoor is one of the best-known British big cat stories: a cryptozoological cat with dark grey or black fur reported in rural Exmoor, especially Devon and Somerset. Sightings were reported from 1970, and the story became national news in 1983 when more than a hundred sheep were killed with torn throats at South Molton.

long_description.id: Makhluk itu diduga macan tutul hitam atau puma yang dilepas secara ilegal, tetapi tidak ada kucing besar yang pernah dipastikan, dan pembantaian 1983 kini dikaitkan dengan penyebab lain seperti anjing besar. Bangkai yang pernah diberitakan sebagai Beast of Exmoor ternyata anjing laut mati.
long_description.en: It was thought to be an illegally released black leopard or puma, but no big cat has ever been confirmed, and the 1983 killings are now attributed to causes such as large dogs. A carcass once reported as the Beast of Exmoor proved to be a dead seal.

short_description.id: Çarşamba Karısı adalah sosok perempuan menakutkan dalam kepercayaan rakyat di Azerbaijan dan Anadolu, yang marah dan membawa celaka ke rumah tempat orang bekerja pada malam Rabu atau membiarkan pekerjaan tak selesai.
short_description.en: Çarşamba Karısı is a frightening female figure of folk belief in Azerbaijan and Anadolu who grows angry and brings harm to houses where people work on Wednesday night or leave work unfinished.

long_description.id: Di Azerbaijan dan sebagian daerah Anadolu, Çarşamba Karısı (juga Çarşamba Avradı) dibayangkan sebagai perempuan buruk rupa, berpakaian jelek, dan menakutkan. Ia marah bila ada pekerjaan dilakukan pada malam Rabu, lalu mendatangkan keburukan pada rumah tersebut.
long_description.en: In Azerbaijan and parts of Anadolu, Çarşamba Karısı (also Çarşamba Avradı) is imagined as an ugly, poorly dressed and frightening woman. She becomes angry when work is done on Wednesday night and then brings misfortune upon that household.

long_description.id: Pada hari Rabu ia disebut masuk ke rumah-rumah yang masih menyimpan pekerjaan belum rampung dan membuat semuanya kacau, serta mencelakai penghuninya. Ia tidak gentar kepada siapa pun dan membawa pergi anak-anak secara terang-terangan di hadapan semua orang, bukan sembunyi-sembunyi.
long_description.en: On Wednesdays she is said to enter houses where work is left unfinished, throw everything into confusion and harm the occupants. She fears nobody and takes children away openly in front of everyone rather than in secret.

long_description.id: Kedua sumber mengaitkannya dengan Alkarısı, dan artikel pertama memandangnya lebih sebagai unsur memorat sejenis hantu, jin, peri, atau momok ketimbang makhluk mitologis. Dalam bahasa sehari-hari, ungkapan Çarşamba Karısı juga dipakai secara kiasan untuk perempuan yang rambut dan pakaiannya acak-acakan.
long_description.en: Both sources link her with Alkarısı, and the first article regards her more as a memorate element akin to ghosts, jinn, fairies or bogeys than as a mythological creature. In everyday speech, the expression Çarşamba Karısı is also used figuratively for a woman whose hair and clothes are in disarray.

who.id: Çarşamba Karısı adalah sosok perempuan menakutkan dalam kepercayaan rakyat.

role.en: She punishes households that work on Wednesday night or leave work unfinished.

claims.quote: Azerbaycan'da ve Anadolu'nun kimi yörelerinde Çarşamba gecesi iş yapılırsa öfkelenen ve o eve kötülük getiren çirkin, kötü giysili, ürkütücü bir kadın olduğu söylenen

statement.id: Di Azerbaijan dan sebagian daerah Anadolu, Çarşamba Karısı disebut sebagai perempuan buruk rupa, berpakaian jelek, dan menakutkan yang marah dan membawa celaka ke rumah bila ada yang bekerja pada malam Rabu (Çarşamba gecesi).
statement.en: In Azerbaijan (Azerbaycan) and some parts of Anadolu, Çarşamba Karısı is said to be an ugly, badly dressed, frightening woman (ürkütücü bir kadın) who grows angry and brings harm to the house (eve kötülük getiren) if work is done on Wednesday night (Çarşamba gecesi).

claims.quote: (Çarşamba Avradı) olarak anılır. Çarşamba günleri bitirilmemiş işler bulunan evlere girerek ortalığı karıştırdığı anlatılır.

statement.id: Ia juga disebut Çarşamba Avradı; konon pada hari Rabu ia masuk ke rumah-rumah yang memiliki pekerjaan belum selesai dan mengacaukan segalanya.
statement.en: It is also called Çarşamba Avradı; it is said to enter houses with unfinished work (bitirilmemiş işler bulunan evlere) on Wednesdays and throw everything into disorder (ortalığı karıştırdığı).

claims.quote: Kimseden korkmaz ve çocukları gizlice değil, herkesin gözü önünde alıp kaçırır.

statement.id: Ia tidak takut kepada siapa pun dan membawa lari anak-anak bukan diam-diam, melainkan di depan mata semua orang.
statement.en: It fears no one (kimseden korkmaz) and carries off children (çocukları alıp kaçırır) not secretly but before everyone's eyes (herkesin gözü önünde).

claims.quote: Türkçe'de mecâzen saçı başı karmakarışık, paspal, özensiz kadın anlamına da gelir.

statement.id: Secara kiasan, dalam bahasa Turki ungkapan ini juga berarti perempuan yang rambutnya kusut dan berpenampilan acak-acakan.
statement.en: Figuratively (mecâzen), in Turkish (Türkçe'de) the expression also means a woman with tangled hair and an untidy, careless appearance (özensiz kadın).

claims.quote: Çarşamba Karısı, Türkçede saçı başı karmakarışık, üstü başı özensiz kadın anlamında kullanılır. Zaman zaman Alkarısı'na tekabül eder.

statement.id: Çarşamba Karısı dipakai untuk menyebut perempuan berambut kusut dan berpakaian acak-acakan; kadang-kadang ia disamakan dengan Alkarısı.
statement.en: Çarşamba Karısı is used (kullanılır) for a woman with tangled hair and careless clothing (özensiz kadın); at times it corresponds to Alkarısı (Alkarısı'na tekabül eder).

claims.quote: Mitolojik bir yaratıktan ziyade hortlak, hayalet, -genel anlamda- cin, peri, öcü, dunganga türünde bir memorat unsurudur.

statement.id: Menurut artikel pertama, Çarşamba Karısı lebih merupakan unsur memorat sejenis hantu, arwah, jin, peri, atau momok daripada makhluk mitologis.
statement.en: According to the first article, Çarşamba Karısı is less a mythological creature (mitolojik bir yaratıktan ziyade) than a memorate element (memorat unsuru) of the type of revenant, ghost (hortlak, hayalet), jinn, fairy or bogey (cin, peri, öcü).

claims.quote: Yine Anadolu inançlarında haftanın belirli bir günü, yarım kalan işlerin olduğu evlere gelerek işleri karıştıran, insanlara kötülük yapan dişi varlık olarak tanımlanır.

statement.id: Dalam kepercayaan Anadolu ia digambarkan sebagai makhluk betina yang pada hari tertentu dalam sepekan datang ke rumah dengan pekerjaan yang belum selesai, mengacaukan pekerjaan itu, dan mencelakai orang.
statement.en: In Anadolu beliefs (Anadolu inançlarında) it is described as a female being (dişi varlık) that on a certain day of the week comes to houses with unfinished work (yarım kalan işlerin olduğu evlere), muddles the work and harms people (insanlara kötülük yapan).

short_description.id: Dyrnwch Gawr adalah raksasa (cawr) dalam tradisi Welsh yang dikenal sebagai pemilik kuali ajaib, salah satu dari Tiga Belas Pusaka Pulau Britania; kuali itu tidak mau merebus daging untuk pengecut.
short_description.en: Dyrnwch Gawr is a giant (cawr) of Welsh tradition known as the owner of a magic cauldron, one of the Thirteen Treasures of the Island of Britain; the cauldron will not boil meat for a coward.

long_description.id: Dyrnwch Gawr, juga dieja Dyrnhwch Gawr, adalah raksasa Welsh (cawr Cymreig) yang dikaitkan dengan Hen Ogledd dan dengan Gwent. Naskah-naskah daftar pusaka juga memuat ejaan Dyrnog dan Tyrnog. Selain dalam daftar pusaka, namanya muncul dalam daftar raksasa Cymru yang disusun Siôn Dafydd Rhys pada akhir abad ke-16, dengan keterangan bahwa ia berada di negeri Ewias.
long_description.en: Dyrnwch Gawr, also spelled Dyrnhwch Gawr, is a Welsh giant (cawr Cymreig) associated with the Hen Ogledd and with Gwent. The manuscripts of the treasure list also give the spellings Dyrnog and Tyrnog. Besides the treasure list, his name appears in the list of the giants of Cymru compiled by Siôn Dafydd Rhys at the end of the 16th century, which places him in the land of Ewias.

long_description.id: Ia terutama dikenal sebagai pemilik kuali istimewa dalam daftar Tri Thlws ar Ddeg Ynys Prydain (Tiga Belas Pusaka Pulau Britania). Kuali itu membedakan pemberani dari pengecut: daging untuk orang pengecut tidak akan pernah mendidih di dalamnya, sedangkan daging untuk orang pemberani cepat matang. Pusaka-pusaka itu digambarkan sebagai benda ajaib tradisi Welsh yang disebut dalam naskah abad ke-15 dan ke-16, dan kebanyakan dikaitkan dengan 'Utara'.
long_description.en: He is known chiefly as the owner of a special cauldron in the list Tri Thlws ar Ddeg Ynys Prydain (the Thirteen Treasures of the Island of Britain). The cauldron tells the brave from the cowardly: meat for a coward will never boil in it, while meat for a brave man cooks quickly. The treasures are described as magical items of Welsh tradition mentioned in 15th- and 16th-century manuscripts, most of them linked with 'The North'.

long_description.id: Kisah kuali ini hampir pasti bersumber dari rujukan pada 'kuali Diwrnach Wyddel' dalam kisah Culhwch ac Olwen, dan karena nama Dyrnwch dan Diwrnach sangat mirip, nama pertama kemungkinan bentuk yang lebih muda dari yang kedua. Sifat serupa dikenakan pada kuali Pen Annwn dalam puisi 'Preiddiau Annwn' di Llyfr Taliesin, yang tidak merebus makanan pengecut. Walaupun pusaka-pusaka itu dikaitkan dengan Hen Ogledd, Dyrnwch tidak disebut dalam silsilah seperti Bonedd Gwŷr y Gogledd.
long_description.en: The story of the cauldron is almost certainly based on a reference to 'the cauldron of Diwrnach Wyddel' in the tale Culhwch ac Olwen, and because the names Dyrnwch and Diwrnach are so alike, the former is probably a later form of the latter. A similar virtue is given to the cauldron of Pen Annwn in the poem 'Preiddiau Annwn' in Llyfr Taliesin, which does not boil a coward's food. Although the treasures are linked with the Hen Ogledd, Dyrnwch is not mentioned in genealogies such as Bonedd Gwŷr y Gogledd.

long_description.id: Culhwch ac Olwen juga memuat tokoh lain bernama Wrnach Gawr, pemilik sebilah pedang istimewa. Mungkin ada hubungan antara Wrnach Gawr dan Diwrnach Wyddel, dan Dyrnwch Gawr mungkin perkembangan lebih kemudian dari tokoh-tokoh itu, tetapi hal ini tidak dapat dibuktikan secara pasti.
long_description.en: Culhwch ac Olwen also contains another character called Wrnach Gawr, who owns a special sword. There may be a link between Wrnach Gawr and Diwrnach Wyddel, and Dyrnwch Gawr may be a later development based on those characters, but this cannot be proven conclusively.

literal_meaning.en: the name Dyrnwch is probably a later form of the name Diwrnach; 'Gawr' means 'the Giant'

claims.quote: Cawr Cymreig a gysylltir â'r Hen Ogledd ac â Gwent yw Dyrnwch Gawr (amrywiad, Dyrnhwch Gawr).

statement.id: Dyrnwch Gawr (varian: Dyrnhwch Gawr) adalah raksasa Welsh (cawr Cymreig) yang dikaitkan dengan Hen Ogledd dan Gwent.
statement.en: Dyrnwch Gawr (variant: Dyrnhwch Gawr) is a Welsh giant (cawr Cymreig) associated with the Hen Ogledd and with Gwent.

claims.quote: Enwir Dyrnwch Gawr yn y rhestr Tri Thlws ar Ddeg Ynys Prydain fel perchennog pair arbennig

statement.id: Dyrnwch Gawr disebut dalam daftar Tri Thlws ar Ddeg Ynys Prydain sebagai pemilik (perchennog) kuali (pair) istimewa.
statement.en: Dyrnwch Gawr is named in the list Tri Thlws ar Ddeg Ynys Prydain as the owner (perchennog) of a special cauldron (pair).

claims.quote: pe rhoid ynddo gig i ŵr llwfr i ferwi, ni ferwai fyth; o rhoid iddo gig i ŵr dewr, berwi a wnâi yn ebrwydd

statement.id: Jika daging (cig) untuk orang pengecut (llwfr) dimasukkan untuk direbus, daging itu tidak akan pernah mendidih (ni ferwai fyth); jika daging untuk orang pemberani (dewr), ia cepat mendidih (berwi).
statement.en: If meat (cig) for a coward (llwfr) were put in to boil, it would never boil (ni ferwai fyth); if meat for a brave man (dewr), it would boil (berwi) quickly.

claims.quote: Priodolir rhinwedd cyffelyb i'r Pair Pen Annwn y cyfeirir ato yn y gerdd 'Preiddiau Annwn' yn Llyfr Taliesin, sydd ddim yn berwi bwyd llwfrgi.

statement.id: Sifat serupa dikenakan pada Pair Pen Annwn yang disebut dalam puisi 'Preiddiau Annwn' di Llyfr Taliesin, yang tidak merebus (berwi) makanan pengecut (llwfrgi).
statement.en: A similar virtue is attributed to the Pair Pen Annwn mentioned in the poem 'Preiddiau Annwn' in Llyfr Taliesin, which does not boil (berwi) a coward's (llwfrgi) food.

claims.quote: Mae hi bron yn sicr fod y stori am y pair yn seiliedig ar gyfeiriad yn y chwedl Culhwch ac Olwen am "bair Diwrnach Wyddel".

statement.id: Hampir pasti kisah tentang kuali (pair) itu didasarkan pada rujukan dalam kisah Culhwch ac Olwen tentang 'bair Diwrnach Wyddel' (kuali Diwrnach Wyddel).
statement.en: It is almost certain that the story of the cauldron (pair) is based on a reference in the tale Culhwch ac Olwen to 'bair Diwrnach Wyddel' (the cauldron of Diwrnach Wyddel).

claims.quote: Cysylltir y Tri Thlws ar Ddeg â'r Hen Ogledd, ond ni cheir cyfeiriad at Ddyrnwch yn yr achau (e.e. Bonedd Gwŷr y Gogledd).

statement.id: Tri Thlws ar Ddeg dikaitkan dengan Hen Ogledd, tetapi Dyrnwch (Ddyrnwch) tidak disebut dalam silsilah (achau), misalnya Bonedd Gwŷr y Gogledd.
statement.en: The Tri Thlws ar Ddeg are associated with the Hen Ogledd, but Dyrnwch (Ddyrnwch) is not mentioned in the genealogies (achau), e.g. Bonedd Gwŷr y Gogledd.

claims.quote: ceir enw Dyrn(h)wch gan Siôn Dafydd Rhys ar ddiwedd y 16g yn ei restr o gewri Cymru

statement.id: Nama Dyrn(h)wch tercantum dalam daftar (rhestr) raksasa Cymru (gewri Cymru) karya Siôn Dafydd Rhys pada akhir abad ke-16 (16g).
statement.en: The name Dyrn(h)wch is given by Siôn Dafydd Rhys at the end of the 16th century (16g) in his list (rhestr) of the giants of Cymru (gewri Cymru).

claims.quote: Dyrnhwch Gawr yng ngwlad Ewias.
claims.locator: Kutipan dari daftar Siôn Dafydd Rhys

statement.id: Dyrnhwch Gawr di negeri (gwlad) Ewias.
statement.en: Dyrnhwch Gawr in the land (gwlad) of Ewias.

claims.quote: Am fod yr enwau Dyrnwch a Diwrnach mor debyg i'w gilydd mae'n debygol fod y cyntaf yn ffurf ddiweddar ar yr ail

statement.id: Karena nama (enwau) Dyrnwch dan Diwrnach sangat mirip, kemungkinan yang pertama adalah bentuk lebih muda (ffurf ddiweddar) dari yang kedua.
statement.en: Because the names (enwau) Dyrnwch and Diwrnach are so alike, the former is probably a later form (ffurf ddiweddar) of the latter.

claims.quote: Efallai fod cysylltiad rhwng Wrnach Gawr a Diwrnach Wyddel, er bod yr hanesion amdanynt yn wahanol, a bod Dyrnwch Gawr yn ddatblygiad diweddarach seiliedig ar y cymeriadau hynny, ond nid oes modd profi hynny'n derfynol.

statement.id: Mungkin ada hubungan (cysylltiad) antara Wrnach Gawr dan Diwrnach Wyddel, dan Dyrnwch Gawr mungkin perkembangan lebih kemudian (datblygiad diweddarach) dari tokoh-tokoh itu, tetapi tidak dapat dibuktikan secara pasti.
statement.en: There may be a link (cysylltiad) between Wrnach Gawr and Diwrnach Wyddel, and Dyrnwch Gawr may be a later development (datblygiad diweddarach) of those characters, but this cannot be proven conclusively.

claims.quote: The cauldron (pair) of Dyrnwch the Giant is said to discriminate between cowards and brave men: whereas it would not boil meat for a coward, it would boil quickly if that meat belonged to a brave man.

statement.id: Kuali (pair) Dyrnwch sang Raksasa dikatakan membedakan pengecut dari pemberani: ia tidak merebus daging untuk pengecut, tetapi cepat merebus daging milik orang pemberani.
statement.en: The cauldron (pair) of Dyrnwch the Giant is said to discriminate between cowards and brave men: it would not boil meat for a coward but would boil quickly meat belonging to a brave man.

claims.quote: Although Dyrnwch is not himself described as an Irishman, it is probable that his name goes back to Diwrnach.

statement.id: Walaupun Dyrnwch sendiri tidak disebut orang Irlandia (Irishman), kemungkinan besar namanya berasal dari Diwrnach.
statement.en: Although Dyrnwch is not himself described as an Irishman, his name probably goes back to Diwrnach.

claims.quote: The extant manuscripts of Tri Thlws ar Ddeg also present such variant spellings as Dyrnog and Tyrnog, without the Irish-sounding ending

statement.id: Naskah-naskah Tri Thlws ar Ddeg yang masih ada juga memuat ejaan varian Dyrnog dan Tyrnog, tanpa akhiran yang berbunyi Irlandia.
statement.en: The extant manuscripts of Tri Thlws ar Ddeg also give the variant spellings Dyrnog and Tyrnog, without the Irish-sounding ending.

claims.quote: Pair Dyrnwch Gawr: The Cauldron of Dyrnwch the Giant

statement.id: Pair Dyrnwch Gawr berarti Kuali Dyrnwch sang Raksasa (The Cauldron of Dyrnwch the Giant).
statement.en: Pair Dyrnwch Gawr means The Cauldron of Dyrnwch the Giant.

claims.quote: These treasures are ancient magical items of Welsh tradition that are mentioned in 15th and 16th Century manuscripts. Most of the treasures are from and in ‘The North’ of the Island of Britain.

statement.id: Pusaka-pusaka (treasures) ini adalah benda ajaib kuno tradisi Welsh yang disebut dalam naskah abad ke-15 dan ke-16; kebanyakan berasal dari 'The North' (Utara) Pulau Britania.
statement.en: These treasures are ancient magical items of Welsh tradition mentioned in 15th and 16th century manuscripts; most of them are from 'The North' of the Island of Britain.

claims.quote: The Thirteen Treasures of the Island of Britain (Welsh: Tri Thlws ar Ddeg Ynys Prydain) are a series of items in late-medieval Welsh tradition.

statement.id: Tiga Belas Pusaka Pulau Britania (Thirteen Treasures of the Island of Britain; Welsh: Tri Thlws ar Ddeg Ynys Prydain) adalah serangkaian benda dalam tradisi Welsh akhir Abad Pertengahan.
statement.en: The Thirteen Treasures of the Island of Britain (Welsh: Tri Thlws ar Ddeg Ynys Prydain) are a series of items in late-medieval Welsh tradition.

gaps.searched: Tidak ditemukan berkas Commons yang dibuat sebagai gambaran Dyrnwch Gawr atau kualinya.
Sumber hanya membahas kualinya dan asal namanya; tidak ada kutipan tentang wujud, sifat, atau kemampuan raksasa itu sendiri.

Tidak ada kisah tersendiri tentang Dyrnwch Gawr; kisah perebutan kuali dalam Culhwch ac Olwen menyangkut Diwrnach Wyddel (entri terpisah, slug dyrnwch), sehingga tidak dimasukkan sebagai kisah tokoh ini.

short_description.id: Gatipedro adalah kucing putih bertanduk satu dari cerita rakyat Galisia yang pada malam hari menuangkan air dari tanduknya sehingga anak-anak mengompol.
short_description.en: The gatipedro is a one-horned white cat of Galician folklore that pours water from its horn at night so children wet their beds.

long_description.id: Gatipedro adalah kucing putih bertanduk satu dalam cerita rakyat Galisia. Pada malam hari ia masuk ke kamar anak dan menuangkan air dari tanduknya; anak yang tidur bermimpi buang air kecil lalu mengompol. Karena berjalan dengan empat kaki dan lidahnya, ia dapat diusir dengan garam di depan pintu dan jendela.
long_description.en: The gatipedro is a one-horned white cat of Galician folklore. At night it enters children's rooms and pours water from its horn; the sleeping child dreams of peeing and wets the bed. Since it walks on four legs and its tongue, salt at the door and window drives it off.

long_description.id: Álvaro Cunqueiro mendeskripsikannya dalam Escola de menciñeiros (1960) dan memakainya dalam Os outros feirantes (1971); pada 2018 terbit cerita O gatipedro karya Jacobo Paz.
long_description.en: Álvaro Cunqueiro described it in Escola de menciñeiros (1960) and used it in Os outros feirantes (1971); in 2018 Jacobo Paz's tale O gatipedro was published.

statement.en: The gatipedro is a legendary creature of Galician folklore that makes children wet their beds, portrayed as a white cat with a single brown horn on its head.

claims.quote: O gatipedro é unha figura mitolóxica de Galicia que fai mexar ós nenos na cama. Ten forma de gato branco cun corno mouro na cabeza.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Galisia, gatipedro adalah tokoh mitologi Galisia yang membuat anak mengompol, berwujud kucing putih dengan tanduk gelap di kepalanya.
statement.en: According to the Galician article, the gatipedro is a mythological figure of Galicia that makes children wet the bed, shaped like a white cat with a dark horn on its head.

claims.quote: At night, it enters houses, goes to children's bedrooms and pours water through its horn. The sleeping child dreams he or she is peeing, and so actually wets the bed.

statement.id: Pada malam hari ia masuk ke rumah, mendatangi kamar anak, dan menuangkan air dari tanduknya; anak yang tidur bermimpi buang air kecil dan sungguh-sungguh mengompol.
statement.en: At night it enters houses, goes to children's rooms and pours water from its horn; the sleeping child dreams of peeing and really wets the bed.

claims.quote: According to popular tradition, it can be scared away by salt grains at a room's door and beside the window. It walks on all fours as well as its tongue, so when it tastes the salt, it turns around and leaves the kids alone.

statement.id: Menurut tradisi rakyat, ia dapat diusir dengan butiran garam di depan pintu kamar dan di samping jendela; karena berjalan dengan empat kaki dan lidahnya, begitu mengecap garam ia berbalik dan meninggalkan anak-anak.
statement.en: By folk tradition it can be scared off with grains of salt at the bedroom door and by the window; since it walks on four legs and its tongue, once it tastes the salt it turns back and leaves the children alone.

short_description.id: Kayış, atau Kayış Baldır dan Kayış Bacak, adalah makhluk jahat berkaki seperti tali kulit dalam kepercayaan rakyat, yang menipu orang agar menggendongnya lalu menjadikan mereka budak; ceritanya dipakai untuk menakuti anak-anak.
short_description.en: Kayış, also called Kayış Baldır or Kayış Bacak, is a malevolent being with leather-strap legs in folk belief that tricks people into carrying it and then enslaves them; its story was used to frighten children.

long_description.id: Kayış adalah makhluk jahat yang dikenal juga dengan nama Kayış Baldır atau Kayış Bacak. Artikel pertama menyebutnya gulyabani (sejenis hantu pemakan manusia) yang kakinya terbuat dari tali kulit, sedangkan kamus kedua menamainya jin bengkok. Dalam bahasa Turki Anatolia, kata kayış berarti sabuk atau kulit.
long_description.en: Kayış is a malevolent being also known as Kayış Baldır or Kayış Bacak. The first article calls it a gulyabani, a kind of ghoul, whose legs are made of leather strap, while the second source names it the crooked jinn. In Anatolian Turkish, the word kayış means belt or leather.

long_description.id: Ia tampak seperti orang tua tanpa tangan dan kaki yang tidak sanggup berjalan sendiri. Menurut kepercayaan setempat, ia duduk di tepi sungai dengan wajah memelas dan meminta orang yang lewat menggendongnya menyeberang. Begitu naik ke punggung seseorang, dari perutnya keluar dua kaki panjang atau lengan mirip ular yang melilit tubuh orang itu.
long_description.en: It looks like an old man with neither hands nor feet who cannot walk unaided. In local belief it sits by a river looking pitiful and begs passers-by to carry it across. Once on a person's back, two long legs or snake-like arms emerge from its belly and coil around the victim's body.

long_description.id: Setelah itu ia melilitkan kakinya ke pinggang korban dan tidak melepaskannya sampai perjalanan selesai, lalu menjadikan orang itu budak yang harus menuruti perintahnya. Kamus kedua menambahkan bahwa ia mengganggu perempuan yang baru melahirkan dengan duduk erat di bahu mereka. Ada pula cerita bahwa tubuhnya bisa memanjang sampai kepalanya menyentuh awan.
long_description.en: It then winds its legs around the victim's waist and will not let go until the trip is over, turning the person into a slave who must obey its orders. The second source adds that it troubles women who have recently given birth by sitting tightly on their shoulders. Other tales say its body can stretch until its head reaches the clouds.

long_description.id: Kayış muncul setelah azan magrib dan, menurut kamus kedua, berkeliaran sampai fajar. Menurut satu tafsiran, kisahnya diceritakan agar anak-anak tidak keluar rumah ketika petang gelap dan tidak berbuat nakal.
long_description.en: Kayış comes out after the evening call to prayer and, according to the second source, roams until dawn. One interpretation holds that its tale was told to keep children indoors after dark and out of mischief.

cultural_context.id: Menurut satu tafsiran, kisah Kayış dipakai untuk mencegah anak-anak keluar rumah dan berbuat nakal saat hari mulai gelap.
cultural_context.en: According to one interpretation, the tale of Kayış served to stop children from going out and misbehaving as darkness fell.

claims.quote: Kayış, Çocukları korkutmak için uydurulmuş kötücül varlıktır. Kayış Baldır veya Kayış Bacak da denilen, ayakları kayıştan gulyabanidir.

statement.id: Kayış adalah makhluk jahat (kötücül varlık) yang direka untuk menakut-nakuti anak-anak (çocukları korkutmak); disebut juga Kayış Baldır atau Kayış Bacak, ia gulyabani yang kakinya dari tali kulit (kayış).
statement.en: Kayış is a malevolent being (kötücül varlık) invented to frighten children (çocukları korkutmak); also called Kayış Baldır or Kayış Bacak, it is a gulyabani (ghoul) whose legs are made of leather strap (kayış).

claims.quote: O, kendi ayakları üzerinde durup yürüyemez. Bunun için de yoldan giden insanları aldatıp, onun boynuna biner.

statement.id: Ia tidak dapat berdiri dan berjalan di atas kakinya sendiri (yürüyemez); karena itu ia menipu orang yang lewat di jalan lalu menunggangi lehernya (boynuna biner).
statement.en: It cannot stand and walk on its own feet (yürüyemez); so it deceives people going along the road and rides on their neck (boynuna biner).

claims.quote: Sonra kayış ayaklarını onun beline dolayıp, yolu bitinceye kadar onu bırakmaz.

statement.id: Lalu ia melilitkan kaki talinya ke pinggang orang itu (beline dolayıp) dan tidak melepaskannya sampai perjalanannya selesai (yolu bitinceye kadar).
statement.en: Then it wraps its strap legs around the person's waist (beline dolayıp) and does not let go until the journey ends (yolu bitinceye kadar).

claims.quote: Elsiz ve ayaksız bir ihtiyar görünümünde olan bu varlık, ırmak kenarında oturup, gariban bir görünüş sergileyerek

statement.id: Makhluk yang tampak seperti orang tua tanpa tangan dan kaki (elsiz ve ayaksız bir ihtiyar) ini duduk di tepi sungai (ırmak kenarında) dengan penampilan memelas (gariban).
statement.en: This being, looking like an old man without hands or feet (elsiz ve ayaksız bir ihtiyar), sits by the river bank (ırmak kenarında) putting on a pitiful appearance (gariban).

claims.quote: Elleriyle de sıkı sıkıya sarılıp, "Ne dersem, onu yapacaksın" diyerek, o insanı kölesi yapar.

statement.id: Dengan tangannya ia memeluk erat (sıkı sıkıya sarılıp) dan, sambil berkata bahwa orang itu harus melakukan apa pun yang ia katakan, menjadikan orang itu budaknya (kölesi yapar).
statement.en: Clinging tightly with its hands (sıkı sıkıya sarılıp) and saying the person will do whatever it says, it makes that person its slave (kölesi yapar).

claims.quote: Söylentilere göre 'Kayış Baldır' uzadıkça uzanan, başı bulutlara değen korkunç bir canlıdır. O, akşam ezanından sonra ortaya çıkar.

statement.id: Menurut cerita, Kayış Baldır makhluk mengerikan yang terus memanjang hingga kepalanya menyentuh awan (başı bulutlara değen), dan ia muncul setelah azan magrib (akşam ezanından sonra).
statement.en: According to rumours, Kayış Baldır is a terrible creature that keeps stretching until its head touches the clouds (başı bulutlara değen), and it appears after the evening call to prayer (akşam ezanından sonra).

claims.quote: Bir yoruma göre, böyle bir hikâye anlatılarak, çocukların akşam karanlığında evden çıkmalarının ve yaramazlık yapmalarının önüne geçilmek isteniyormuş.

statement.id: Menurut satu tafsiran, cerita semacam itu diceritakan untuk mencegah anak-anak (çocukların) keluar rumah saat gelap petang dan berbuat nakal (yaramazlık).
statement.en: According to one interpretation, such a story was told to stop children (çocukların) from leaving the house in the evening darkness and misbehaving (yaramazlık).

claims.quote: KAYIŞ: Çarpık Cin. ... Hava karardıktan sonra genellikle akşam ezanının ardından ortaya çıkarak tan vaktine kadar dolaşır. Eğri bacaklı, korkunç görünüşlü bir yaratıktır.

statement.id: Kamus kedua menyebut Kayış jin bengkok (Çarpık Cin) yang muncul setelah hari gelap, biasanya sesudah azan magrib (akşam ezanının ardından), dan berkeliaran sampai fajar (tan vaktine kadar); ia makhluk berkaki bengkok (eğri bacaklı) dan berpenampilan mengerikan.
statement.en: The second source calls Kayış the crooked jinn (Çarpık Cin), which appears after dark, usually after the evening call to prayer (akşam ezanının ardından), and roams until dawn (tan vaktine kadar); it is a crooked-legged (eğri bacaklı), terrifying-looking creature.

claims.quote: Lohusalara musallat olarak, omuzlarına ayakları önden sarkacak şekilde sımsıkı oturur. Sonra da yakaladığı kadından gezinmesini ister.

statement.id: Ia mengganggu perempuan yang baru melahirkan (lohusalara musallat), duduk erat di bahu mereka dengan kaki menjuntai ke depan, lalu menyuruh perempuan yang ditangkapnya berjalan-jalan (gezinmesini ister).
statement.en: It haunts women who have recently given birth (lohusalara musallat), sitting tightly on their shoulders with its legs dangling in front, and then demands that the woman it has caught walk it around (gezinmesini ister).

claims.quote: Ancak insanın sırtına binince karnından üç arşın uzunluğunda iki bacak veyâ yılana benzer kollar çıkıp kişinin bedenine dolanır.

statement.id: Namun begitu naik ke punggung orang, dari perutnya keluar dua kaki sepanjang tiga arşın (üç arşın) atau lengan menyerupai ular (yılana benzer kollar) yang melilit tubuh orang itu.
statement.en: But once it climbs onto a person's back, two legs three arşın long (üç arşın) or snake-like arms (yılana benzer kollar) come out of its belly and wrap around the person's body.

claims.quote: Anlam: (Kay). Anadolu Türkçe'sinde Kayış sözcüğü kemer, deri demektir.

statement.id: Dalam bahasa Turki Anatolia (Anadolu Türkçe), kata Kayış berarti sabuk, kulit (kemer, deri).
statement.en: In Anatolian Turkish (Anadolu Türkçe) the word Kayış means belt, leather (kemer, deri).

short_description.id: Leontophone adalah hewan kecil dari tulisan Yunani-Romawi dan bestiari Abad Pertengahan yang begitu beracun sehingga singa yang menggigitnya mati.
short_description.en: The leontophone is a small animal of Greco-Roman writings and Medieval bestiaries so poisonous that a lion biting it dies.

long_description.id: Leontophone, dari bahasa Yunani kuno "pembunuh singa", adalah hewan kecil yang kemungkinan besar legendaris. Ia pertama dicatat penulis Yunani-Romawi lalu masuk bestiari Abad Pertengahan. Singa yang menggigitnya akan mati; dalam ritual yang tepat, dagingnya dibakar dan abunya ditaburkan pada daging umpan di persimpangan jalan untuk meracuni singa.
long_description.en: The leontophone, Ancient Greek for 'lion-killer', is a small and most probably legendary animal. Greco-Roman writers first recorded it, and it later entered Medieval bestiaries. A lion that bites one dies; in the proper ritual its flesh is burned and the ashes scattered on bait meat at a crossroads to poison lions.

long_description.id: Singa membenci leontophone dan mencabiknya dengan cakar alih-alih menggigit. Namun menurut sebagian sumber singa justru lari dan hanya menyerang bila terdesak, karena air seninya pun mematikan. Wujudnya tidak pernah digambarkan pasti: babi hutan kecil, beruang kecil, atau ular.
long_description.en: Lions hate the leontophone and rip it with their claws instead of biting. Yet some sources say the lion runs away and fights only when cornered, because even its urine is deadly. Its look is never fixed: a little boar, a little bear, or a serpent.

who.en: A small poisonous animal.

origin.id: Tulisan Yunani-Romawi dan bestiari Abad Pertengahan.

role.en: Poison to lions.

claims.quote: Leontophone (Leontophonus, Leontophonos, Leophontes, from Ancient Greek: λεοντοφόνος, meaning "lion-killer") was a small animal, most probably legendary, that was deadly to lions.

statement.id: Leontophone (Leontophonus, Leontophonos, Leophontes; dari bahasa Yunani Kuno λεοντοφόνος, "pembunuh singa") adalah hewan kecil, kemungkinan besar legendaris, yang mematikan bagi singa.
statement.en: The leontophone (Leontophonus, Leontophonos, Leophontes; from Ancient Greek λεοντοφόνος, 'lion-killer') was a small, most probably legendary animal deadly to lions.

claims.quote: The first written record is from Greco-Roman writers, but it was also known later during the Medieval period, in Medieval bestiaries.

statement.id: Catatan tertulis pertamanya berasal dari penulis Yunani-Romawi, dan kemudian ia juga dikenal dalam bestiari Abad Pertengahan.
statement.en: Its first written record comes from Greco-Roman writers, and it was later known in Medieval bestiaries.

claims.quote: Leontophones are described as fatally poisonous to lions, such that a lion will die if it merely bites a leontophone.

statement.id: Leontophone digambarkan sangat beracun bagi singa: singa akan mati hanya dengan menggigitnya.
statement.en: Leontophones are described as fatally poisonous to lions: a lion dies merely by biting one.

claims.quote: In a proper ritual, the leontophone's flesh is burned and its ashes are sprinkled on a piece of meat, which is placed at a crossroad; if a lion eats even a small amount of the tainted meat, it dies.

statement.id: Dalam ritual yang tepat, daging leontophone dibakar dan abunya ditaburkan pada sepotong daging yang diletakkan di persimpangan jalan; singa yang memakannya sedikit saja akan mati.
statement.en: In the proper ritual its flesh is burned and the ashes sprinkled on meat left at a crossroads; a lion eating even a little of it dies.

claims.quote: However, some sources state that the lion will instead flee from the small creature, only attacking and killing it when left with no option to flee (since attacking the leontophone may cause it to urinate, and the urine of the leontophone is also fatally poisonous to lions).

statement.id: Sebagian sumber menyebut singa justru lari darinya dan hanya menyerang bila terdesak, karena air seni leontophone juga mematikan bagi singa.
statement.en: Some sources say the lion flees instead and attacks only when cornered, since the leontophone's urine is also deadly to lions.

claims.quote: Likewise, due to the danger they pose to lions, lions instinctively hate leontophones. Confronted by a leontophone, they often hunt and kill them, tearing them apart with their claws rather than biting them.

statement.id: Singa membenci leontophone; bila berhadapan, singa sering memburu dan membunuhnya dengan mencabik memakai cakar, bukan menggigit.
statement.en: Lions hate leontophones; confronted with one, they often hunt and kill it, tearing it with their claws rather than biting.

claims.quote: Though no sources give a definite depiction of the leontophone's appearance, some sources speculate that the creature looks like a small boar or a small bear, while others speculate that it is serpentine

statement.id: Tidak ada sumber yang memberi gambaran pasti tentang wujudnya; sebagian menduga mirip babi hutan kecil atau beruang kecil, yang lain menduga mirip ular.
statement.en: No source gives a definite description of its appearance; some guess a small boar or small bear, others that it is serpentine.

claims.quote: Leeuwen haten leontophonen. Ze jagen erop en doden hen, eerder door ze te verscheuren met hun klauwen, dan ze te bijten.

statement.id: Artikel bahasa Belanda juga menyebut singa membenci leontophone dan memburunya, mencabiknya dengan cakar alih-alih menggigit.
statement.en: The Dutch article also says lions hate leontophones and hunt them, tearing them with their claws rather than biting.

topic.en: How lions react to the leontophone

summary.id: Singa memburu dan mencabiknya dengan cakar.
summary.en: Lions hunt it and rip it with their claws.

summary.id: Singa lari dan hanya menyerang bila terdesak.
summary.en: Lions flee and attack only when cornered.

summary.id: Mirip babi hutan kecil atau beruang kecil.
summary.en: Like a small boar or small bear.

summary.id: Mirip ular.
summary.en: Serpentine.

short_description.id: Oçi Koçi atau Ochokochi adalah iblis berbulu dalam mitologi Georgian dan kepercayaan rakyat Megrel, penghuni gunung yang menyerang manusia dan mengejar Tkashi-Mapa, Ratu Hutan.
short_description.en: Oçi Koçi or Ochokochi is a hairy demon of Georgian mythology and Megrel folk belief, a mountain dweller that attacks people and pursues Tkashi-Mapa, the Queen of the Forest.

long_description.id: Oçokoçi, juga ditulis Oçi Koçi atau Ochokochi (ოჩოკოჩი), adalah sosok dari mitologi Georgian, terutama di kalangan Mingrelian dan Colchian. Artikel pertama menempatkannya dalam mitologi Gürcü-Megrel-Laz sebagai penghuni gunung, sedangkan artikel kedua mengartikan namanya sebagai manusia-kambing.
long_description.en: Oçokoçi, also written Oçi Koçi or Ochokochi (ოჩოკოჩი), is a figure of Georgian mythology, especially among the Mingrelian and Colchian groups. The first article places it in Gürcü-Megrel-Laz mythology as a dweller of the mountains, while the second renders its name as goat-man.

long_description.id: Menurut kepercayaan rakyat Megrel, ia iblis berwujud manusia yang seluruh tubuhnya ditutupi bulu hitam pekat, bercakar panjang dan tajam. Pada musim dingin ia mendatangi desa dan memangsa anak laki-laki serta anak sapi di kandang. Ia tidak dapat berbicara, tetapi bunyi yang dikeluarkannya tak tertahankan bagi manusia.
long_description.en: In Megrel folk belief it is a demon in human form whose whole body is covered in jet-black hair, with long sharp claws. In winter it comes to the villages and preys on boys and on calves in the barn. It cannot talk, yet the noise it makes is unbearable to people.

long_description.id: Kedua artikel menggambarkan senjatanya secara berbeda. Artikel pertama menyebut ia membawa alat mirip kapak untuk membelah dua para penentangnya; artikel kedua menyebut dadanya bertonjolan berupa tulang runcing atau kapak batu dan ia membunuh orang lewat dengan memeluknya. Oçokoçi yang telah dibunuh pun dikatakan hidup lagi jika ditembak untuk kedua kalinya.
long_description.en: The two articles describe its weapon differently. The first says it carries an axe-like tool with which it splits its opponents in two; the second says its chest bears a protuberance like a pointed bone or stone axe and that it kills passers-by by embracing them. An Oçokoçi that has been killed is even said to come back to life if shot a second time.

long_description.id: Ia tergila-gila pada Tkashi-Mapa, Ratu Hutan, dan terus mengejarnya, tetapi para pemburu yang datang ke hutan sering menggagalkannya. Kajian tentang panteon pagan Megrelian menyebut Ochokochi menempati tempat penting di dalamnya dan, bersama Tkashmapa, tampil di dekat manusia dalam legenda serta memberi keberuntungan berburu.
long_description.en: He is infatuated with Tkashi-Mapa, the Queen of the Forest, and keeps chasing her, but hunters visiting the forest often foil him. A study of the Megrelian pagan pantheon says Ochokochi holds an important place in it and, together with Tkashmapa, appears near people in legends and grants luck in hunting.

who.id: Oçi Koçi adalah iblis berbulu hitam dalam mitologi Georgian.
who.en: Oçi Koçi is a black-haired demon of Georgian mythology.

origin.id: Ia dikenal dalam tradisi Megrel dan Mingrelian.
origin.en: It is known in Megrel and Mingrelian tradition.

role.id: Ia memangsa anak-anak dan ternak serta menyerang orang lewat.
role.en: It preys on children and livestock and attacks passers-by.

famous_for.id: Ia dikenal karena terus mengejar Tkashi-Mapa, Ratu Hutan.
famous_for.en: It is known for endlessly chasing Tkashi-Mapa, the Queen of the Forest.

did_you_know.id: Menurut kepercayaan Megrel, Oçokoçi yang sudah dibunuh dapat hidup kembali bila ditembak untuk kedua kalinya.
did_you_know.en: In Megrel belief, an Oçokoçi that has been killed can come back to life if it is shot a second time.

description.id: Bila ditembak untuk kedua kalinya setelah dibunuh, ia hidup lagi.
description.en: If shot a second time after being killed, it comes back to life.

note.id: Ratu Hutan yang dikejar Ochokochi; keduanya disebut wakil panteon pagan Megrelian.
note.en: The Queen of the Forest pursued by Ochokochi; both are named as members of the Megrelian pagan pantheon.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa satu makhluk bisa digambarkan dengan senjata yang berbeda dalam sumber yang berbeda?
learning_questions.en: Why might one creature be described with different weapons in different sources?

claims.quote: Oçokoçi veya Oçi Koçi (Gürcüce: ოჩოკოჩი), Gürcü-Megrel-Laz mitolojisinde dağda yaşayan bir kişilik.

statement.id: Oçokoçi atau Oçi Koçi (ოჩოკოჩი) adalah sosok yang tinggal di gunung (dağda yaşayan) dalam mitologi Gürcü-Megrel-Laz.
statement.en: Oçokoçi or Oçi Koçi (ოჩოკოჩი) is a mountain-dwelling (dağda yaşayan) figure in Gürcü-Megrel-Laz mythology.

claims.quote: Megrel halk inanışında kışın köylere dadanan ve erkek çocuklarla ahırdaki inek yavrularını yiyen vücudu kıllarla kaplı insan görünümünde bir iblistir.

statement.id: Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Megrel, ia iblis (iblis) berwujud manusia bertubuh penuh bulu yang mendatangi desa pada musim dingin dan memakan anak laki-laki serta anak sapi di kandang.
statement.en: In Megrel folk belief it is a demon (iblis) of human appearance with a hair-covered body that haunts villages in winter and eats boys and calves in the barn.

claims.quote: Oçokoçi, konuşmasını bilmez, ama çıkardığı ses insanlar için dayanılmaz bir sestir. Oçokoçi'nin bütün vücudu simsiyah tüylerle kaplıdır. Uzun ve keskin pençeleri vardır.

statement.id: Oçokoçi tidak bisa berbicara, tetapi suaranya tak tertahankan bagi manusia; seluruh tubuhnya berbulu hitam pekat (simsiyah) dan cakarnya panjang serta tajam.
statement.en: Oçokoçi cannot speak, but the sound it makes is unbearable to people; its whole body is covered in jet-black (simsiyah) hair and it has long sharp claws.

claims.quote: Yanında baltaya benzer bir alet taşır ve kendisine karşı gelen insanları bu aletle ikiye ayırır.

statement.id: Ia membawa alat mirip kapak (baltaya benzer) dan membelah dua orang yang melawannya dengan alat itu.
statement.en: It carries an axe-like tool (baltaya benzer) and splits in two the people who oppose it.

claims.quote: İnsanlar tarafından öldürülen Oçokoçi, ikinci kez ateş edildiğinde canlanır.

statement.id: Oçokoçi yang dibunuh manusia hidup kembali (canlanır) bila ditembak untuk kedua kalinya.
statement.en: An Oçokoçi killed by people comes back to life (canlanır) if it is shot a second time.

claims.quote: literally goat-man) is a figure from Georgian mythology, particularly the Colchian and Mingrelian ethnic groups.

statement.id: Ochokochi secara harfiah berarti manusia-kambing (goat-man) dan merupakan sosok mitologi Georgian, khususnya kelompok Colchian dan Mingrelian.
statement.en: Ochokochi, literally goat-man, is a figure from Georgian mythology, particularly of the Colchian and Mingrelian groups.

claims.quote: Instead of hair on his breast, he has a protuberance in the form of a pointed bone or a stone-axe. He attacks passers by, whom he kills by embracing them.

statement.id: Alih-alih bulu di dadanya, ia memiliki tonjolan berbentuk tulang runcing atau kapak batu (stone-axe); ia menyerang orang lewat dan membunuh mereka dengan memeluk (embracing).
statement.en: Instead of hair on his breast he has a protuberance shaped like a pointed bone or a stone-axe; he attacks passers-by and kills them by embracing them.

claims.quote: He is infatuated by the beauty of the Queen of the Forest, Tkashi-Mapa, after whom he chases. However, his attempts to catch her are often thwarted by the hunters who visit her forest.

statement.id: Ia tergila-gila pada kecantikan Ratu Hutan (Queen of the Forest), Tkashi-Mapa, dan mengejarnya, tetapi usahanya sering digagalkan para pemburu (hunters) yang datang ke hutannya.
statement.en: He is infatuated with the beauty of the Queen of the Forest, Tkashi-Mapa, and chases her, but his attempts are often thwarted by hunters who visit her forest.

claims.quote: the representatives of the pagan pantheon (Tkashmapa, Ochokochi) appear next to people and possess the magical qualities that make them obedient to humans. They also give people the fortune to hunt.

statement.id: Dalam legenda, wakil panteon pagan (Tkashmapa, Ochokochi) muncul di dekat manusia dan memiliki sifat magis (magical qualities) yang membuat mereka patuh kepada manusia; mereka juga memberi keberuntungan berburu (fortune to hunt).
statement.en: In legends the representatives of the pagan pantheon (Tkashmapa, Ochokochi) appear near people and have magical qualities that make them obedient to humans; they also give people the fortune to hunt.

claims.quote: And Ochococh occupies an important place in the Megrelian pagan pantheon.

statement.id: Ochococh (Ochokochi) menempati tempat penting dalam panteon pagan Megrelian (Megrelian pagan pantheon).
statement.en: Ochococh (Ochokochi) occupies an important place in the Megrelian pagan pantheon.

summary.en: First article: it carries an axe-like tool and splits its opponents in two.
