short_description.id: Icovellauna adalah dewi Kelt yang dipuja di Gaul, terutama di kuil mata air Le Sablon di Metz dan di Trier; namanya diartikan "mata air yang baik".
short_description.en: Icovellauna was a Celtic goddess worshipped in Gaul, notably at the spring temple of Le Sablon in Metz and at Trier; her name has been glossed 'good fountain'.

long_description.id: Icovellauna adalah dewi Kelt yang dipuja di Gaul. Tempat pemujaannya antara lain kuil segi delapan di Le Sablon, Metz, yang semula dibangun di atas mata air dan menghasilkan lima prasasti persembahan untuknya, serta kompleks kuil Altbachtal di Trier. Kedua tempat itu berada di lembah Sungai Moselle, kini Lorraine di Prancis dan Rheinland-Pfalz di Jerman.
long_description.en: Icovellauna was a Celtic goddess worshipped in Gaul. Her shrines included an octagonal temple at Le Sablon in Metz, first built over a spring, which yielded five inscriptions dedicated to her, and the Altbachtal temple complex at Trier. Both lie in the Moselle valley, today Lorraine in France and Rhineland-Palatinate in Germany.

long_description.id: Di kuil Metz, tangga melingkar turun ke permukaan air agar pemuja dapat meninggalkan persembahan di mata air atau mengambil airnya. Persembahan yang ditemukan meliputi patung kecil Merkurius Gaul lokal, koin, dan keramik dari abad ke-2 hingga ke-4 M. Di prasasti ia disebut "dewi yang sangat suci" dan sering dikaitkan dengan dewi Mogontia.
long_description.en: At the Metz temple a spiral staircase led down to the water so worshippers could leave offerings in the spring or take the waters. Offerings found there include a statuette of a local Gaulish Mercury, coins and ceramics from the 2nd to 4th centuries CE. Inscriptions call her a 'most holy divinity', and she is often associated with the goddess Mogontia.

long_description.id: Demarolle mengartikan namanya bonne fontaine, "mata air yang baik". Miranda Green, mengikuti Joseph Vendryes, menafsirkan akar ico- sebagai "air" dan menyebutnya dewi air yang menguasai nymphaeum di Sablon, sebuah situs mata air panas. Xavier Delamarre menganggap tafsiran itu sangat tidak mungkin dan mengusulkan ico- sebagai nama burung, mungkin pelatuk. Dalam satu uraian ia juga dipandang pancaran dewi-ibu Kelt Herta yang menguasai air suci yang memancar dari perut bumi.
long_description.en: Demarolle glosses her name as bonne fontaine, 'good fountain'. Miranda Green, following Joseph Vendryes, reads the root ico- as 'water' and calls her a water goddess presiding over the nymphaeum at Sablon, a thermal spring site. Xavier Delamarre thinks that very improbable and suggests ico- may name a bird, perhaps the woodpecker. One account also sees her as an emanation of the Celtic mother goddess Herta, ruling the sacred waters that rise from deep in the earth.

statement.en: Icovellauna was a Celtic goddess worshipped in Gaul; her shrines included an octagonal temple at Le Sablon in Metz, built over a spring and yielding five inscriptions to her, and Trier, where she was honoured in an inscription in the Altbachtal temple complex.

claims.quote: Both of these places lie in the valley of the river Moselle of eastern Gaul in what are now Lorraine in France and Rhineland-Palatinate in Germany. One such inscription was, somewhat unusually, inscribed on a copper tablet in Roman cursive letters.

statement.id: Kedua tempat itu berada di lembah Sungai Moselle di Gaul timur, kini Lorraine di Prancis dan Rheinland-Pfalz di Jerman; salah satu prasasti, agak tidak biasa, diukir pada lempeng tembaga dengan huruf kursif Romawi.
statement.en: Both places lie in the Moselle valley of eastern Gaul, now Lorraine in France and Rhineland-Palatinate in Germany; one inscription was, unusually, cut on a copper tablet in Roman cursive.

claims.quote: At the temple in Metz, a spiral staircase led down to the water level, allowing worshipers to leave offerings in the spring and/or to take the waters. A statuette of a local Gaulish Mercury was among the ex-votos deposited at the shrine, which also included coins and ceramics dating from the 2nd to 4th centuries CE.

statement.id: Di kuil Metz, tangga melingkar turun ke permukaan air sehingga pemuja dapat meninggalkan persembahan di mata air atau mengambil airnya; persembahan di sana meliputi patung kecil Merkurius Gaul lokal, koin, dan keramik dari abad ke-2 hingga ke-4 M.
statement.en: At the Metz temple a spiral staircase led down to the water so worshippers could leave offerings in the spring or take the waters; ex-votos there included a statuette of a local Gaulish Mercury, coins and ceramics of the 2nd to 4th centuries CE.

claims.quote: Demarolle glosses the name Icovellauna as bonne fontaine or "good fountain". Miranda Green follows Joseph Vendryes in interpreting the Gaulish root ico- as "water" and characterizes Icovellauna as a "water goddess" who "presided over the nymphaeum at Sablon in the Moselle Basin, a thermal spring-site".

statement.id: Demarolle mengartikan nama Icovellauna sebagai bonne fontaine, "mata air yang baik"; Miranda Green mengikuti Joseph Vendryes menafsirkan akar Gaul ico- sebagai "air" dan menyebutnya "dewi air" penguasa nymphaeum di Sablon, situs mata air panas.
statement.en: Demarolle glosses Icovellauna as bonne fontaine, 'good fountain'; Miranda Green follows Joseph Vendryes in reading Gaulish ico- as 'water', calling her a 'water goddess' of the Sablon nymphaeum, a thermal spring site.

claims.quote: Icovellauna qualifiée de "très sainte divinité" sur les ex-voto est souvent associée à la déesse Mogontia

statement.id: Icovellauna, yang disebut "dewi yang sangat suci" pada persembahan nazar, sering dikaitkan dengan dewi Mogontia.
statement.en: Icovellauna, called 'most holy divinity' on the ex-votos, is often associated with the goddess Mogontia.

claims.quote: Émanation de la déesse-mère celte Herta, elle préside les flux d'eaux turbulentes et sacrées venues des entrailles de la Terre.

statement.id: Sebagai pancaran dewi-ibu Kelt Herta, ia menguasai aliran air bergolak dan suci yang keluar dari perut bumi.
statement.en: An emanation of the Celtic mother goddess Herta, she presides over turbulent, sacred waters rising from the bowels of the Earth.

claims.quote: Xavier Delamarre, however, considers Vendryes' interpretation to be very improbable; on purely etymological grounds, he suggests that ico- might be the name of a bird, perhaps the woodpecker.

statement.id: Xavier Delamarre menganggap tafsiran Vendryes sangat tidak mungkin dan, atas dasar etimologi, mengusulkan ico- sebagai nama burung, mungkin pelatuk.
statement.en: Xavier Delamarre considers Vendryes' reading very improbable and, on etymological grounds, suggests ico- may name a bird, perhaps the woodpecker.

summary.id: "Air" (Vendryes, Green).
summary.en: 'Water' (Vendryes, Green).

summary.id: Nama burung, mungkin pelatuk (Delamarre).
summary.en: A bird name, perhaps woodpecker (Delamarre).

short_description.id: Indrajit atau Meghanada adalah putra sulung Ravana dan putra mahkota Lanka dalam Ramayana.
short_description.en: Indrajit or Meghanada is Ravana's eldest son and Lanka's crown prince in the Ramayana.

long_description.id: Indrajit atau Meghanada adalah putra sulung Ravana dan putra mahkota Lanka dalam Ramayana. Ia dapat bertempur dari langit sambil tersembunyi di balik awan.
long_description.en: Indrajit or Meghanada is Ravana's eldest son and Lanka's crown prince in the Ramayana. He can fight from the sky while hidden behind clouds.

long_description.id: Nama Indrajit berarti penakluk Indra, berkaitan dengan kemenangannya atas raja para deva. Ibunya adalah Mandodari, istri Ravana. Sulochana disebut sebagai istrinya dalam versi belakangan, bukan dalam epos asli. Mackenzie mengisahkan Indrajit membelenggu Hanuman dengan anak panah sihir berwujud ular.
long_description.en: Indrajit means conqueror of Indra, linked to his victory over the deva king. His mother is Mandodari, Ravana's wife. Sulochana is called his wife in later versions rather than the original epic. Mackenzie recounts Indrajit binding Hanuman with a magical serpent arrow.

short_description.id: Iravan adalah putra Arjuna dan putri naga Ulupi dalam Mahabharata.
short_description.en: Iravan is Arjuna and the naga princess Ulupi's son in the Mahabharata.

long_description.id: Iravan adalah putra Arjuna dan putri naga Ulupi dalam Mahabharata. Ia menjadi dewa utama dalam kultus Kuttantavar dan tokoh penting dalam tradisi Draupadi.
long_description.en: Iravan is Arjuna and the naga princess Ulupi's son in the Mahabharata. He becomes the central deity in the Kuttantavar cult and an important figure in Draupadi traditions.

long_description.id: Mahabharata mengisahkan kematiannya pada hari kedelapan perang Kurukshetra. Tradisi India Selatan menghormati pengorbanannya kepada Kali demi kemenangan Pandava. Dalam tradisi Draupadi, Krishna mengizinkan kepala Iravan yang terpenggal menyaksikan seluruh perang. Mackenzie menyebut Iravat pemberani sebagai salah satu pahlawan muda pasukan Pandava.
long_description.en: The Mahabharata recounts his death on the eighth day of the Kurukshetra war. South Indian traditions honor his sacrifice to Kali for the Pandavas' victory. In Draupadi traditions Krishna allows Iravan's severed head to witness the whole war. Mackenzie calls brave Iravat one of the Pandava army's young heroes.

cultural_context.en: Epic death and South Indian sacrificial traditions are presented as different versions.

claims.quote: Iravan  also known as Iravat and Iravant, is a minor character from the Hindu epic Mahabharata. The son of Pandava prince Arjuna (one of the main heroes of the Mahabharata) and the Naga princess Ulupi, Iravan is the central deity of the cult of Kuttantavar (Kuttandavar) which is also the name commonly given to him in that tradition—and plays a major role in the sect of Draupadi.

statement.id: Ia menjadi dewa utama dalam kultus Kuttantavar dan tokoh penting dalam tradisi Draupadi.
statement.en: He becomes the central deity in the Kuttantavar cult and an important figure in Draupadi traditions.

claims.quote: The Mahabharata portrays Iravan as dying a heroic death on the 8th day of the 18-day Kurukshetra War, the epic's main subject. However, the South Indian traditions have a supplementary practice of honouring Aravan's self-sacrifice to the goddess Kali to ensure her favour and the victory of the Pandavas in the war.

short_description.id: Iyaya adalah yōkai Jepang dalam kumpulan ilustrasi Sekien.
short_description.en: Iyaya is a Japanese yōkai in Sekien’s illustrated collection.

long_description.id: Iyaya adalah yōkai Jepang dalam kumpulan ilustrasi Sekien. Gambar memperlihatkan perempuan cantik dari belakang dengan wajah tua terpantul di air. Karya seni belakangan memakai nama Iyami untuk sosok serupa.
long_description.en: Iyaya is a Japanese yōkai in Sekien’s illustrated collection. The image shows a beautiful woman from behind with an old face reflected in water. Later artworks use the name Iyami for a similar figure.

long_description.id: Cerita Sendai belakangan mungkin ciptaan baru atau tradisi yang dihiasi. Kisah belakangan memberinya tampilan perempuan muda berpakaian indah dari belakang. Kisah belakangan itu menempatkan kejutan darinya di jalan kota pada malam hari.
long_description.en: A later Sendai narrative may be an invention or embellished tradition. A later account gives it the appearance of a well-dressed young woman from behind. That later account places its surprises on town streets at night.

claims.quote: 後ろ姿は美しい女性で、水面に老人のような顔が映った姿として描かれており、解説文には「むかし 漢の東方朔 あやしき虫をみて怪哉（かいさい）と名づけしためしあり 今この否哉もこれにならひて名付たるなるべし」と、中国の東方朔の故事にある虫「怪哉」に倣って「否哉」を名づけたことが述べられているが、否哉自体の具体的な特徴などは特に書かれていない。

short_description.id: Izanagi adalah dewa Shinto yang dalam kisah penciptaan Jepang membentuk pulau-pulau bersama Izanami.
short_description.en: Izanagi is a Shinto deity who forms islands with Izanami in a creation myth.

long_description.id: Kisah penciptaan menggambarkan Izanagi dan Izanami berdiri di Jembatan Langit lalu mengaduk laut dengan tombak. Tetesan dari tombak itu menjadi sebuah pulau. Setelah Izanami meninggal saat melahirkan dewa api, Izanagi pergi menyusulnya ke Yomi.
long_description.en: The creation story places Izanagi and Izanami on the Floating Bridge of Heaven, stirring the sea with a spear. Drops from the spear become an island. After Izanami dies giving birth to the fire god, Izanagi follows her to Yomi.

long_description.id: Izanagi melarikan diri dari Yomi dan menutup pintu keluarnya dengan batu besar. Ia lalu mandi untuk menyucikan diri. Kisah ini menyebut Amaterasu lahir ketika ia membasuh mata kiri, Tsukuyomi dari mata kanan, dan Susanoo dari hidung.
long_description.en: Izanagi flees Yomi and closes its exit with a large boulder. He then bathes to purify himself. The story says Amaterasu is born when he washes his left eye, Tsukuyomi from his right eye, and Susanoo from his nose.

claims.quote: Izanami ('she who invites') and Izanagi ('he who invites') are the primordial gods of the Shinto religion who are believed to have created the islands of Japan

statement.id: Izanagi adalah dewa purba Shinto yang dipercaya ikut menciptakan pulau-pulau Jepang.
statement.en: Izanagi is a primordial Shinto god believed to have helped create the islands of Japan.

claims.quote: According to Kojiki and Nihongi, one of the two kami (together with his consort Izanami) principally responsible for the formation of the world.

statement.id: Menurut Kojiki dan Nihongi, Izanagi bersama Izanami berperan utama dalam pembentukan dunia.
statement.en: According to the Kojiki and Nihongi, Izanagi and Izanami are central to the world’s formation.

claims.quote: According to the myth, the two kami first stood on the "floating bridge of heaven" and used a spear to stir the sea below, whereupon the brine dripping from the spear's point congealed and formed the island of Onogoro.

statement.id: Kedua kami berdiri di jembatan langit dan mengaduk laut dengan tombak; tetesannya menjadi Pulau Onogoro.
statement.en: The two kami stand on a heavenly bridge and stir the sea with a spear; its drips form Onogoro Island.

claims.quote: Izanami died as the result of giving birth to the kami of fire

statement.id: Izanami meninggal akibat melahirkan dewa api.
statement.en: Izanami died as a result of giving birth to the fire kami.

claims.quote: Izanagi, no doubt unable to live without his beloved wife, rashly followed her down into the underworld or Yomi

statement.id: Izanagi mengikuti Izanami ke Yomi.
statement.en: Izanagi followed Izanami to Yomi.

claims.quote: On finally reaching the outside world, Izanagi blocked the entrance to Yomi with an enormous stone. Fortunate to escape unharmed from such a terrible place of darkness the god had to perform a cleansing ritual in the river Woto to rid himself of the impurities of the underworld.

statement.id: Izanagi menutup pintu Yomi dengan batu besar dan menjalani penyucian diri di sungai.
statement.en: Izanagi sealed Yomi with a large stone and performed river purification.

claims.quote: It was during these rituals that various gods were born: Amaterasu, the sun goddess, when he washed his left eye, Tsuki-yomi, the god of the moon, when he washed his right eye, Susanoo (or Take-haya-Susa-no-wo), the storm god, when he washed his nose

statement.id: Saat penyucian, Amaterasu lahir dari mata kiri, Tsuki-yomi dari mata kanan, dan Susanoo dari hidung Izanagi.
statement.en: During purification, Amaterasu emerges from his left eye, Tsuki-yomi from his right, and Susanoo from his nose.

claims.quote: the "three noble children" Amaterasu, Tsukuyomi, and Susanoo were also produced at this time

statement.id: Amaterasu, Tsukuyomi, dan Susanoo dikenal sebagai tiga anak mulia.
statement.en: Amaterasu, Tsukuyomi, and Susanoo are known as the three noble children.

short_description.id: Izanami adalah dewi pencipta yang bersama Izanagi membentuk pulau-pulau Jepang dan melahirkan banyak dewa.
short_description.en: Izanami is a creator goddess who forms Japan’s islands and gives birth to many deities with Izanagi.

long_description.id: Izanami adalah pasangan Izanagi dalam kisah penciptaan. Mereka menciptakan pulau-pulau Jepang dan banyak dewa. Peran Izanami sebagai ibu para dewa membuatnya dikaitkan dengan citra dewi bumi.
long_description.en: Izanami is Izanagi’s partner in the creation story. Together they create Japan’s islands and many deities. Izanami’s role as mother of gods is associated with an earth-mother image.

long_description.id: Izanami meninggal setelah terbakar ketika melahirkan dewa api. Izanagi kemudian menyusulnya ke Yomi, tetapi melarikan diri setelah melihat wujudnya yang telah membusuk. Dalam kisah ini Izanami mengancam akan membunuh seribu orang setiap hari, sementara Izanagi menjawab akan melahirkan seribu lima ratus orang.
long_description.en: Izanami dies after being burned while giving birth to the fire god. Izanagi then follows her to Yomi but flees after seeing her decayed body. In this story Izanami threatens to kill a thousand people each day, while Izanagi replies that he will bring forth fifteen hundred.

claims.quote: As the kami responsible for the birth of various other kami representing the land and its contents, Izanami has strong connotations of an "earth mother" goddess.

statement.id: Izanami adalah kami yang melahirkan dewa-dewa alam dan dikaitkan dengan citra ibu bumi.
statement.en: Izanami is a kami who bore deities of the land and is associated with an earth-mother image.

claims.quote: Izanami ('she who invites') and Izanagi ('he who invites') are the primordial gods of the Shinto religion who are believed to have created the islands of Japan and given birth to many of the other Shinto gods or kami.

statement.id: Izanami dan Izanagi dipercaya menciptakan pulau-pulau Jepang dan melahirkan banyak dewa Shinto.
statement.en: Izanami and Izanagi are believed to have created Japan’s islands and given birth to many Shinto gods.

claims.quote: Consort of the kami Izanagi. The name Izanami has been understood in various ways

statement.id: Izanami adalah pasangan Izanagi.
statement.en: Izanami is Izanagi’s consort.

claims.quote: Burning her genitals as she gave birth to the god of fire, Izanami fell sick and then died

statement.id: Izanami terbakar saat melahirkan dewa api, lalu sakit dan meninggal.
statement.en: Izanami was burned giving birth to the fire god, then fell ill and died.

claims.quote: Izanagi, no doubt unable to live without his beloved wife, rashly followed her down into the underworld or Yomi

statement.id: Izanagi menyusul Izanami ke Yomi.
statement.en: Izanagi followed Izanami to Yomi.

claims.quote: was shocked by the putrefying appearance of his dead wife, whereupon he fled from the place

statement.id: Izanagi terkejut melihat wujud Izanami yang membusuk, lalu melarikan diri.
statement.en: Izanagi was shocked by Izanami’s decayed appearance and fled.

claims.quote: the dead Izanami threatened to kill one thousand persons each day, but Izanagi stated that he would respond by giving birth to fifteen hundred persons

statement.id: Izanami mengancam akan membunuh seribu orang setiap hari, dan Izanagi menjawab akan melahirkan seribu lima ratus orang.
statement.en: Izanami threatened to kill one thousand people daily, and Izanagi replied he would give birth to fifteen hundred.

short_description.id: Jarilo (Yarilo) adalah tokoh mitologi Slavia yang dikaitkan dengan kesuburan musim semi; sebagian sumber menyebutnya dewa vegetasi dan musim semi, sementara yang lain menganggapnya tokoh ritual.
short_description.en: Jarilo (Yarilo) is a Slavic mythological figure linked with spring fertility; some sources call him a god of vegetation and springtime, others a ritual character.

long_description.id: Jarilo, juga dieja Yarilo atau Yaryla dan disebut pula Gerovit, adalah dewa vegetasi, kesuburan, dan musim semi yang keberadaannya sebagai dewa masih diperdebatkan, dari kalangan Slavia Timur dan Selatan. Satu sumber melihatnya terutama sebagai tokoh mitos dan ritual yang terkait dengan kesuburan musim semi dan daya seksual, sekaligus personifikasi salah satu perayaan musim panas dalam kalender rakyat Rusia; tafsiran lain menganggapnya dewa kesuburan musim semi. Sumber yang sama menegaskan bahwa ia bukan dewa matahari, sedangkan sumber lain justru menyebutnya dewa matahari di wilayah berbahasa Rusia. Sumber autentik tentang Jarilo berasal dari Rusia Raya dan menggambarkan perayaan untuknya, sementara satu sumber menyebut biografi abad ke-12 tentang uskup Otto dari Bamberg sebagai satu-satunya catatan sejarah yang menyebut dewa ini.
long_description.en: Jarilo, also spelled Yarilo or Yaryla and called Gerovit, is a disputed deity of plant growth, fertility and spring in East and South Slavic belief. One source sees him mainly as a mythological and ritual character tied to spring fertility and sexual power, and as the personification of a summer festival in the Russian folk calendar; another reading makes him a deity of spring fertility. The same source insists he was not a sun god, while another calls him the sun god of the Russian-speaking area. The authentic sources on Jarilo are Great Russian and describe a festival in his honour, while one source names a 12th-century biography of bishop Otto of Bamberg as the only historical record of the god.

long_description.id: Namanya berasal dari akar kata Proto-Slavia *jarъ yang bermakna musim semi atau musim panas, kuat, garang, dan penuh daya hidup muda. Daya hidup muda itu dianggap suci dalam agama Slavia pra-Kristen, sehingga dewa yang mempersonifikasikannya disebut Jarovit, atau dengan nama akrab Jarilo.
long_description.en: His name comes from the Proto-Slavic root *jarъ, meaning spring or summer, strong, furious and full of youthful life-force. That life-force was held sacred in Slavic pre-Christian religion, so the god who personified it was called Jarovit, or affectionately Jarilo.

long_description.id: Jarilo berperan khusus dalam upacara pertanian, terutama pada musim semi, dan sosoknya mirip dengan Kostroma dan boneka jerami Maslenitsa. Di sebuah desa Kostroma, boneka bernama Jarilo dimasukkan ke peti mati, diarak keliling desa oleh seorang lelaki tua berpakaian compang-camping sambil diratapi, lalu dikubur di ladang. Hingga abad ke-19, festival rakyat bernama Jarilo dirayakan di Rusia, Belarusia, dan Serbia pada akhir musim semi atau awal musim panas.
long_description.en: Jarilo has a special place in agricultural rites, especially in spring, and his figure resembles Kostroma and the Maslenitsa straw effigy. In one Kostroma village an effigy called Jarilo was laid in a coffin, carried through the village by an old man dressed in rags amid lamentation, and then buried in the field. Until the 19th century a folk festival named Jarilo was held in Russia, Belarus and Serbia in late spring or early summer.

long_description.id: Menurut satu sumber, Jarilo adalah putra dewa guntur Perun dan istrinya, dewi Mokosch; wujud hewannya kuda dan ia dikaitkan dengan warna hijau. Dalam siklus tahunan ia datang dari jauh untuk bersatu dalam pernikahan suci dengan saudarinya Mara/Morana, sehingga kesuburan musim semi terlepas. Dalam tafsiran Kristen, ia dipadankan dengan Santo Georg dan Yohanes; di Kroasia utara dan Slovenia selatan, perayaan musim semi serupa disebut Jurjevo atau Zeleni Juraj dan dipersembahkan untuk St. George.
long_description.en: According to one source, Jarilo is the son of the thunder god Perun and his wife, the goddess Mokosch; his animal form is a horse and he is associated with the colour green. In the yearly cycle he comes from afar to unite in sacred marriage with his sister Mara/Morana, releasing spring fertility. In Christian interpretation he corresponds to Saint George (Georg) and John (Johannes); in northern Croatia and southern Slovenia a similar spring festival called Jurjevo or Zeleni Juraj is dedicated to St. George.

short_description.id: Jaunagorri, "Tuan Merah", adalah roh Basque berpakaian merah yang tinggal di istana di puncak Pic d'Anie dan mengirim badai serta hujan es kepada para pendaki.
short_description.en: Jaunagorri, the 'Red Lord', is a red-clad Basque spirit living in a palace atop the Pic d'Anie who sends storms and hail against climbers.

long_description.id: Jaunagorri, "tuan merah", adalah roh mitologi Basque yang terkait Mari; satu-satunya keterangan tentang rupanya adalah pakaiannya yang merah. Ia tinggal di istana di puncak Pic d'Anie (Auñamendi, 2.504 m), gunung suci orang Basque, yang konon memiliki taman berbuah keabadian. Para pendaki diusirnya dengan badai dan hujan es; menjelang Revolusi, penduduk Lescun konon mencegah ilmuwan Borda mendaki karena hal ini.
long_description.en: Jaunagorri, the 'red lord', is a Basque spirit linked with Mari; the only detail of his looks is his red clothing. He lives in a palace on the summit of the Pic d'Anie (Auñamendi, 2,504 m), the sacred mountain of the Basques, said to hold a garden whose fruit gives immortality. He drives climbers back with storms and hail; before the Revolution the people of Lescun reportedly stopped the scientist Borda from climbing for this reason.

statement.id: Gunung itu konon memiliki taman ajaib berbuah keabadian, tetapi orang berani yang mencoba mendakinya diusir badai dahsyat atau hujan es yang dikirim Tuan Merah.
statement.en: The mountain is said to have a wondrous garden whose fruits give immortality, but the bold who try to climb it are driven back by terrible storms or hailstorms sent by the Red Lord.

claims.quote: Peu avant la Révolution, le savant Jean-Charles de Borda fut empêché par les habitants de Lescun, pour cette raison, de tenter l'ascension du pic d'Anie. Selon d’autres sources, il s'agissait de son cousin, le géologue Jean-François de Borda.

statement.id: Sesaat sebelum Revolusi, penduduk Lescun mencegah ilmuwan Jean-Charles de Borda mendaki Pic d'Anie karena alasan ini; sumber lain menyebutnya sepupunya, ahli geologi Jean-François de Borda.
statement.en: Shortly before the Revolution, the people of Lescun stopped the scientist Jean-Charles de Borda from climbing the Pic d'Anie for this reason; other sources say it was his cousin, the geologist Jean-François de Borda.

claims.quote: Altres llegendes expliquen que tant el palau com els jardins de Jaunagorri (o Jona Gorri) els protegeixen els «Peluts» (mot gascó homònim al català), uns gegants mitològics que hom ha relacionat amb els basajaunak bascos.

statement.id: Legenda lain menyebut istana dan taman Jaunagorri dijaga Peluts, raksasa mitologis yang dikaitkan dengan basajaunak Basque.
statement.en: Other legends say Jaunagorri's palace and gardens are guarded by the Peluts, mythical giants linked with the Basque basajaunak.

claims.quote: Al Varetons es creia que certes plantes que creixen als jardins de Jona Gorri, a més d'atorgar la immortalitat, donarien a qualsevol home prou força per a derrotar els Peluts si se'n feia una poció.

statement.id: Di Barétous dipercaya tanaman dari taman Jona Gorri, selain memberi keabadian, dapat dijadikan ramuan yang memberi kekuatan untuk mengalahkan Peluts.
statement.en: In Barétous it was believed that plants from Jona Gorri's gardens, besides granting immortality, could be made into a potion giving the strength to defeat the Peluts.

claims.quote: Yanagorri Auñamendin, Mariri lotutako jeinu baten izena da.

statement.id: Artikel bahasa Basque menyebut Yanagorri nama roh di Auñamendi yang terkait dengan Mari.
statement.en: The Basque article says Yanagorri is the name of a spirit on Auñamendi linked with Mari.

short_description.id: Jean de l'Ours adalah pahlawan dongeng setengah beruang setengah manusia, anak seekor beruang dan seorang perempuan, yang dengan tongkat besinya menyelamatkan tiga putri dari dunia bawah.
short_description.en: Jean de l'Ours is the half-bear, half-human hero of a folktale, son of a bear and a woman, who with his iron cane rescues three princesses from an underworld.

long_description.id: Jean de l'Ours atau John the Bear adalah tokoh utama dongeng Tipe 301B, salah satu dongeng paling populer dalam tradisi Hispanik dan Frankofon dan sangat dikenal di Pyrenees. Ia lahir dari seorang perempuan yang diculik dan dikurung seekor beruang di guanya, tubuhnya berbulu, dan kekuatannya luar biasa; dalam satu versi Meksiko ia manusia di atas pinggang dan beruang di bawahnya.
long_description.en: Jean de l'Ours or John the Bear is the hero of tale Type 301B, one of the most popular tales in Hispanic and Francophone tradition and very well known in the Pyrenees. He is born to a woman abducted and kept in a cave by a bear, his body is hairy and his strength superhuman; in one Mexican version he is human above the waist and bear below.

long_description.id: Dengan tongkat besi yang berat ia berkelana bersama dua atau tiga kawan, mengalahkan lawan di sebuah kastel, turun ke dunia bawah, dan menyelamatkan tiga putri, lalu dikhianati kawan-kawannya, lolos, dan menikahi putri tercantik. Sebagai Juan Oso, mitos ini tersebar di dunia berbahasa Spanyol dengan lebih dari 300 versi, termasuk dalam bahasa Quechua.
long_description.en: With a heavy iron cane he travels with two or three companions, defeats a foe at a castle, descends to an underworld and rescues three princesses, is betrayed by his companions, escapes and marries the fairest princess. As Juan Oso the myth has spread across the Spanish-speaking world in over 300 versions, including in Quechua.

who.en: A half-bear hero.

role.en: Rescues three princesses.

famous_for.id: Tongkat besinya.
famous_for.en: His iron cane.

description.id: Ia memiliki kekuatan luar biasa untuk melewati berbagai ujian.
description.en: He has superhuman strength to overcome trials.

description.id: Pahlawan manusia di atas pinggang dan beruang di bawahnya.
description.en: The hero is human above the waist and bear below.

description.id: Versi Rusia dengan pahlawan setengah beruang.
description.en: The Russian version with a half-bear hero.

title.en: The three princesses in the underworld

role.en: Hero

summary.id: Jean mengejar lawan ke lubang, menyelamatkan tiga putri, ditinggal kawan-kawannya, lalu lolos dan menikahi putri tercantik.
summary.en: Jean chases a foe down a hole, rescues three princesses, is abandoned by his companions, then escapes and marries the fairest princess.

claims.quote: or John the Bear, John of the Bear, John-of-the-Bear, John Bear, is the leading character in the French folktale Jean de l'Ours classed as Type 301B in the Aarne–Thompson system; it can also denote any tale of this type.

statement.id: Jean de l'Ours atau John the Bear adalah tokoh utama dongeng Prancis Jean de l'Ours yang digolongkan Tipe 301B dalam sistem Aarne–Thompson; nama itu juga dipakai untuk semua dongeng bertipe ini.
statement.en: Jean de l'Ours or John the Bear is the hero of the French folktale Jean de l'Ours, classed as Type 301B in the Aarne–Thompson system; the name also denotes any tale of this type.

claims.quote: Some typical elements are that the hero is born half-bear, half-human; he obtains a weapon, usually a heavy iron cane, and on his journey; he bands up with two or three companions.

statement.id: Unsur khasnya: sang pahlawan lahir setengah beruang setengah manusia, mendapat senjata, biasanya tongkat besi yang berat, dan dalam perjalanannya bergabung dengan dua atau tiga kawan.
statement.en: Typically the hero is born half-bear, half-human, gets a weapon, usually a heavy iron cane, and on his journey joins two or three companions.

claims.quote: At a castle the hero defeats an adversary, pursues him to a hole, discovers an underworld, and rescues three princesses. The companions abandon him in the hole, taking the princesses for themselves.

statement.id: Di sebuah kastel ia mengalahkan seorang lawan, mengejarnya ke sebuah lubang, menemukan dunia bawah, dan menyelamatkan tiga putri, tetapi kawan-kawannya meninggalkannya di lubang dan merebut para putri.
statement.en: At a castle he defeats a foe, chases him down a hole, finds an underworld and rescues three princesses, but his companions abandon him in the hole and take the princesses.

claims.quote: The hero escapes, finds the companions and gets rid of them. He marries the most beautiful princess of the three, but not before going through certain ordeal(s) by the king.

statement.id: Ia lolos, menemukan dan menyingkirkan kawan-kawannya, lalu menikahi putri tercantik setelah menjalani ujian dari raja.
statement.en: He escapes, finds and disposes of the companions, and marries the fairest princess after ordeals set by the king.

claims.quote: The character is said to be one of "the most popular tale-types in Hispanic and Francophone tradition". Numerous variants exist in France, often retaining the name Jean de l'Ours or something similar for the hero.

statement.id: Tokoh ini disebut salah satu "tipe dongeng paling populer dalam tradisi Hispanik dan Frankofon", dengan banyak varian di Prancis yang sering tetap menamai pahlawannya Jean de l'Ours.
statement.en: The tale is called one of 'the most popular tale-types in Hispanic and Francophone tradition', with many French variants often keeping the hero's name Jean de l'Ours.

claims.quote: Several French versions explicitly comment on Jean de l'ours being covered with body hair on his entire body.

statement.id: Beberapa versi Prancis menyebut tubuh Jean de l'Ours tertutup bulu seluruhnya.
statement.en: Several French versions say Jean de l'Ours was covered in hair all over his body.

claims.quote: The hero is human from the waist up and bear from the waist down in one Mexican version (Juan el Oso) as well as the Russian tale

statement.id: Dalam satu versi Meksiko (Juan el Oso) dan dongeng Rusia "Ivanko Medvedko", pahlawan itu manusia dari pinggang ke atas dan beruang dari pinggang ke bawah.
statement.en: In one Mexican version (Juan el Oso) and the Russian tale 'Ivanko Medvedko', the hero is human above the waist and bear below.

claims.quote: Juan Oso („Johann Bär“), der Sohn des Bären (Hijo del Oso, Cusco-Quechua Ukukuq wawan oder Ukuku uña, Chanka-Quechua Ukumaripa churin oder auch Maqta peludo), ist der Mythos von einem halb bärenhaften, halb menschlichen Helden

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, Juan Oso, "Putra Beruang" (Hijo del Oso, dalam bahasa Quechua Cusco Ukukuq wawan atau Ukuku uña), adalah mitos tentang pahlawan setengah beruang setengah manusia.
statement.en: According to the German article, Juan Oso, 'Son of the Bear' (Hijo del Oso, Cusco Quechua Ukukuq wawan or Ukuku uña), is the myth of a half-bear, half-human hero.

claims.quote: Der Mythos ist insbesondere im spanischsprachigen Raum (Spanien, Lateinamerika, New Mexico, Kalifornien), aber auch in Teilen Asiens verbreitet. Es gibt mehr als 300 Versionen in etwa 20 Sprachen, neben dem Spanischen auch in indigenen Sprachen Amerikas.

statement.id: Mitos ini tersebar terutama di dunia berbahasa Spanyol (Spanyol, Amerika Latin, New Mexico, California) dan sebagian Asia, dengan lebih dari 300 versi dalam sekitar 20 bahasa, termasuk bahasa pribumi Amerika.
statement.en: The myth is widespread especially in the Spanish-speaking world (Spain, Latin America, New Mexico, California) and parts of Asia, with over 300 versions in about 20 languages, including indigenous American ones.

claims.quote: In einer sehr verbreiteten Version verschleppt ein Bär eine junge Frau (oft eine Prinzessin), sperrt sie in seine Höhle ein, wo er sie auch versorgt, und zeugt mit ihr einen Sohn, der halb Bär und halb Mensch ist.

statement.id: Dalam versi yang sangat umum, seekor beruang menculik seorang perempuan muda, sering seorang putri, mengurungnya di guanya, dan memperoleh anak setengah beruang setengah manusia darinya.
statement.en: In a very common version a bear abducts a young woman, often a princess, keeps her in his cave and fathers on her a son who is half bear and half human.

claims.quote: Jean de l’Ours est un être hybride, mi-humain, mi-animal, né d'une femme et d'un ours, et doté d'une force surhumaine qui lui permet de surmonter diverses épreuves.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, Jean de l'Ours adalah makhluk campuran setengah manusia setengah binatang, lahir dari seorang perempuan dan seekor beruang, dengan kekuatan luar biasa untuk melewati berbagai ujian.
statement.en: According to the French article, Jean de l'Ours is a hybrid, half-human and half-animal, born of a woman and a bear, with superhuman strength to overcome many trials.

claims.quote: Il est particulièrement populaire dans les régions pyrénéennes.

statement.id: Dongeng ini sangat populer di daerah Pyrenees.
statement.en: The tale is especially popular in the Pyrenean regions.

short_description.id: Kagutsuchi adalah kami api yang kelahirannya menyebabkan kematian Izanami.
short_description.en: Kagutsuchi is a fire kami whose birth caused Izanami’s death.

long_description.id: Kagutsuchi adalah kami api, putra pasangan Izanagi dan Izanami. Dalam sebuah kisah, Izanami meninggal setelah melahirkan dewa api itu dan masuk ke Yomi. Izanagi yang berduka lalu memenggal Kagutsuchi dengan pedang. Darah yang menetes dari bilah pedang melahirkan delapan dewa, sedangkan delapan lainnya muncul dari tubuh Kagutsuchi; mereka berkaitan dengan batu, pedang, petir, api, air terjun, dan lembah.
long_description.en: Kagutsuchi is a fire kami, a child of Izanagi and Izanami. In one account, Izanami dies after giving birth to the fire god and enters Yomi. The grieving Izanagi then beheads Kagutsuchi with a sword. Blood dripping from the blade gives rise to eight deities, and eight more emerge from Kagutsuchi’s body; they are associated with rocks, swords, thunder, flames, waterfalls, and valleys.

long_description.id: Kagutsuchi juga hadir dalam pemujaan yang berkaitan dengan pencegahan kebakaran. Di Akiha Gongendō ia dipuja sebagai Hi no Kagutsuchi no Kami; warga setempat berkumpul dua kali setahun untuk memohon perlindungan dari api dan bencana lain. Keterangan tempat itu mencatat nama Akiha Daigongen dan sebutan lokal Akiha-san, yang memperlihatkan percampuran dua tradisi keagamaan. Kuil Akiba di Ogimachi resmi didedikasikan kepadanya pada zaman Taishō. Di wilayah Daisen, sebagian orang dahulu juga mengenali dewa agung gunung itu sebagai Kagutsuchi.
long_description.en: Kagutsuchi also figures in worship concerned with preventing fires. At Akiha Gongendō he is enshrined as Hi no Kagutsuchi no Kami; residents gather twice yearly to pray for protection from fire and other disasters. The site records the name Akiha Daigongen and local name Akiha-san, reflecting a blending of two religious traditions. Akiba Shrine in Ogimachi was formally dedicated to him in the Taishō era. Around Mt. Daisen, some also identified the mountain’s great deity as Kagutsuchi.

sources.title: The Myths of Japan: The Beheading of the God of Fire

claims.quote: After burying Izanami, Izanagi turns toward Kagutsuchi, the fire god who caused the tragedy.

statement.id: Kagutsuchi adalah dewa api yang terkait dengan kematian Izanami.
statement.en: Kagutsuchi is the fire god linked to Izanami’s death.

claims.quote: When the goddess died after giving birth to the god of fire, she entered the world of darkness called Yomi-no-kuni.

statement.id: Izanami meninggal seusai melahirkan dewa api lalu masuk ke Yomi.
statement.en: Izanami died after giving birth to the fire god and entered Yomi.

claims.quote: Filled with wrath, he pulls his sword and beheads Kagutsuchi with a single swing.

statement.id: Izanagi memenggal Kagutsuchi dengan pedangnya.
statement.en: Izanagi beheaded Kagutsuchi with his sword.

claims.quote: Blood drips from the blade onto the ground, producing eight new deities, while eight others emerge from Kagutsuchi’s maimed body.

statement.id: Darah pedang dan tubuh Kagutsuchi masing-masing melahirkan delapan dewa.
statement.en: Blood from the sword and Kagutsuchi’s body each gave rise to eight deities.

claims.quote: These are the gods of rocks, swords, thunder, flames, waterfalls, and valleys

statement.id: Dewa-dewa yang lahir berkaitan dengan batu, pedang, petir, api, air terjun, dan lembah.
statement.en: The emergent deities are linked to rocks, swords, thunder, flames, waterfalls, and valleys.

claims.quote: The enshrined kami (Shinto deity) is Hi no Kagutsuchi no Kami, who is associated with fire prevention and appears in one of the earliest written records of Japan.

statement.id: Akiha Gongendō memuja Hi no Kagutsuchi no Kami, terkait pencegahan kebakaran.
statement.en: Akiha Gongendō enshrines Hi no Kagutsuchi no Kami, associated with fire prevention.

claims.quote: Local residents gather there twice a year to pray for protection from fire and other calamities.

statement.id: Warga berkumpul dua kali setahun untuk memohon perlindungan dari api dan bencana.
statement.en: Residents gather twice a year to pray for protection from fire and calamities.

claims.quote: Hi no Kagutsuchi no Kami is also known by the Buddhist name “Akiha Daigongen,” and he is known locally as “Akiha-san.”

statement.id: Nama Buddhisnya Akiha Daigongen dan sebutan setempat Akiha-san.
statement.en: He is called Akiha Daigongen in Buddhism and Akiha-san locally.

claims.quote: This sanctuary remained a modest place of worship until the Taisho era (1912–1926), when the shrine building was reconstructed and officially dedicated to Kagutsuchi, the Shinto god of fire.

statement.id: Kuil Akiba di Ogimachi didedikasikan kepada Kagutsuchi pada zaman Taishō.
statement.en: Akiba Shrine in Ogimachi was dedicated to Kagutsuchi in the Taishō era.

claims.quote: The God was believed by many to be the Kagutsuchi-no-mikoto, or God of Fire.

statement.id: Sebagian orang mengenali dewa Gunung Daisen sebagai Kagutsuchi.
statement.en: Some identified Mt. Daisen’s great deity as Kagutsuchi.

short_description.id: Kamimusubi adalah kami penciptaan dalam mitologi Jepang.
short_description.en: Kamimusubi is a creation kami in Japanese mythology.

long_description.id: Kamimusubi adalah kami penciptaan dalam mitologi Jepang. Ia termasuk tiga kami pertama yang muncul, bersama Ame-no-Minakanushi dan Takamimusubi. Nama itu memadukan kata kami dan musubi yang dikaitkan dengan daya penciptaan.
long_description.en: Kamimusubi is a creation kami in Japanese mythology. It belongs to the first three kami alongside Ame-no-Minakanushi and Takamimusubi. The name joins kami and musubi, a creative force.

long_description.id: Pada kisah penciptaan, Kamimusubi berada di Takamagahara bersama dua kami awal lainnya. Kojiki menggambarkannya sebagai dewa leluhur yang menolong dewa-dewa Izumo. Kamimusubi dikaitkan dengan asal lima jenis biji-bijian dari tubuh Ōgetsu-hime. Menurut Kojiki, Kamimusubi menghidupkan kembali Ōnamuchi atas permintaan ibunya.
long_description.en: In the creation account, Kamimusubi is in Takamagahara with the other early kami. The Kojiki portrays Kamimusubi as an ancestral god helping the gods of Izumo. Kamimusubi is linked to the emergence of five grains from Ōgetsu-hime’s body. According to the Kojiki, Kamimusubi restored Ōnamuchi to life at his mother’s request.

claims.quote: Kamimusubi (神産巣日, lit. "Sacred Generative Force"), also known as Kamimusuhi among other variants, is a kami and god of creation in Japanese mythology.

statement.id: Kamimusubi adalah kami penciptaan dalam mitologi Jepang.
statement.en: Kamimusubi is a creation kami in Japanese mythology.

claims.quote: They are a hitorigami, and the third of the first three kami to come into existence (Kotoamatsukami), alongside Ame-no-Minakanushi and Takamimusubi, forming a trio at the beginning of all creation.

statement.id: Ia termasuk tiga kami pertama yang muncul, bersama Ame-no-Minakanushi dan Takamimusubi.
statement.en: It belongs to the first three kami alongside Ame-no-Minakanushi and Takamimusubi.

claims.quote: The name is composed of kami, denoting deity, and musubi, meaning "effecting force of creation".

statement.id: Nama itu memadukan kata kami dan musubi yang dikaitkan dengan daya penciptaan.
statement.en: The name joins kami and musubi, a creative force.

claims.quote: At the time of the creation of heaven and earth, Kamimusubi was in Takamagahara next to Ame-no-Minakanushi and Takamimusubi.

statement.id: Pada kisah penciptaan, Kamimusubi berada di Takamagahara bersama dua kami awal lainnya.
statement.en: In the creation account, Kamimusubi is in Takamagahara with the other early kami.

claims.quote: In Kojiki, Kamimusubi is an ancestral god who sits in Takamagahara and assists the gods of Izumo, and is called "Mi-Oya" (honorfic name for ancestor) by other gods.

statement.id: Kojiki menggambarkannya sebagai dewa leluhur yang menolong dewa-dewa Izumo.
statement.en: The Kojiki portrays Kamimusubi as an ancestral god helping the gods of Izumo.

claims.quote: Kamimusubi became the ancestral god of the five grains (progenitors) after Kamimusubi transformed the grains produced from the body of Ōgetsu-hime, the goddess of food, who was killed by Susanoo, the god of storms.

statement.id: Kamimusubi dikaitkan dengan asal lima jenis biji-bijian dari tubuh Ōgetsu-hime.
statement.en: Kamimusubi is linked to the emergence of five grains from Ōgetsu-hime’s body.

claims.quote: she granted the wish of Ōnamuchi's mother by restoring him to life

statement.id: Menurut Kojiki, Kamimusubi menghidupkan kembali Ōnamuchi atas permintaan ibunya.
statement.en: According to the Kojiki, Kamimusubi restored Ōnamuchi to life at his mother’s request.

short_description.id: Katawaguruma adalah yōkai Jepang dari cerita gaib lama.
short_description.en: Katawaguruma is a Japanese yōkai from old supernatural tales.

long_description.id: Katawaguruma adalah yōkai Jepang dari cerita gaib lama. Wujudnya kereta beroda tunggal yang terbakar dan membawa perempuan atau laki-laki menakutkan. Satu kisah menyebut ia mengutuk orang yang melihatnya. Cerita Shiga menggambarkan penculikan anak dari seorang perempuan yang mengintipnya.
long_description.en: Katawaguruma is a Japanese yōkai from old supernatural tales. It takes the form of a flaming single-wheeled cart bearing a woman or frightening man. An account says it curses people who see it. A Shiga tale describes the abduction of a curious woman’s child.

long_description.id: Cerita tersebut berakhir dengan anak dikembalikan setelah ibunya menyesal. Ia konon tidak pernah muncul lagi di desa itu. Kartu zaman Edo menggambar wujud laki-laki berdasarkan Shokoku Hyaku Monogatari. Kumpulan ilustrasi Sekien justru menggambar wujud perempuan.
long_description.en: That tale ends with the child being returned after the mother’s remorse. It is said never to appear in that village again. An Edo-period card depicts a male form based on Shokoku Hyaku Monogatari. Sekien’s illustrated collection instead depicts a female form.

claims.quote: 片輪車（かたわぐるま）は、江戸時代の怪談などの古書に見られる日本の妖怪。炎に包まれた片輪のみの牛車が美女または恐ろしい男を乗せて走り、姿を見たものを祟るとされる。

statement.id: Katawaguruma adalah yōkai Jepang dari cerita gaib lama.
statement.en: Katawaguruma is a Japanese yōkai from old supernatural tales.

claims.quote: 片輪車（かたわぐるま）は、江戸時代の怪談などの古書に見られる日本の妖怪。炎に包まれた片輪のみの牛車が美女または恐ろしい男を乗せて走り、姿を見たものを祟るとされる。

statement.id: Wujudnya kereta beroda tunggal yang terbakar dan membawa perempuan atau laki-laki menakutkan.
statement.en: It takes the form of a flaming single-wheeled cart bearing a woman or frightening man.

claims.quote: These demons bestow powerful curses on any who see them.

statement.id: Satu kisah menyebut ia mengutuk orang yang melihatnya.
statement.en: An account says it curses people who see it.

claims.quote: In a 17th century record, when a katawaguruma attacked a village in what is now Shiga, she abducted the child of a woman who dared to peek at her through a crack in her door, saying “Instead of watching me you should have been watching your child!”

statement.id: Cerita Shiga menggambarkan penculikan anak dari seorang perempuan yang mengintipnya.
statement.en: A Shiga tale describes the abduction of a curious woman’s child.

claims.quote: The next night, the katawaguruma came again and saw that the woman was truly regretful. She returned the child unharmed.

statement.id: Cerita tersebut berakhir dengan anak dikembalikan setelah ibunya menyesal.
statement.en: That tale ends with the child being returned after the mother’s remorse.

claims.quote: The katawaguruma was never seen in that village again.

statement.id: Ia konon tidak pernah muncul lagi di desa itu.
statement.en: It is said never to appear in that village again.

short_description.id: Kayanohime adalah dewi rumput dan ladang dalam mitologi Jepang.
short_description.en: Kayanohime is a Japanese goddess of grasses and fields.

long_description.id: Kayanohime adalah dewi rumput dan ladang dalam mitologi Jepang. Ia dianggap pelindung ladang. Ia juga dikaitkan dengan asal-usul tumbuhan.
long_description.en: Kayanohime is a Japanese goddess of grasses and fields. She is regarded as a protector of fields. She is also associated with the ancestry of herbs.

long_description.id: Mitologi menyebut Izanami dan Izanagi sebagai orang tuanya. Ōyamatsumi disebut sebagai suami sekaligus saudaranya. Satu kebiasaan melibatkan doa kepadanya sebelum memotong bahan bangunan. Terjemahan Kojiki memberi Kayanohime nama lain Notsuchi.
long_description.en: The mythology names Izanami and Izanagi as her parents. Ōyamatsumi is described as her spouse and brother. One custom involved praying to her before cutting building materials. The Kojiki translation gives Kayanohime the alternate name Notsuchi.

sources.title: Studies on the Kojiki: Chapter 6, Giving Birth to Deities

short_description.id: Kazenbō adalah yōkai yang digambar dalam kumpulan Sekien.
short_description.en: Kazenbō is a yōkai illustrated in Sekien’s collection.

long_description.id: Kazenbō adalah yōkai yang digambar dalam kumpulan Sekien. Ia tampak sebagai biksu pengemis berselubung api dan asap di Toribeyama. Satu kisah menjelaskannya sebagai biksu yang gagal mencapai Tanah Suci setelah pengorbanan api.
long_description.en: Kazenbō is a yōkai illustrated in Sekien’s collection. It appears as a beggar monk enveloped in fire and smoke at Toribeyama. One account explains it as a monk who failed to attain the Pure Land after fiery sacrifice.

long_description.id: Teori lain menganggapnya ciptaan Sekien dari nama tempat di Edo. Kisah belakangan menyebut penampakan itu tidak berbahaya tetapi mengganggu. Kisah itu menyebutnya menderita dalam api yang tidak menghabiskannya lalu menghilang.
long_description.en: Another theory treats it as Sekien’s invention from an Edo place name. A later account calls the apparition harmless but disturbing. That account has it suffer in unconsuming flames before disappearing.

short_description.id: Kesaran Pasaran adalah makhluk misterius cerita rakyat Jepang yang digambarkan sejak zaman Edo.
short_description.en: Kesaran Pasaran is a mysterious being of Japanese folklore described since the Edo period.

long_description.id: Kesaran Pasaran adalah makhluk misterius cerita rakyat Jepang yang digambarkan sejak zaman Edo. Ia menyerupai bola putih halus seperti ekor kelinci. Kisah berbeda mengenai apakah ia hewan, tumbuhan, atau yōkai kecil.
long_description.en: Kesaran Pasaran is a mysterious being of Japanese folklore described since the Edo period. It resembles a white fluffy ball like a rabbit’s tail. Accounts disagree over whether it is an animal, plant or small yōkai.

long_description.id: Memeliharanya dalam kotak paulownia berventilasi dengan bedak wajah disebut membawa keberuntungan atau perkembangbiakan. Kajian pembentukan kata menyimpulkan bahwa asal nama dari onomatope tidak mungkin besar. Kajian mengutip tradisi yang memberi rentang ukuran dari kacang azuki hingga telur ayam.
long_description.en: Keeping it in a ventilated paulownia box with face powder is said to bring luck or multiplication. A word-formation study concludes that an onomatopoeic origin for the name is unlikely. The study cites traditions giving a size range from an adzuki bean to a chicken egg.

sources.title: The Onomatopoeic Origin of Kesaran Pasaran
sources.author: Megumi Kawasaki

short_description.id: Kosenjōbi adalah cahaya gaib Jepang yang dicatat dalam buku zaman Edo.
short_description.en: Kosenjōbi is a Japanese ghost light recorded in Edo books.

long_description.id: Kosenjōbi adalah cahaya gaib Jepang yang dicatat dalam buku zaman Edo. Cahaya itu dikaitkan dengan roh tentara dan hewan yang tewas dalam pertempuran. Sekien menyebut cahaya itu timbul dari darah yang tertumpah di tanah.
long_description.en: Kosenjōbi is a Japanese ghost light recorded in Edo books. The lights are attributed to spirits of soldiers and animals killed in battle. Sekien says the lights arise from blood spilled on the ground.

long_description.id: Mereka konon terbang berkeliling tanpa langsung menyakiti orang. Uraian belakangan menggambarkan tak terhitung nyala api yang melayang tanpa arah. Uraian itu juga memberi mereka bentuk tentara dan hewan yang terluka.
long_description.en: They reportedly fly about without directly harming people. A later description presents countless aimlessly floating flames. That description also gives them forms of wounded warriors and animals.

short_description.id: Koto-furunushi adalah makhluk alat musik dalam kisah gaib Jepang.
short_description.en: Koto-furunushi is a musical-instrument being in Japanese supernatural lore.

long_description.id: Koto-furunushi adalah makhluk alat musik dalam kisah gaib Jepang. Ia digambarkan sebagai yōkai yang tidak membahayakan manusia. Wujudnya menyerupai koto dengan wajah iblis.
long_description.en: Koto-furunushi is a musical-instrument being in Japanese supernatural lore. It is described as a yōkai harmless to people. Its form resembles a koto with a demonic face.

long_description.id: Senarnya yang tidak teratur disamakan dengan rambut kusut. Satu kisah belakangan memberinya ingatan tentang musik yang pernah dimainkan dengannya. Dalam kisah itu, ia memainkan musik ketika tidak ada orang di dekatnya.
long_description.en: The loose strings are compared with an untidy mane. One later account gives it a memory of music previously played on it. In that account it plays music when nobody is nearby.

claims.quote: The koto-furunushi (琴古主; English: "old master koto") is a fictitious being from Japanese folklore.

statement.id: Koto-furunushi adalah makhluk alat musik dalam kisah gaib Jepang.
statement.en: Koto-furunushi is a musical-instrument being in Japanese supernatural lore.

claims.quote: It is a Yōkai and is said to be harmless to humans.

statement.id: Ia digambarkan sebagai yōkai yang tidak membahayakan manusia.
statement.en: It is described as a yōkai harmless to people.

statement.en: Its form resembles a koto with a demonic face.

statement.en: One later account gives it a memory of music previously played on it.

short_description.id: Kubera adalah dewa kekayaan dan raja yaksha dalam Hindu.
short_description.en: Kubera is the Hindu god of wealth and king of yakshas.

long_description.id: Kubera adalah dewa kekayaan dan raja yaksha dalam Hindu. Ia menjadi penjaga arah utara dan pelindung dunia.
long_description.en: Kubera is the Hindu god of wealth and king of yakshas. He is regent of the north and protector of the world.

long_description.id: Penggambaran umum memperlihatkan tubuh gemuk, perhiasan, wadah uang, dan gada. Dalam kisah kitab, Ravana menggulingkannya dari Lanka sebelum ia menetap di Alaka di Himalaya. Nama Buddhisnya Vaisravana; di Indonesia ia juga dikenal sebagai Daneswara. Mackenzie menempatkan kediaman Kuvera di Himalaya dan mengaitkannya dengan yaksha penjaga harta.
long_description.en: Common depictions show a plump body, jewels, money pot, and club. In scriptural narratives Ravana overthrows him from Lanka before he settles in Alaka in the Himalayas. His Buddhist name is Vaisravana; in Indonesia he is also known as Daneswara. Mackenzie places Kuvera's dwelling in the Himalayas and associates him with treasure guarding yakshas.

sources.title: The Project Gutenberg eBook of Indian Myth and Legend, by Donald A. Mackenzie.

statement.en: Kubera is the Hindu god of wealth and king of yakshas.

The scriptures describe that Kubera once ruled Lanka, but was overthrown by his half-brother Ravana, later settling in the city of Alaka in the Himalayas.

statement.en: In scriptural narratives Ravana overthrows him from Lanka before he settles in Alaka in the Himalayas.

statement.en: His Buddhist name is Vaisravana; in Indonesia he is also known as Daneswara.

short_description.id: Kuda Sembrani adalah kuda mitologis yang dalam sebuah cerita dikisahkan dapat terbang.
short_description.en: Kuda Sembrani is a mythological horse said to fly in one tale.

long_description.id: Sebuah cerita setempat menyebut Kuda Sembrani sebagai tunggangan bidadari yang turun ke Tlogo Guyangan. Jejak kakinya dipercaya membentuk cekungan batu di dekat telaga. Dalam cerita Kyai Bodho, kuda itu dipelihara oleh Kyai Bodho. Kuda tersebut kemudian lolos dari kandang dengan terbang.
long_description.en: A local story describes Kuda Sembrani as a celestial being’s mount that descends to Tlogo Guyangan. Its hoofbeats are believed to have left hollows in rock near the lake. In the Kyai Bodho tale, he cares for the horse. The horse later escapes its stable by flying.

description.id: Kuda Sembrani dikisahkan dapat terbang.
description.en: Kuda Sembrani is said to be able to fly.

claims.quote: Cerita itu dihubungkan dengan makhluk mitologi berupa kuda yang menjadi tunggangan bidadari. Kuda tersebut bernama Kuda Sembrani

statement.id: Kuda Sembrani adalah kuda mitologis tunggangan bidadari dalam cerita setempat.
statement.en: Kuda Sembrani is a mythological horse ridden by celestial beings in local stories.

claims.quote: Kuda tersebut bernama Kuda Sembrani yang konon sering turun ke Tlogo Guyangan untuk berendam dan mandi.

statement.id: Kuda Sembrani dikisahkan turun ke Tlogo Guyangan untuk mandi.
statement.en: Kuda Sembrani is said to descend to Tlogo Guyangan to bathe.

statement.en: In the story, its hoofbeats left marks that named the Tapak Jaran Sembrani site.

claims.quote: Saran yang diberikan oleh Kyai Bodho untuk mengusahakan terjaminnya ketenteraman seluruh negeri dan kesejahteraan hidup seluruh rakyat adalah dengan memelihara kuda sembrani.

statement.id: Kyai Bodho menyarankan pemeliharaan Kuda Sembrani demi kesejahteraan negeri.
statement.en: Kyai Bodho recommends keeping Kuda Sembrani for the realm’s welfare.

claims.quote: Sesampai di Mataram, Kuda Sembrani itu lalu diserahkan kepada Kyai Bodho. Kyai Bodholah yang diserahi tugas sebagai "pekathik" khusus mengurus dan memelihara Kuda Sembrani

statement.id: Kyai Bodho ditugaskan memelihara Kuda Sembrani.
statement.en: Kyai Bodho is tasked with caring for Kuda Sembrani.

short_description.id: Kurent adalah tokoh cerita rakyat Slovenia, pemain biola ajaib dan dewa kegembiraan, yang kini hidup sebagai topeng karnaval pengusir musim dingin di Ptujsko polje.
short_description.en: Kurent is a figure of Slovenian folklore, a miraculous fiddler and god of joy, who lives on as the winter-chasing carnival masks of Ptujsko polje.

long_description.id: Kurent atau Korant adalah tokoh cerita rakyat Slovenia, pemain biola ajaib dalam mitologi Slavia dan dewa kegembiraan, mungkin juga seksualitas. Kisahnya pertama diterbitkan Janez Trdina pada 1858 dari cerita yang dikumpulkan di Mengeš, Carniola, tetapi keasliannya kadang diragukan. Ia muncul pula dalam kisah Kurent dan manusia serta Kurent yang menjadi lembu.
long_description.en: Kurent or Korant is a figure of Slovenian folklore, a miraculous fiddler of Slavic mythology and a god of joy, perhaps also of sexuality. His stories were first published by Janez Trdina in 1858 from tales collected at Mengeš in Carniola, though their authenticity is sometimes questioned. He also appears in Kurent and the Man and Kurent Turned into an Ox.

long_description.id: Setelah terlupakan sebagai dewa, ia bertahan sebagai roh pengusir musim dingin saat karnaval, dan kini dikenal lewat topeng kurenti dari Ptujsko polje. Para peneliti membandingkannya dengan Bakkhus, Siwa, Priapos, atau Keremet; Grafenauer menyebutnya dewa bulan yang jahat, sedangkan Monika Kropej menganggapnya dewa kesuburan.
long_description.en: Forgotten as a god, he survived as a spirit chasing winter away at carnival and is known today through the kurenti masks of Ptujsko polje. Scholars have compared him to Bacchus, Shiva, Priapus or Keremet; Grafenauer called him a malevolent moon god, while Monika Kropej sees a fertility god.

statement.en: Davorin Trstenjak compared him to the Hindu Shiva and Matevž Ravnikar-Poženčan to the Greek Priapus, while France Bezlaj derived his name from the root kur, 'to create, to work'.

statement.id: Monika Kropej mencatat bahwa saat karnaval di Slovenia para kurent ditemani pikeci ("anak ayam"), mengaitkannya dengan korybant pengiring dewi Kybele, dan menganggap Kurent dewa kesuburan dan kebebasan seksual.
statement.en: Monika Kropej notes that at Slovene carnival the kurents are accompanied by pikeci ('chicks'), links this with the Corybantes who attended the goddess Cybele, and considers Kurent a god of fertility and sexual licence.

short_description.id: Kyūso adalah tikus yang menjadi yōkai karena usia.
short_description.en: Kyūso is a rat that becomes a yōkai with age.

long_description.id: Kyūso adalah tikus yang menjadi yōkai karena usia. Berbagai kisah menggambarkannya memakan kucing, membesarkan anak kucing, atau menyakiti manusia. Satu kisah menyebutnya membesarkan anak kucing yatim sebelum menghilang.
long_description.en: Kyūso is a rat that becomes a yōkai with age. Accounts variously describe it eating cats, raising kittens or harming humans. One story has it raise orphaned kittens before disappearing.

long_description.id: Kisah lain menggambarkan tikus tiga warna di Yamato yang memakan kucing. Kisah belakangan membandingkan ukurannya dengan kucing atau anjing sedang. Uraian belakangan menduga permainan kata dari pepatah tikus terpojok menggigit kucing.
long_description.en: Another account describes a tricolored rat in Yamato that ate cats. A later account compares its size with cats or medium-sized dogs. The later account proposes a pun on the saying that a cornered rat bites a cat.

short_description.id: Llŷr kemungkinan adalah dewa laut dalam mitologi Wales, berkerabat dengan Ler dari Irlandia, dan ayah Brân, Brânwen, serta Manawydan.
short_description.en: Llŷr was probably a sea god of Welsh myth, related to the Irish Ler, and father of Brân, Brânwen and Manawydan.

long_description.id: Llŷr (Wales/Welsh: Llŷr Llediaith; Lleddiaith berarti "setengah bicara" atau "setengah bahasa") kemungkinan adalah dewa laut dalam mitologi Wales, berkerabat dengan Ler dari Irlandia (Irish), "Sang Laut", ayah Manannán mac Lir. Dalam sebagian legenda ia pemimpin Children of Llyr yang terus berperang dengan Children of Dôn. Dalam Branwen, Daughter of Llyr, Cabang Kedua Mabinogi, ia ayah Brân, Brânwen, dan Manawydan dari Penarddun. Welsh Triads menyebut Llŷr dipenjarakan oleh Euroswydd, yang kemudian tampaknya menikahi Penarddun dan menjadi ayah Nisien dan Efnisien.
long_description.en: Llŷr (Welsh Llŷr Llediaith; Lleddiaith meaning 'half-speech' or 'half-language') was probably a sea god of Welsh myth, kin to the Irish Ler, 'the Sea', father of Manannán mac Lir. Some legends make him leader of the Children of Llyr, forever at war with the Children of Dôn. In Branwen, Daughter of Llyr, the Second Branch of the Mabinogi, he is the father of Brân, Brânwen and Manawydan by Penarddun. The Welsh Triads say Llŷr was jailed by Euroswydd, who apparently then wed Penarddun and fathered Nisien and Efnisien.

long_description.id: Lakon William Shakespeare King Lear berdasar secara tidak langsung pada raja mitos Geoffrey of Monmouth, King Leir, yang sering dikaitkan dengan Llŷr meski kemungkinan tidak berhubungan. Menurut artikel de, llyr dalam bahasa Wales berarti "laut" dan Llŷr adalah padanan Wales dari dewa laut Irlandia Lir; baik Llŷr maupun Lir tampaknya punya kedekatan dengan burung, karena nama anak-anak Llŷr memuat lambang gagak. Ia juga disebut salah satu dari "tiga tahanan agung Pulau Britania".
long_description.en: William Shakespeare's King Lear rests, at second hand, on Geoffrey of Monmouth's mythical King Leir, often linked with Llŷr though probably unrelated. According to the de article, llyr means 'sea' in Welsh and Llŷr is the Welsh counterpart of the Irish sea god Lir; both seem to have a bird affinity, since the names of Llŷr's children carry raven symbolism. He is also named one of the 'three exalted prisoners of the Isle of Britain'.

short_description.id: Hantu Longga adalah hantu bertubuh sangat tinggi dalam cerita rakyat Bugis dan Makassar di Sulawesi Selatan.
short_description.en: Hantu Longga is an unusually tall ghost in Bugis and Makassar folklore of South Sulawesi.

long_description.id: Sebuah kajian tentang kepercayaan Makassar mencatat Setang Longga sebagai hantu gentayangan yang sangat jangkung. Nama longga dijelaskan sebagai sebutan bagi sesuatu yang tinggi atau orang berpostur jangkung. Kajian lain mencatat Hantu Longga dalam kepercayaan Bugis dan kisah kemunculannya di jalan sepi pada malam hari. Artikel ensiklopedia juga mencatat nama Hantu Dongga sebagai sebutan lain.
long_description.en: A study of Makassar beliefs records Setang Longga as a wandering ghost of exceptional height. It explains longga as referring to height or a tall person. Another study records Hantu Longga in Bugis belief and stories of its appearance on quiet roads at night. An encyclopedia article also records Hantu Dongga as an alternative name.

short_description.id: Lorelei adalah ondina atau peri air Sungai Rhein dalam legenda Jerman, yang memikat para pelaut dengan kecantikan dan nyanyiannya dari batu karang yang menyandang namanya hingga kapal mereka karam.
short_description.en: Lorelei is an undine or water nymph of the Rhine in German legend, who lured boatmen with her beauty and song from the rock that bears her name until their vessels were wrecked.

long_description.id: Menurut legenda, Lorelei adalah ondina cantik Sungai Rhein yang memikat para lelaki dengan nyanyian dan rupanya, sehingga terjadi kapal karam dan bencana. Batu karang tempat ia menurut tradisi menampakkan diri hingga kini masih menyandang namanya.
long_description.en: According to legend, Lorelei was a beautiful undine of the Rhine who drew men to her with her singing and looks, bringing shipwreck and disaster. The rock where tradition says she appeared still carries her name today.

long_description.id: Ia konon semula gadis cantik yang dikhianati lelaki yang dicintainya lalu terjun dari tebing karena tak sanggup menanggung pedihnya; artikel bahasa Turki menyebutnya ingin membalas dendam kepada para pelaut setelah dikhianati seorang nelayan kekasihnya.
long_description.en: She is said to have first been a lovely girl betrayed by the man she loved, who threw herself from a cliff because she could not bear the pain; the Turkish article says she sought revenge on boatmen after being deceived by the fisherman she loved.

long_description.id: Suatu hari, untuk membalas kematian putranya, seorang bangsawan mengirim prajurit yang tahan terhadap pesonanya untuk membunuh Lorelei. Mereka hampir berhasil, tetapi Lorelei memanggil ayahnya, yang mengirim seekor kuda buih untuk membawanya ke dasar sungai; ia tak pernah kembali, dan sejak itu para pelaut tidak lagi perlu takut padanya.
long_description.en: One day a nobleman, avenging his dead son, sent soldiers who could resist her charm to kill Lorelei. They nearly succeeded, but she called on her father, who sent a horse of foam to carry her down into the depths of the river; she never returned, and from then on boatmen no longer had to fear her.

role.en: Her song wrecks ships.

did_you_know.id: Untuk menyelamatkan Lorelei dari prajurit seorang bangsawan, ayahnya mengirim kuda buih yang membawanya ke dasar Sungai Rhein.
did_you_know.en: To save Lorelei from a nobleman's soldiers, her father sent a horse of foam that carried her to the bottom of the Rhine.

statement.en: According to legend she was a beautiful siren of the Rhine (Rin) who drew men from the rock bearing her name with her beauty and songs, causing shipwrecks and disasters.

claims.quote: Lorelei è una figura leggendaria della Germania.

statement.id: Lorelei adalah tokoh legenda dari Jerman (Germania).
statement.en: Lorelei is a legendary figure of Germany (Germania).

claims.quote: Secondo la leggenda, Lorelei era una bellissima ondina del fiume Reno, che attirava a sé gli uomini col suo canto e con il suo aspetto, causando naufragi e sciagure.

statement.id: Menurut legenda, Lorelei adalah ondina cantik Sungai Rhein (Reno) yang memikat para lelaki dengan nyanyian dan rupanya, menyebabkan kapal karam dan bencana; batu karang tempat ia menampakkan diri masih menyandang namanya.
statement.en: According to legend Lorelei was a lovely undine of the Rhine (Reno) who drew men with her song and looks, causing shipwrecks and misfortune; the rock where she appeared still bears her name.

claims.quote: Según se creía, originariamente era una hermosa muchacha que fue traicionada por el hombre al que amaba, tras lo cual se arrojó de un acantilado por no poder soportar el dolor.

statement.id: Konon ia semula gadis cantik yang dikhianati lelaki yang dicintainya, lalu terjun dari tebing karena tak sanggup menanggung pedihnya.
statement.en: She was believed to have first been a beautiful girl betrayed by the man she loved, who then threw herself from a cliff, unable to bear the pain.

claims.quote: Efsaneye göre âşık olduğu balıkçının kendisini aldatması üzerine gemicilerden öç almak istemektedir.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Turki, legenda menyebut ia ingin membalas dendam kepada para pelaut setelah nelayan kekasihnya mengkhianatinya.
statement.en: Per the Turkish article, the legend says she wants revenge on sailors after the fisherman she loved deceived her.

claims.quote: Un giorno, per vendicare il figlio morto, un nobile inviò i suoi soldati a uccidere la fanciulla, soldati che seppero resistere al suo incanto e che l'avrebbero uccisa, se lei non avesse chiamato suo padre in aiuto: egli mandò un cavallo di schiuma che condusse la ninfa nelle profondità del fiume, da cui ella non fece più ritorno.

statement.id: Untuk membalas kematian putranya, seorang bangsawan mengirim prajurit yang tahan pesona Lorelei untuk membunuhnya; ayahnya mengirim kuda buih yang membawanya ke dasar sungai dan ia tak pernah kembali.
statement.en: To avenge his dead son, a nobleman sent soldiers immune to her charm to kill her; her father sent a horse of foam that took the nymph to the river depths, from which she never returned.

claims.quote: Questa figura leggendaria si ritrova spesso nei componimenti dei poeti tedeschi dell'epoca romantica, come ad esempio in Das Lied der Loreley (1827) di Heinrich Heine o in Waldgespräch (1815) di Joseph Freiherr von Eichendorff. Fu inoltre proprio da questo mito che il compositore Alfredo Catalani trasse ispirazione per la sua opera Loreley.

statement.id: Tokoh ini sering muncul dalam karya penyair Jerman era Romantik, seperti Das Lied der Loreley (1827) karya Heinrich Heine dan Waldgespräch (1815) karya Joseph Freiherr von Eichendorff; komponis Alfredo Catalani terinspirasi mitos ini untuk operanya Loreley.
statement.en: The figure often appears in German Romantic poetry, as in Heinrich Heine's Das Lied der Loreley (1827) or Joseph Freiherr von Eichendorff's Waldgespräch (1815); composer Alfredo Catalani drew on the myth for his opera Loreley.

summary.id: Gadis yang dikhianati kekasihnya lalu terjun dari tebing.
summary.en: A girl betrayed by her lover who leapt from a cliff.

summary.id: Ingin membalas dendam setelah dikhianati nelayan kekasihnya.
summary.en: Seeks revenge after her fisherman lover deceived her.

short_description.id: Macchanu adalah putra Hanuman dalam versi Thailand dan versi lain Ramayana.
short_description.en: Macchanu is Hanuman's son in the Thai and other versions of the Ramayana.

long_description.id: Macchanu adalah putra Hanuman dalam versi Thailand dan versi lain Ramayana. Ia digambarkan bertubuh atas vanara dan berekor ikan.
long_description.en: Macchanu is Hanuman's son in the Thai and other versions of the Ramayana. He is described as having a vanara upper body and a fish tail.

long_description.id: Suara Akashvani mengungkapkan bahwa musuh yang hendak diserang Hanuman adalah putranya dari Suvannamaccha. Dalam versi lain, ia menjaga kolam pada perjalanan Hanuman mencari Rama dan Laxmana. Ia menyebut Maiyarap sebagai ayah angkat, lalu memberi petunjuk teka-teki tentang jalan masuk melalui teratai. Thailand Foundation menyebut Macchanu dibesarkan Maiyarap dan ditugaskan menjaga jalan masuk dunia bawah.
long_description.en: Akashvani reveals that the enemy Hanuman is about to harm is his own son by Suvannamaccha. In another version he guards a pond on Hanuman's journey to find Rama and Laxmana. He names Maiyarap as his foster father and gives a riddle about the entrance through a lotus. Thailand Foundation describes Macchanu as raised by Maiyarap and assigned to guard the netherworld entrance.

note.en: Macchanu's father.

sources.title: Ramakien: Thailand’s National Epic - Thailand Foundation

Thai version of the story and other versions of the Ramayana.

short_description.id: Mada dalam Mahabharata adalah kegilaan yang dipersonifikasikan sebagai asura.
short_description.en: Mada in the Mahabharata is madness personified as an asura.

long_description.id: Mada dalam Mahabharata adalah kegilaan yang dipersonifikasikan sebagai asura. Ia termasuk krtya, makhluk hasil sihir.
long_description.en: Mada in the Mahabharata is madness personified as an asura. He is categorized as a krtya, a product of sorcery.

long_description.id: Ia digambarkan amat besar dan mampu menelan seluruh kosmos. Cyavana memanggilnya ketika Indra menolak memberi Ashvin hak meminum soma. Ia muncul dari api persembahan. Setelah Indra menyerah, Cyavana menariknya kembali dan membaginya menjadi empat bagian. Terjemahan Mahabharata menuturkan satu rahang Mada berada di bumi dan yang lainnya mencapai langit.
long_description.en: He is described as immense and able to swallow the entire cosmos. Cyavana calls him when Indra refuses the Ashvins the right to drink soma. He appears from the sacrificial fire. After Indra surrenders Cyavana withdraws him and divides him into four parts. The Mahabharata translation recounts one of Mada's jaws resting on earth and the other reaching heaven.

sources.title: The Mahabharata, Vana Parva, Part I

short_description.id: Mahishasura adalah asura berwujud kerbau dalam Hindu.
short_description.en: Mahishasura is a bovine asura in Hinduism.

long_description.id: Mahishasura adalah asura berwujud kerbau dalam Hindu. Cerita menggambarkannya menggunakan perubahan wujud untuk menjalankan niat jahat.
long_description.en: Mahishasura is a bovine asura in Hinduism. The narrative depicts him using shape shifting to pursue evil intentions.

long_description.id: Ia disebut putra Rambha dan saudara Mahishi. Durga membunuhnya dengan trisula dan memperoleh epitet Mahishasuramardini. Navaratri merayakan pertempuran itu dan berakhir dengan perayaan kekalahannya pada Vijayadashami. Dalam kisah, ia memperoleh anugerah bahwa tidak ada laki-laki yang dapat membunuhnya. Versi WHE menggambarkan Mahisa bertubuh manusia dan berkepala kerbau.
long_description.en: He is called Rambha's son and Mahishi's brother. Durga kills him with a trident and gains the epithet Mahishasuramardini. Navaratri celebrates the battle and culminates in celebrating his defeat at Vijayadashami. In the narrative he obtains a boon that no man can kill him. WHE's version depicts Mahisa with a human body and buffalo head.

note.en: Mahishasura's slayer in the narrative.

claims.quote: is a bovine asura in Hinduism. He is depicted in Hindu literature as a deceitful demon who pursued his evil ways by shape-shifting.

statement.id: Mahishasura adalah asura berwujud kerbau dalam Hindu.
statement.en: Mahishasura is a bovine asura in Hinduism.

claims.quote: Mahishasura (Sanskrit: महिषासुर, IAST: Mahiṣāsura), (Kannada: ಮಹಿಷಾಸುರ) is a bovine asura in Hinduism. He is depicted in Hindu literature as a deceitful demon who pursued his evil ways by shape-shifting. Mahishasura was the son of the asura Rambha and the brother of buffalo-demoness named Mahishi.

statement.id: Cerita menggambarkannya menggunakan perubahan wujud untuk menjalankan niat jahat.
statement.en: The narrative depicts him using shape shifting to pursue evil intentions.

statement.en: He is called Rambha's son and Mahishi's brother.

claims.quote: He was ultimately killed by the goddess Durga with her trishula (trident) after which she gained the epithet Mahishasuramardini ("Slayer of Mahishasura").

statement.id: Durga membunuhnya dengan trisula dan memperoleh epitet Mahishasuramardini.
statement.en: Durga kills him with a trident and gains the epithet Mahishasuramardini.

claims.quote: The Navaratri ("Nine Nights") festival eulogises this battle between Mahishasura and Durga, culminating in Vijayadashami, a celebration of his ultimate defeat. This story of the "triumph of good over evil" carries profound symbolism in Hinduism, particularly Shaktism, and is both narrated as well as reenacted from the Devi Mahatmya at many South and Southeast Asian Hindu temples.
