short_description.id: Kamunaobi dan Ōnaobi adalah dewa pemulih Shinto yang terkait dengan penghapusan pencemaran.
short_description.en: Kamunaobi and Ōnaobi are Shinto rectifying deities associated with removing pollution.

long_description.id: Kamunaobi dan Ōnaobi adalah dewa pemulih Shinto yang terkait dengan penghapusan pencemaran. Mereka muncul untuk memulihkan malapetaka setelah penyucian Izanagi dari Yomi. Kojiki mencantumkan pasangan itu bersama Izunome.
long_description.en: Kamunaobi and Ōnaobi are Shinto rectifying deities associated with removing pollution. They arise to repair calamities following Izanagi’s purification from Yomi. The Kojiki lists the pair together with Izunome.

long_description.id: Satu versi Nihon Shoki menempatkan Ōnaobi sebelum dewa malapetaka. Terjemahan universitas menyebut kedua dewa itu pemulih malapetaka. Catatan terjemahan menjelaskan nao sebagai lurus atau memulihkan.
long_description.en: A Nihon Shoki variant places Ōnaobi before the calamity deity. The university translation presents both deities as rectifiers of calamity. The translation notes explain nao as straight or rectifying.

claims.quote: 直毘神（なおびのかみ、なほびのかみ）は神道の神である。 穢れを払い、禍（まが）を直す神とする説がある。

statement.id: Kamunaobi dan Ōnaobi adalah dewa pemulih Shinto yang terkait dengan penghapusan pencemaran.
statement.en: Kamunaobi and Ōnaobi are Shinto rectifying deities associated with removing pollution.

claims.quote: 日本神話の神産みにおいて、黄泉から帰ったイザナギが禊を行って黄泉の穢れを祓ったときに、その穢れから禍津日神が生まれた。この禍津日神がもたらす禍を直すために生まれたのが直毘神である。

statement.id: Mereka muncul untuk memulihkan malapetaka setelah penyucian Izanagi dari Yomi.
statement.en: They arise to repair calamities following Izanagi’s purification from Yomi.

claims.quote: 『古事記』では八十禍津日神・大禍津日神が成った後に神直毘神（かみなほびのかみ）、大直毘神（おほなほびのかみ）と伊豆能売の三柱が成ったとしている。

statement.id: Kojiki mencantumkan pasangan itu bersama Izunome.
statement.en: The Kojiki lists the pair together with Izunome.

claims.quote: 同段第十の一書では少し異なっており、イザナギが禊の際に大直日神を生み、その後に大綾津日神（大禍津日神と同一神格）を生んだとしている。

statement.id: Satu versi Nihon Shoki menempatkan Ōnaobi sebelum dewa malapetaka.
statement.en: A Nihon Shoki variant places Ōnaobi before the calamity deity.

claims.quote: Next, to rectify the calamities [they brought], a deity named Kamunaobi no kami 神直毗神 came into existence. Next, Ōnaobi no kami 大直毗神 (2).

statement.id: Terjemahan universitas menyebut kedua dewa itu pemulih malapetaka.
statement.en: The university translation presents both deities as rectifiers of calamity.

claims.quote: These nao (“straight,” “rectifying”) deities are the counterpart to the maga deities described in the previous text note.

statement.id: Catatan terjemahan menjelaskan nao sebagai lurus atau memulihkan.
statement.en: The translation notes explain nao as straight or rectifying.

short_description.id: Kanayamahiko adalah dewa dalam mitologi Jepang.
short_description.en: Kanayamahiko is a deity in Japanese mythology.

long_description.id: Kanayamahiko adalah dewa dalam mitologi Jepang. Ia dipasangkan dengan dewi Kanayamahime. Pasangan itu ditafsirkan sebagai dewa pertambangan.
long_description.en: Kanayamahiko is a deity in Japanese mythology. He is paired with the goddess Kanayamahime. The pair is interpreted as deities of mines.

long_description.id: Kojiki menyebut Kanayamahiko muncul dari muntahan Izanami. Kelahirannya terjadi setelah Izanami terluka akibat melahirkan Kagutsuchi. Versi alternatif Nihon Shoki hanya menyebut Kanayamahiko dalam peristiwa kelahiran ini.
long_description.en: The Kojiki has Kanayamahiko emerge from Izanami’s vomit. His birth follows Izanami’s injuries from bearing Kagutsuchi. A Nihon Shoki variant mentions only Kanayamahiko in this birth episode.

claims.quote: 金山彦神（かなやまひこのかみ）は、日本神話に登場する神である。天津国玉神の父という説がある。

statement.id: Kanayamahiko adalah dewa dalam mitologi Jepang.
statement.en: Kanayamahiko is a deity in Japanese mythology.

claims.quote: 『古事記』では金山毘古神、『日本書紀』では金山彦神と表記する。金山毘売神（かなやまびめのかみ、金山姫神）と対偶をなす神である。

statement.id: Ia dipasangkan dengan dewi Kanayamahime.
statement.en: He is paired with the goddess Kanayamahime.

claims.quote: 「金山」は鉱山と解するのが一般的で、金山毘古神・金山毘売神の二神は鉱山の神と解釈される。

statement.id: Pasangan itu ditafsirkan sebagai dewa pertambangan.
statement.en: The pair is interpreted as deities of mines.

claims.quote: From her vomit (2) was born a deity named Kanayamabiko no kami 金山毗古神. Next [appeared] Kanayamabime no kami 金山毗売神 (3).

statement.id: Kojiki menyebut Kanayamahiko muncul dari muntahan Izanami.
statement.en: The Kojiki has Kanayamahiko emerge from Izanami’s vomit.

claims.quote: 神産みにおいて、イザナミが火の神カグツチを産んで火傷をし病み苦しんでいるときに、その嘔吐物（たぐり）から化生した神である。

statement.id: Kelahirannya terjadi setelah Izanami terluka akibat melahirkan Kagutsuchi.
statement.en: His birth follows Izanami’s injuries from bearing Kagutsuchi.

claims.quote: 『古事記』では金山毘古神・金山毘売神の二神、『日本書紀』の第三の一書では金山彦神のみが化生している。

statement.id: Versi alternatif Nihon Shoki hanya menyebut Kanayamahiko dalam peristiwa kelahiran ini.
statement.en: A Nihon Shoki variant mentions only Kanayamahiko in this birth episode.

topic.id: Dewa yang muncul pada peristiwa kelahiran
topic.en: Deities appearing in the birth episode

summary.id: Kojiki menyebut Kanayamahiko lalu Kanayamahime.

long_description.id: Karkotaka adalah raja naga Hindu, putra Kashyapa dan Kadru. Ia tinggal di hutan dekat kerajaan Nishadha.
long_description.en: Karkotaka is a Hindu naga king, child of Kashyapa and Kadru. He lives in a forest near the Nishadha kingdom.

short_description.id: Karna adalah tokoh utama wiracarita Hindu Mahabharata dan putra Surya serta Kunti.
short_description.en: Karna is a major character in the Hindu epic Mahabharata and son of Surya and Kunti.

long_description.id: Karna adalah tokoh utama wiracarita Hindu Mahabharata dan putra Surya serta Kunti. Radha dan Adhiratha menemukan dan membesarkannya setelah ia ditinggalkan dalam keranjang di Gangga.
long_description.en: Karna is a major character in the Hindu epic Mahabharata and son of Surya and Kunti. Radha and Adhiratha find and foster him after he is abandoned in a basket on the Ganges.

long_description.id: Ia menjadi sahabat Duryodhana dan diangkat sebagai raja Anga. Ia berperang di pihak Kaurava dan akhirnya dibunuh Arjuna. Menurut penjelasan David Slavitt, nama masa kecilnya Vasusena dan nama Karna dikaitkan dengan anting emas Surya. Mackenzie menceritakan putra Pritha dan dewa matahari disembunyikan dalam keranjang yang dihanyutkan di sungai.
long_description.en: He becomes Duryodhana's friend and is appointed king of Anga. He fights on the Kaurava side and is ultimately killed by Arjuna. According to David Slavitt's explanation, his childhood name is Vasusena and the name Karna is linked to Surya's golden earrings. Mackenzie recounts Pritha and the sun god's son being concealed in a basket floated on a river.

short_description.id: Kasuga Gongen adalah identitas ilahi kolektif yang berkaitan dengan Kasuga Taisha.
short_description.en: Kasuga Gongen is a collective divine identity associated with Kasuga Taisha.

long_description.id: Kasuga Gongen adalah identitas ilahi kolektif yang berkaitan dengan Kasuga Taisha. Sebutan itu merujuk pada lima dewa sekaligus wujud ilahi gabungan mereka. Kelompok itu mencakup Takemikazuchi, Futsunushi, Ame no Koyane, Himegami, dan Ame no Oshikumone.
long_description.en: Kasuga Gongen is a collective divine identity associated with Kasuga Taisha. It refers both to five deities and to their combined divine form. The group includes Takemikazuchi, Futsunushi, Ame no Koyane, Himegami and Ame no Oshikumone.

long_description.en: The deer around Nara are regarded as the deity’s messengers. The shrine’s historical account records a hall for four deities in 768. Its origin narrative connects the first deity with protecting the capital.

short_description.id: Katakurokushin adalah nama kolektif enam dewa rumah Jepang yang lahir dari Izanagi dan Izanami.
short_description.en: Katakurokushin is the collective name of six Japanese household deities born to Izanagi and Izanami.

long_description.id: Katakurokushin adalah nama kolektif enam dewa rumah Jepang yang lahir dari Izanagi dan Izanami. Kelompok itu melambangkan bagian dan bahan bangunan. Tafsir mengaitkan Ishitsuchibiko dengan tanah dan Ishisuhime dengan pasir.
long_description.en: Katakurokushin is the collective name of six Japanese household deities born to Izanagi and Izanami. The group represents parts and materials of a building. Interpretations associate Ishitsuchibiko with soil and Ishisuhime with sand.

short_description.id: Katie King adalah nama yang diberikan kaum Spiritualis tahun 1870-an kepada sosok yang mereka yakini sebagai roh yang mewujud (materialisasi) dalam seans.
short_description.en: Katie King is the name 1870s Spiritualists gave to what they took to be a spirit materialising at séances.

long_description.id: Katie King adalah nama yang diberikan kaum Spiritualis pada 1870-an kepada apa yang mereka percayai sebagai roh yang mewujud. Apakah roh itu nyata atau tipuan menjadi kontroversi publik pada pertengahan 1870-an. Ia dikatakan pertama muncul antara 1871 dan 1874 dalam seans medium Florence Cook di London, kemudian pada 1874–1875 di New York dalam seans pasangan medium Jennie dan Nelson Holmes. Kaum Spiritualis menganggapnya putri John King, roh pengendali (spirit control) yang mengaku roh bajak laut Henry Morgan.
long_description.en: Katie King was the name 1870s Spiritualists gave to what they held to be a materialised spirit, and whether she was genuine or a fraud became a public dispute in the middle of that decade. She reportedly first appeared from 1871 to 1874 at séances given by Florence Cook in London, and in 1874–1875 in New York with the mediums Jennie and Nelson Holmes. Spiritualists regarded her as the daughter of John King, a spirit control claiming to be the buccaneer Henry Morgan.

long_description.id: Pada 9 Desember 1873 di Hackney, pengacara William Volckman menangkap tangan dan pinggang "roh" itu dan menuduhnya Cook yang menyamar. Ilmuwan Sir William Crookes kemudian menelitinya antara 1871 dan 1874; artikel es menyebut ia memperoleh 44 foto. Di New York, seorang perempuan bernama Eliza White mengaku pernah menyamar sebagai Katie, dan wajahnya cocok dengan foto-foto yang dijual keluarga Holmes.
long_description.en: At Hackney on 9 December 1873 the lawyer William Volckman grabbed the 'spirit' by the hand and waist and accused it of being Cook in disguise. The scientist Sir William Crookes later studied the phenomenon between 1871 and 1874; the es article credits him with 44 photographs. In New York a woman named Eliza White said she had posed as Katie, and her face matched the photographs the Holmeses sold.

short_description.id: Keibu Keioiba adalah makhluk berkepala harimau dan bertubuh manusia dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Meitei di Manipur.
short_description.en: Keibu Keioiba is a tiger-headed, human-bodied creature of Meitei mythology and folklore in Manipur.

long_description.id: Keibu Keioiba adalah makhluk berkepala harimau dan bertubuh manusia dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Meitei di Manipur. Menurut legenda, ia dahulu pendeta Kabui Salang Maiba yang menggunakan sihir untuk berubah menjadi harimau.
long_description.en: Keibu Keioiba is a tiger-headed, human-bodied creature of Meitei mythology and folklore in Manipur. Legend describes him as the priest Kabui Salang Maiba who used witchcraft to become a tiger.

long_description.id: Dalam kisahnya, seorang perempuan tua mengarahkan makhluk itu kepada Thabaton yang tinggal sendirian. Ia membawa Thabaton ke hutan dan memaksanya menjadi istrinya. Thabaton menyuruhnya mengambil air dengan pipa terbuka di kedua ujung agar dapat melarikan diri bersama saudara-saudaranya. Dalam terjemahan cerita Jayantakumar Sharma, Keibu Keioiba menjadi manusia pada siang hari dan harimau pada malam hari.
long_description.en: In the tale an old woman directs the creature to Thabaton, who is home alone. He takes Thabaton to the forest and forces her to become his wife. Thabaton sends him to fetch water with a pipe open at both ends so she can escape with her brothers. In the translation of Jayantakumar Sharma's tale Keibu Keioiba is human by day and a tiger at night.

claims.quote: Keibu Keioiba, also known as Kabui Keioiba, is a mythical creature with the head of a tiger and the body of a human in the Meitei mythology and folklore of Manipur. According to legend, he was once a skilful priest named Kabui Salang Maiba. He used witchcraft to turn himself into a ferocious tiger. As punishment of his pride, he could not completely turn back to his original human form.

statement.id: Keibu Keioiba adalah makhluk berkepala harimau dan bertubuh manusia dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Meitei di Manipur.
statement.en: Keibu Keioiba is a tiger-headed, human-bodied creature of Meitei mythology and folklore in Manipur.

statement.en: Legend describes him as the priest Kabui Salang Maiba who used witchcraft to become a tiger.

claims.quote: Keibu Keioiba was a human in the daytime and a tiger at night. During night, he prowled around looking for food. One night, he found an older woman's house and planned to devour her. The old woman said that her wrinkled skin would not be tasty and suggested that he eat a beautiful and young woman named Thabaton instead. Thabaton was the only sister in a family with seven brothers.

statement.en: In the tale an old woman directs the creature to Thabaton, who is home alone.

claims.quote: Keibu Keioiba has not eaten Thabaton. Instead, he has forced Thabaton to become his wife, and they live together in the forest.

statement.en: He takes Thabaton to the forest and forces her to become his wife.

short_description.id: Kianda atau Dandalunda adalah dewi laut dan pelindung nelayan dalam tradisi budaya Angola dan mitologi Bantu.
short_description.en: Kianda or Dandalunda is a sea goddess and protector of fishermen in Angolan culture and Bantu mythology.

long_description.id: Kianda, yang juga dikenal sebagai Dandalunda atau Quianda, adalah dewi perairan, laut, dan pelindung bagi kaum nelayan dalam kepercayaan tradisional Angola serta mitologi Bantu. Penghormatan kepadanya secara turun-temurun dilakukan dengan mempersembahkan makanan dan pakaian ke dalam laut.
long_description.en: Kianda, also known as Dandalunda or Quianda, is a deity of waters, seas, and the protector of fishers in Angolan folklore and Bantu mythology. Traditional worship involves offering food and garments into the ocean.

long_description.id: Di kota Luanda, perayaan tahunan Luanda Island Feast diselenggarakan demi menghormati dewi ini, yang juga dirayakan sebelum prosesi Nossa Senhora do Cabo. Kehadirannya mengilhami sastra modern Angola, seperti dalam karya penulis Pepetela berjudul O Desejo de Kianda.
long_description.en: In Luanda, an annual festival known as the Luanda Island Feast honors the deity, also held before the Procession of Nossa Senhora do Cabo. Her cultural significance is reflected in Angolan literature, notably in works by author Pepetela such as O Desejo de Kianda.

short_description.id: Kingu atau Qingu adalah dewa Mesopotamia yang dikenal dari Enuma Elish.
short_description.en: Kingu, or Qingu, is a Mesopotamian deity known from the Enuma Elish.

long_description.id: Kingu atau Qingu adalah dewa Mesopotamia yang dikenal dari Enuma Elish. Qingu menjadi bawahan sekaligus pasangan Tiamat dan musuh Marduk.
long_description.en: Kingu, or Qingu, is a Mesopotamian deity known from the Enuma Elish. Qingu is Tiamat’s subordinate and spouse and Marduk’s adversary.

long_description.id: Setelah kalah, Qingu dibunuh dan darahnya dipakai menciptakan manusia. Ejaan Qingu lebih umum dan dinilai lebih dekat pada pelafalan asli daripada Kingu. Nama Qingu dipandang berasal dari bahasa Sumeria. Qingu menjadi jagoan Tiamat dalam perang melawan dewa muda.
long_description.en: After defeat, Qingu is killed and his blood is used to create humanity. The spelling Qingu is more common and considered closer to the original pronunciation than Kingu. Qingu’s name is regarded as having a Sumerian origin. Qingu is Tiamat’s champion in the war against younger gods.

short_description.id: Kokuri-baba adalah yōkai perempuan tua dalam kumpulan Sekien.
short_description.en: Kokuri-baba is an old-woman yōkai in Sekien’s collection.

long_description.id: Kokuri-baba adalah yōkai perempuan tua dalam kumpulan Sekien. Sekien menggambarkan janda pendeta yang mencuri persembahan kuil dan memakan mayat. Teks Tiongkok yang dikutip menjelaskan kata istri pendeta, bukan yōkai ini.
long_description.en: Kokuri-baba is an old-woman yōkai in Sekien’s collection. Sekien depicts a priest’s widow stealing temple offerings and eating corpses. The cited Chinese text explains the word priest’s wife, not this yōkai.

long_description.id: Peneliti menafsirkan gambar itu sebagai sindiran terhadap pendeta yang melanggar sumpah. Kisah belakangan menempatkannya tersembunyi di bagian belakang kuil sambil memakan mayat. Uraian belakangan secara tegas mengatribusikan penciptaannya kepada Sekien.
long_description.en: Researchers interpret the image as satire of priests breaking their vows. A later account places her hidden in temple quarters feeding on corpses. The later account explicitly attributes the invention to Sekien.

short_description.id: Konohanasakuyahime adalah dewi bunga dalam mitos Ninigi yang kemudian dipuja sebagai dewi Gunung Fuji.
short_description.en: Konohanasakuyahime is a blossom goddess in the Ninigi myth who later became identified with Mt. Fuji’s deity.

long_description.id: Konohanasakuyahime adalah kami perempuan, putri dewa gunung Ōyamatsumi dan istri Ninigi. Namanya memuat unsur “bunga pohon” yang dikaitkan dengan singkatnya masa mekarnya sakura; kisah itu membandingkannya dengan kakaknya, Iwanagahime, yang berumur panjang. Menurut Kojiki dan Nihon Shoki, Ninigi bertemu dengannya di Tanjung Kasasa. Setelah ia hamil hanya dalam satu malam, Ninigi meragukan ayah anak itu. Untuk membuktikan keturunan dewa langit, ia membakar pondok tempat melahirkan dan melahirkan tiga putra di tengah api; versi Kojiki menamai mereka Hoderi, Hosuseri, dan Hoori.
long_description.en: Konohanasakuyahime is a female kami, daughter of the mountain deity Ōyamatsumi and wife of Ninigi. Her name contains “tree-flower,” linked to the brief beauty of cherry blossoms and contrasted with her long-lived elder sister Iwanagahime. The Kojiki and Nihon Shoki say Ninigi met her at Cape Kasasa. When she became pregnant after only one night, Ninigi doubted the child’s paternity. To prove descent from a heavenly deity, she set fire to her birthing hut and delivered three sons amid the flames; the Kojiki names them Hoderi, Hosuseri, and Hoori.

long_description.id: Konohanasakuyahime kini berhubungan erat dengan pemujaan Gunung Fuji dan kuil Asama atau Sengen. Namun, penyamaan dirinya dengan dewa gunung itu memiliki sejarah yang ditelusuri ke awal abad ke-17. Jimat tahun 1788 masih menampilkan Amida di atas Fuji, sedangkan jimat tahun 1860 menampilkan dewi Shinto. Pada abad ke-19, patung yang lebih tua pun mulai ditafsirkan sebagai dirinya. Sesudah kebijakan pemisahan Shinto dan Buddha pada 1868, penyamaan ini menjadi hampir universal di kuil-kuil Asama dan Sengen.
long_description.en: Konohanasakuyahime is now closely linked to worship at Mt. Fuji and Asama or Sengen shrines. That identification has a history dating to the early seventeenth century. A 1788 amulet still showed Amida above Fuji, while an 1860 amulet showed a Shinto goddess. By the nineteenth century, older statues were being interpreted as her images. After the 1868 policy separating Shinto and Buddhism, the identification became almost universal at Asama and Sengen shrines.

statement.en: The Shinto-Buddhist separation policy came in 1868 after the shift at Fuji.

short_description.id: Kotoamatsukami adalah sebutan bagi lima kami pertama dalam Kojiki. Kelompok ini mencakup tiga kami penciptaan.
short_description.en: Kotoamatsukami names the first five kami in the Kojiki, including the three creation kami.

long_description.id: Dalam Kojiki, Kotoamatsukami merujuk pada lima kami awal. Tiga di antaranya ialah Amenominakanushi, Takamimusuhi, dan Kamimusuhi, yang bersama-sama disebut tiga kami penciptaan. Dua anggota lainnya ialah Umashiashikabihikoji dan Amenotokotachi.
long_description.en: In the Kojiki, Kotoamatsukami refers to five early kami. Three are Amenominakanushi, Takamimusuhi, and Kamimusuhi, together called the three creation kami. The other two are Umashiashikabihikoji and Amenotokotachi.

long_description.id: Ensiklopedia Shinto menjelaskan bahwa kelimanya hadir sendiri dan kemudian menyembunyikan diri. Istilah Kotoamatsukami terdapat dalam Kojiki, tetapi tidak ditemukan dalam Nihongi. Dengan demikian, nama kelompok ini merujuk pada susunan dewa dalam satu teks tertentu.
long_description.en: The Encyclopedia of Shinto says all five came into existence alone and later hid themselves. The term Kotoamatsukami occurs in the Kojiki but is absent from the Nihongi. The group name therefore refers to the arrangement of deities in a particular text.

claims.quote: In Shinto, Kotoamatsukami (別天津神; literally "distinguishing heavenly kami") is the collective name for the first gods which came into existence at the time of the creation of the universe.

statement.en: Kotoamatsukami is a collective name for early Shinto deities.

statement.en: Three of the five are Amenominakanushi, Takamimusuhi, and Kamimusuhi.

statement.en: The other two are Umashiashikabihikoji and Amenotokotachi.

claims.quote: These five kami are characterized by the fact that they came into existence alone (hitorigami), and after coming into being, "hid" themselves.

statement.id: Kelima kami itu dikisahkan muncul sendiri lalu menyembunyikan diri.
statement.en: The five kami are said to have come into existence alone and then hidden themselves.

short_description.id: Küldürgiş atau Kultarqaç adalah jin pembuat tertawa dalam kepercayaan rakyat Turk dan Altai, berwujud gadis yang tinggal di hutan dan padang serta menghadang orang untuk membuatnya tertawa dan menggelitikinya.
short_description.en: Küldürgiş or Kultarqaç is a laughter-causing jinn of Turkic and Altaic folk belief, appearing as girls who live in forests and steppes and waylay people to make them laugh and tickle them.

long_description.id: Dalam kepercayaan dan budaya rakyat Turk dan Altai, Küldürgiş, yang juga disebut Kultarqaç, adalah jin yang membuat orang tertawa. Kamus kedua menamainya jin tawa dan mencatat padanan Kultarkaç serta Kultarkaş. Makhluk ini dipercaya menghuni hutan dan padang.
long_description.en: In Turkic and Altaic folk belief and culture, Küldürgiş, also called Kultarqaç, is a jinn that makes people laugh. The second source names it the laughter jinn and records the equivalents Kultarkaç and Kultarkaş. These beings are thought to inhabit forests and steppes.

long_description.id: Küldürgiş digambarkan sebagai gadis-gadis berpayudara sangat besar. Mereka mencegat orang, terutama yang berjalan seorang diri, lalu setelah menangkapnya berulah agar orang itu tertawa dan kadang menggelitikinya.
long_description.en: Küldürgiş are pictured as girls with very large breasts. They stop people on their way, especially lone travellers, and once they catch someone they act up to make the person laugh and sometimes tickle them.

long_description.id: Kamus kedua menghubungkan kepercayaan ini dengan kebiasaan masyarakat menyebut gila orang yang terus tertawa sendiri saat sendirian, karena perilaku itu dikaitkan dengan makhluk gaib. Nama Küldürgiş berasal dari akar Kül/Gül yang bermakna tertawa dan membuat tertawa.
long_description.en: The second source connects this belief to the popular habit of calling people mad who keep laughing alone, since that behaviour was linked to spirit beings. The name Küldürgiş comes from the root Kül/Gül, meaning to laugh and to make laugh.

cultural_context.id: Menurut kamus kedua, kebiasaan menyebut gila orang yang tertawa sendirian berakar pada pengaitan perilaku itu dengan makhluk gaib seperti Küldürgiş.
cultural_context.en: According to the second source, the habit of calling people mad who laugh alone is rooted in linking that behaviour to spirit beings such as Küldürgiş.

literal_meaning.id: tertawa, membuat tertawa; makhluk yang membuat tertawa
literal_meaning.en: to laugh, to make laugh; the being that makes one laugh

who.id: Küldürgiş adalah jin tawa berwujud gadis.
who.en: Küldürgiş is a laughter jinn in the form of girls.

origin.id: Ia berasal dari kepercayaan rakyat Turk dan Altai.
origin.en: It comes from Turkic and Altaic folk belief.

role.id: Ia menghadang orang yang berjalan sendirian lalu membuatnya tertawa.
role.en: It waylays lone travellers and makes them laugh.

famous_for.id: Ia dikenal karena menggelitiki orang yang ditangkapnya.
famous_for.en: It is known for tickling the people it catches.

did_you_know.id: Kamus kedua mengaitkan kepercayaan pada Küldürgiş dengan anggapan bahwa orang yang tertawa sendiri itu gila.
did_you_know.en: The second source links belief in Küldürgiş to the notion that people who laugh to themselves are mad.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa tawa yang tidak wajar sering dikaitkan dengan makhluk gaib dalam cerita rakyat?
learning_questions.en: Why is unusual laughter often linked to spirit beings in folklore?

claims.quote: Küldürgiş və ya Kultarqaç — türk və altay xalq inancında və xalq mədəniyyətində güldürücü cin. Meşələr və çöllərdə yaşayırlar.

statement.id: Küldürgiş atau Kultarqaç adalah jin pembuat tertawa (güldürücü cin) dalam kepercayaan dan budaya rakyat Turk (türk) dan Altai (altay); mereka tinggal di hutan dan padang (meşələr və çöllər).
statement.en: Küldürgiş or Kultarqaç is a laughter-causing jinn (güldürücü cin) in Turkic (türk) and Altaic (altay) folk belief and folk culture; they live in forests and steppes (meşələr və çöllər).

claims.quote: Çox böyük məmələri olan qızlardır. İnsanları yaxalayanda onları güldürəcək davranışlar sərgilərlər. İnsanların yollarını kəsib qıdıqlarlar.

statement.id: Mereka gadis-gadis (qızlar) berpayudara sangat besar; saat menangkap orang, mereka berbuat hal yang membuat orang tertawa (güldürəcək), dan mereka menghadang jalan orang lalu menggelitikinya (qıdıqlarlar).
statement.en: They are girls (qızlar) with very large breasts; when they catch people they behave in ways that make them laugh (güldürəcək), and they block people's paths and tickle them (qıdıqlarlar).

claims.quote: (Kül/ Gül)kökündən törəmişdir. Gülmək və güldürmək mənası daşıyır.

statement.id: Namanya berasal dari akar Kül/Gül yang bermakna tertawa dan membuat tertawa (gülmək və güldürmək).
statement.en: The name derives from the root Kül/Gül, meaning to laugh and to make laugh (gülmək və güldürmək).

claims.quote: KÜLDÜRGİŞ: Güldürü Cini. ... Eşdeğer: KULTARKAÇ, KULTARKAŞ

statement.id: Kamus kedua mendefinisikan Küldürgiş sebagai jin tawa (Güldürü Cini), dengan padanan nama Kultarkaç dan Kultarkaş.
statement.en: The second source defines Küldürgiş as the laughter jinn (Güldürü Cini), with the equivalent names Kultarkaç and Kultarkaş.

claims.quote: Ormanlar ve çöllerde yaşadıklarına inanılır. Bu varlıklar çok büyük göğüsleri olan kızlardır.

statement.id: Mereka dipercaya tinggal di hutan dan padang (ormanlar ve çöller); makhluk ini gadis-gadis (kızlar) berpayudara sangat besar.
statement.en: They are believed to live in forests and steppes (ormanlar ve çöller); these beings are girls (kızlar) with very large breasts.

claims.quote: Özellikle yalnız gezen insanların yollarını keserler yakalayınca da onları güldürecek davranışlar sergilerler ve kimi zaman da gıdıklarlar.

statement.id: Mereka terutama menghadang orang yang bepergian sendirian (yalnız gezen insanların), dan setelah menangkapnya berbuat hal yang membuat tertawa serta kadang menggelitiki (gıdıklarlar).
statement.en: They especially block the way of people travelling alone (yalnız gezen insanların), and when they catch them they act to make them laugh and sometimes tickle them (gıdıklarlar).

claims.quote: Yalnızken sürekli kendi kendine gülen insanların halk arasında deli olarak nitelenmesinin veyâ o kişilerin uyarılmasının kökeninde de yine bu davranış biçiminin ruhsal varlıklara bağlanması ile alâkası vardır.

statement.id: Menurut kamus kedua, kebiasaan masyarakat menyebut gila (deli) orang yang terus tertawa sendiri saat sendirian, atau menegurnya, berakar pada pengaitan perilaku itu dengan makhluk gaib (ruhsal varlıklar).
statement.en: According to the second source, the popular habit of calling mad (deli) people who keep laughing to themselves when alone, or warning them, is rooted in linking that behaviour to spirit beings (ruhsal varlıklar).

claims.quote: Anlam: (Kül/Gül). Güldüren varlık demektir. Gülmek ve Güldürmek anlamları taşır.

statement.id: Namanya berarti makhluk yang membuat tertawa (güldüren varlık), dari akar Kül/Gül yang bermakna tertawa dan membuat tertawa.
statement.en: The name means the being that makes one laugh (güldüren varlık), from the root Kül/Gül meaning to laugh and to make laugh.

short_description.id: Kumanokusubi adalah dewa dalam mitologi Jepang.
short_description.en: Kumanokusubi is a deity in Japanese mythology.

long_description.id: Kumanokusubi adalah dewa dalam mitologi Jepang. Tradisi menghitungnya sebagai putra kelima Amaterasu. Kelahirannya merupakan bagian dari perlombaan antara Amaterasu dan Susanoo.
long_description.en: Kumanokusubi is a deity in Japanese mythology. The tradition counts him as Amaterasu’s fifth son. His birth belongs to a contest between Amaterasu and Susanoo.

long_description.id: Satu versi menggambarkan lima kami laki-laki lahir dari manik-manik yang dikunyah. Kojiki menghubungkan kemunculannya dengan untaian permata di pergelangan kanan Amaterasu. Narasi kelahiran menggambarkan bahan yang dikunyah diludahkan sebagai semburan berkabut.
long_description.en: One version describes five male kami arising from chewed beads. The Kojiki connects his emergence with the jeweled cord on Amaterasu’s right wrist. The birth narrative describes the chewed material being spat out as a misty spray.

claims.quote: Kumanokusubi (熊野久须毘命,熊野櫲樟日命, Wonder Worker of Bear Moors) is a God in Japanese mythology.

short_description.id: Dalam tradisi Nepal, Kumari adalah perwujudan hidup Taleju Bhawani yang dipuja melalui seorang anak perempuan Newar.
short_description.en: In Nepalese tradition Kumari is a living embodiment of Taleju Bhawani venerated through a Newar girl.

long_description.id: Dalam tradisi Nepal, Kumari adalah perwujudan hidup Taleju Bhawani yang dipuja melalui seorang anak perempuan Newar. Praktik ini melibatkan pemuja Hindu dan Buddha di Lembah Kathmandu.
long_description.en: In Nepalese tradition Kumari is a living embodiment of Taleju Bhawani venerated through a Newar girl. The practice involves Hindu and Buddhist devotees in the Kathmandu Valley.

long_description.id: Kumari berasal dari Sanskerta dalam arti perawan atau gadis muda belum menikah. Legenda pendirian menuturkan Taleju menghilang setelah pertemuan rahasianya dengan raja diketahui. Dalam mimpi, Taleju meminta raja mencari gadis Shakya tempat ia akan mewujud. Dewan Pariwisata Nepal menyatakan calon Kumari dipilih dari keluarga Buddhis klan Shakya.
long_description.en: Kumari derives from Sanskrit meaning virgin or young unmarried girl. The foundation legend recounts Taleju disappearing after her secret meetings with the king are discovered. In a dream Taleju asks the king to find a Shakya girl in whom she will manifest. The Nepal Tourism Board states that a Kumari candidate is selected from a Buddhist family of the Shakya clan.

cultural_context.id: Entri membahas manifestasi dewi dalam tradisi, bukan biografi gadis pemegang peran tertentu.
cultural_context.en: The entry treats a manifestation of the goddess in tradition, rather than a biography of an individual girl holding the role.

claims.quote: also known as the Living Goddess, is a centuries‑old tradition in Nepal in which a prepubescent girl from the Newar community is venerated as a living embodiment of the goddess Taleju Bhawani (a form of Durga).

statement.id: Dalam tradisi Nepal, Kumari adalah perwujudan hidup Taleju Bhawani yang dipuja melalui seorang anak perempuan Newar.
statement.en: In Nepalese tradition Kumari is a living embodiment of Taleju Bhawani venerated through a Newar girl.

claims.quote: The practice is central to the religious life of the Kathmandu Valley and draws devotees from both Hindu and Buddhist traditions.

statement.id: Praktik ini melibatkan pemuja Hindu dan Buddha di Lembah Kathmandu.
statement.en: The practice involves Hindu and Buddhist devotees in the Kathmandu Valley.

claims.quote: The word Kumari is derived from Sanskrit, where it means "virgin" or "young unmarried girl". In the Newar language the term is also rendered as kumhaḥ (𑐎𑐸𑐩𑑂𑐴𑑅).

statement.id: Kumari berasal dari Sanskerta dalam arti perawan atau gadis muda belum menikah.
statement.en: Kumari derives from Sanskrit meaning virgin or young unmarried girl.

claims.quote: the goddess Taleju would visit the king nightly to play Tripasa (a dice game), on condition that he tell no one of their meetings. One night the king’s daughter followed him and discovered the goddess, who was angered and vanished.

statement.id: Legenda pendirian menuturkan Taleju menghilang setelah pertemuan rahasianya dengan raja diketahui.
statement.en: The foundation legend recounts Taleju disappearing after her secret meetings with the king are discovered.

claims.quote: Taleju later appeared in a dream, telling the king to search for a young Shakya girl in whom she would manifest.

statement.id: Dalam mimpi, Taleju meminta raja mencari gadis Shakya tempat ia akan mewujud.
statement.en: In a dream Taleju asks the king to find a Shakya girl in whom she will manifest.

statement.id: Dewan Pariwisata Nepal menyatakan calon Kumari dipilih dari keluarga Buddhis klan Shakya.
statement.en: The Nepal Tourism Board states that a Kumari candidate is selected from a Buddhist family of the Shakya clan.

short_description.id: Kumbhakarna adalah rakshasa perkasa dan adik Ravana dalam Ramayana.
short_description.en: Kumbhakarna is a mighty rakshasa and Ravana's younger brother in the Ramayana.

long_description.id: Kumbhakarna adalah rakshasa perkasa dan adik Ravana dalam Ramayana. Teks Hindu menggambarkannya bertubuh raksasa dan berselera makan besar tetapi juga kesatria berbudi.
long_description.en: Kumbhakarna is a mighty rakshasa and Ravana's younger brother in the Ramayana. Hindu texts depict him as gigantic and voracious but also a virtuous warrior.

long_description.id: Menurut versi yang diringkas artikel, Brahma mengubah kutukannya menjadi tidur enam bulan dan bangun enam bulan. Dalam retelling lain, Saraswati membuat lidahnya meminta tempat tidur alih-alih takhta Indra. Dalam retelling ini ia tidur lagi setelah rasa laparnya terpenuhi. Dalam retelling Mackenzie, ia tidur enam bulan dan bangun hanya satu hari.
long_description.en: In the version summarized by the article Brahma modifies his curse to six months asleep and six months awake. In another retelling Saraswati makes his tongue request a sleeping bed instead of Indra's throne. In this retelling he sleeps again after his appetite is satisfied. In Mackenzie's retelling he sleeps six months and wakes for only one day.

note.en: Kumbhakarna's elder brother.

sources.title: The Project Gutenberg eBook of Indian Myth and Legend, by Donald A. Mackenzie.
sources.author: Donald A. Mackenzie
sources.publisher: The Gresham Publishing Company; Project Gutenberg

claims.quote: Kumbhakarna (Sanskrit: कुम्भकर्ण, lit. pot-eared) is a powerful rakshasa and younger brother of Ravana from the Hindu epic Ramayana. Despite his gigantic size and appetite, he is described as a virtuous character and a great warrior in Hindu texts. He is said to have slaughtered 8,000 vanaras over the course of Rama's mission to rescue Sita.

statement.id: Kumbhakarna adalah rakshasa perkasa dan adik Ravana dalam Ramayana.
statement.en: Kumbhakarna is a mighty rakshasa and Ravana's younger brother in the Ramayana.

claims.quote: he commuted the curse to have the rakshasa sleep for six months at a time, and wake up for other six months to wreak havoc and devour to his heart's content.

statement.id: Menurut versi yang diringkas artikel, Brahma mengubah kutukannya menjadi tidur enam bulan dan bangun enam bulan.
statement.en: In the version summarized by the article Brahma modifies his curse to six months asleep and six months awake.

claims.quote: When Kumbhakarna asked for his boon, his tongue was tied by the goddess Saraswati, who acted on Indra's request. Instead of asking for Indrāsana (the throne of Indra), he asked for Nidrāsana (a bed for sleeping). It is also said that he intended to ask for Nirdevatvam (annihilation of the devas) and instead asked for Nidravatvam (sleep). His request was instantly granted.

Brahma intervened and decreed that he

only.

short_description.id: Kuramitsuha adalah dewa Jepang yang lahir ketika Izanagi membunuh Kagutsuchi.
short_description.en: Kuramitsuha is a Japanese deity born when Izanagi slays Kagutsuchi.

long_description.id: Kuramitsuha adalah dewa Jepang yang lahir ketika Izanagi membunuh Kagutsuchi. Kojiki menyebut darah gagang pedang menghasilkan Kuramitsuha bersama Kuraokami. Namanya ditafsirkan melalui lembah gelap dan air yang muncul.
long_description.en: Kuramitsuha is a Japanese deity born when Izanagi slays Kagutsuchi. The Kojiki has blood from the sword handle produce Kuramitsuha with Kuraokami. The name is interpreted through a dark valley and water emerging.

long_description.id: Pemujaan menghubungkan dewa itu dengan hujan, irigasi, dan sumur. Terjemahan universitas menyebut Kuraokami yang disusul Kuramitsuha. Terjemahan itu menghitung Kuramitsuha di antara delapan dewa yang lahir dari pedang.
long_description.en: Worship connects the deity with rain, irrigation and wells. The university translation names Kuraokami followed by Kuramitsuha. It counts Kuramitsuha among eight deities born from the sword.

claims.quote: 日本神話では、神産みにおいて、伊邪那岐命が火之迦具土神を斬り殺した際に生まれたとしている。

statement.id: Kuramitsuha adalah dewa Jepang yang lahir ketika Izanagi membunuh Kagutsuchi.
statement.en: Kuramitsuha is a Japanese deity born when Izanagi slays Kagutsuchi.

claims.quote: 『古事記』及び『日本書紀』の一書では、迦具土神を斬った御刀の柄に溜まった血が、指の間から漏れ出て、闇淤加美神（くらおかみのかみ）とともに闇御津羽神が生まれ、『日本書紀』の一書では軻遇突智命を斬って生じた三柱の神のうちの一柱が高龗神（たかおかみのかみ）であるとしている。

statement.id: Namanya ditafsirkan melalui lembah gelap dan air yang muncul.
statement.en: The name is interpreted through a dark valley and water emerging.

statement.en: Worship connects the deity with rain, irrigation and wells.

claims.quote: The deity that thereupon came into existence was named Kura okami no kami 闇淤加美 神. Next [appeared] Kura mitsuha no kami 闇御津羽神 (8).

statement.en: It counts Kuramitsuha among eight deities born from the sword.

short_description.id: Kuraokami adalah dewa air dalam mitologi Jepang.
short_description.en: Kuraokami is a water deity in Japanese mythology.

long_description.id: Kuraokami adalah dewa air dalam mitologi Jepang. Ia dipuja untuk hujan, penghentian hujan, serta pengairan. Kojiki menurunkannya dari darah yang mengalir dari pedang Izanagi setelah kematian Kagutsuchi.
long_description.en: Kuraokami is a water deity in Japanese mythology. He is worshiped for rain, stopping rain and irrigation. The Kojiki derives him from blood running off Izanagi’s sword after Kagutsuchi’s death.

short_description.id: Kutkh adalah roh Gagak yang dihormati berbagai masyarakat adat Timur Jauh Rusia, tokoh penciptaan, leluhur manusia, dukun sakti, sekaligus penipu.
short_description.en: Kutkh is a Raven spirit revered by various indigenous peoples of the Russian Far East, a creation figure, ancestor of mankind, mighty shaman and trickster.

long_description.id: Kutkh, juga Kutkha atau Kutq, adalah roh Gagak yang secara tradisional dihormati dalam berbagai bentuk oleh masyarakat adat Timur Jauh Rusia. Ia muncul dalam banyak legenda sebagai tokoh kunci penciptaan, leluhur manusia yang subur, dukun sakti, dan penipu. Ia tokoh populer dalam cerita orang Chukchi dan berperan sentral dalam mitologi orang Koryak dan Itelmen di Kamchatka.
long_description.en: Kutkh, also Kutkha or Kutq, is a Raven spirit honoured in various guises by the native peoples of the Russian Far East. Legends cast him as a key creator figure, a fertile forefather of humankind, a powerful shaman and a trickster. He is a favourite of Chukchi tales and central to the myths of the Koryaks and Itelmens of Kamchatka.

long_description.id: Di kalangan Chukchi ia disebut Kúrkil, di kalangan Itelmen Kutq, dan dalam bahasa Koryak namanya sering dipakai dalam bentuk pembesar seperti KutqÍnnaku, "Kutkh Besar", yang sering diterjemahkan "Tuhan". Kisah-kisahnya beragam dan sering bertentangan: dalam sebagian ia diciptakan oleh Sang Pencipta dan membawa fajar ke bumi, dalam kisah lain ia menciptakan dirinya sendiri. Banyak kisahnya mirip cerita Gagak masyarakat adat Pantai Barat Laut Pasifik, yang menunjukkan kontak budaya tak langsung yang panjang antara Asia dan Amerika Utara.
long_description.en: The Chukchi call him Kúrkil, the Itelmens Kutq, and in Koryak the name is often used in an augmentative form such as KutqÍnnaku, "Big Kutkh", often translated "God". His tales come in many, often contradictory versions: in some a Creator makes him and he lets dawn onto the earth, in others he creates himself. Many resemble Raven stories of the Pacific Northwest Coast peoples, suggesting long indirect cultural contact between Asia and North America.

short_description.id: Latis adalah nama dua dewa Kelt yang dipuja di Britania Romawi, seorang dewi (Dea Latis) dan seorang dewa (Deus Latis), masing-masing hanya dikenal dari satu prasasti di Cumbria.
short_description.en: Latis is the name of two Celtic deities of Roman Britain, a goddess (Dea Latis) and a god (Deus Latis), each known from a single inscription in Cumbria.

long_description.id: Dalam politeisme Kelt (Celtic) kuno, Latis adalah nama dua dewa yang dipuja di Britania Romawi (Roman Britain): seorang dewi (Dea Latis) dan seorang dewa (Deus Latis), masing-masing hanya dikenal dari satu prasasti. Persembahan untuk Dea Latis ditemukan di benteng Romawi Birdoswald di Cumbria, Inggris (England), pada 1873, berbunyi "DIE LATI" ("untuk dewi Latis"), dan batunya kini di Carlisle Museum; ia mungkin dikaitkan dengan sungai-sungai di dekatnya.
long_description.en: In ancient Celtic polytheism Latis is the name of two deities worshipped in Roman Britain: a goddess (Dea Latis) and a god (Deus Latis), each known from a single inscription. Dea Latis's dedication turned up in 1873 at the Roman fort of Birdoswald in Cumbria, England; it reads 'DIE LATI' ('for the goddess Latis'), and the stone is now in Carlisle Museum; she may have been linked with the nearby rivers.

long_description.id: Persembahan untuk Deus Latis ditemukan pada batu altar di benteng Romawi Aballava, Burgh-by-Sands (juga di Cumbria), berbunyi "DEO LATI LVCIVS VRSEI", dan ditemukan dekat gambar dewa bertanduk serta persembahan lain untuk dewa Belatucadros. Nama Latis mungkin berhubungan dengan kata Proto-Kelt *lati- "minuman keras", *lat- "hari", atau *lāto- "nafsu". Menurut artikel fr, Latis dikenal sebagai dewi air dan bir, dan nama kota benteng Latiscum dekat Vix di Burgundy utara mungkin merujuk salah satu dewa ini.
long_description.en: An altar-stone for Deus Latis, from Aballava fort at Burgh-by-Sands, likewise in Cumbria, bears the words 'DEO LATI LVCIVS VRSEI' and lay close to a carving of a horned god and to a second altar, dedicated to Belatucadros. The name Latis may relate to Proto-Celtic *lati- 'liquor', *lat- 'day' or *lāto- 'lust'. According to the fr article Latis is known as a goddess of water and beer, and the name of the hill-fort town Latiscum near Vix in northern Burgundy may refer to one of these deities.

short_description.en: Lazy Laurence is a pixie and nature spirit of English folklore in the New Forest, a guardian of orchards and cider who makes people lazy, drowsy or sick to the stomach.

long_description.id: Lazy Laurence adalah pixie dan roh alam dalam cerita rakyat Inggris yang mendiami kawasan New Forest di Hampshire dan Dorset. Ia dikaitkan dengan perlindungan kebun buah dan sari apel, dan dikenal membuat orang tertidur di bawah pohon buah, menjadi malas dan ragu-ragu, atau terkena kram perut. Pencuri apel dan wisatawan yang tidak sopan konon dibuatnya sakit perut.
long_description.en: Lazy Laurence is a pixie and nature spirit of English folklore who lives in the New Forest area of Hampshire and Dorset. He is linked with protecting orchards and cider, and is known for sending people to sleep beneath fruit trees, making them lazy and dithering, or giving them stomach cramps. Apple scrumpers and rude tourists are said to get indigestion from him.

long_description.id: John Wise menulis bahwa di Forest masih tinggal para peri, dan makhluk jahil Laurence masih memikat orang sehingga mereka bermalas-malasan. Orang yang malas disebut dengan peribahasa "Laurence has got upon him", dan sejumlah barrow dinamai menurut namanya. Gundukan yang dipercaya menjadi rumahnya, Laurence's Barrow, terletak di Beaulieu Heath dekat barrow lain yang juga dikaitkan dengan pixie.
long_description.en: John Wise wrote that fairies still lived in the Forest and that the mischievous sprite Laurence still held men under his spell and made them idle. A lazy person was described with the proverb "Laurence has got upon him", and barrows were named after him. The mound believed to be his home, Laurence's Barrow, lies on Beaulieu Heath near other barrows also linked with pixies.

long_description.id: Laurence dulu juga dikenal di Sussex dan Somerset sebagai momok penakut anak, serta dalam dialek Devon dan Cornwall yang menekankan kemalasannya. Rujukan sastra awalnya adalah pamflet tahun 1770-an berjudul "The Pleasant history of lazy Laurence". Brewer's Dictionary of Phrase and Fable mencatat dua dugaan asal nama: panas di sekitar hari raya St Lawrence, atau lelucon tentang kemalasan sang martir di atas panggangan.
long_description.en: Laurence was once also known in Sussex and Somerset as a bogeyman to scare children, and in the dialects of Devon and Cornwall, which stressed his laziness. An early literary reference is a 1770s pamphlet titled "The Pleasant history of lazy Laurence". Brewer's Dictionary of Phrase and Fable records two conjectures about the name: the heat around the feast of St Lawrence, or a joke about the martyr's laziness on his gridiron.

cultural_context.id: Namanya menjadi peribahasa untuk orang malas: "Laurence has got upon him".
cultural_context.en: His name became a proverb for a lazy person: "Laurence has got upon him".

short_description.id: Lir atau Ler ("laut" dalam bahasa Irlandia Kuno) adalah dewa laut mitologi Irlandia, personifikasi laut, ayah Manannán mac Lir, dan raja dalam kisah The Children of Lir.
short_description.en: Lir or Ler ('sea' in Old Irish) is a sea god of Irish mythology, a personification of the sea, father of Manannán mac Lir and king in the tale The Children of Lir.

long_description.id: Lir atau Ler ("laut" dalam Old Irish; Ler bentuk nominatif dan Lir bentuk genitif) adalah dewa laut dalam mitologi Irlandia (Irish mythology). Namanya menunjukkan bahwa ia lebih merupakan personifikasi laut daripada dewa yang berdiri sendiri. Dalam silsilah awal ia bernama Allód, dan ia sepadan dengan Llŷr dalam mitologi Wales. Lir terutama tokoh leluhur, ayah dewa Manannán mac Lir yang sering muncul dalam sastra Irlandia abad pertengahan; dalam mitos Gaelik putranya tampaknya mengambil alih kedudukannya.
long_description.en: Lir or Ler ('sea' in Old Irish; Ler is the nominative and Lir the genitive) is a sea god of Irish mythology. His name suggests he is a personification of the sea rather than a separate deity. In early genealogies he is called Allód, and he matches Llŷr of Welsh mythology. Lir is chiefly an ancestor figure, father of the god Manannán mac Lir who appears often in medieval Irish literature; in Gaelic myth his son seems to take over his position.

long_description.id: Lir adalah tokoh utama kisah The Children of Lir, walau tidak pasti apakah ia sama dengan ayah Manannán. Dalam kisah itu Lir menjadi saingan Bodb Dearg memperebutkan takhta Tuatha Dé Danann; untuk menenangkannya, Bodb menikahkannya dengan putrinya Aeb, yang melahirkan Fionnuala, Aed, serta si kembar Fiachra dan Conn. Menurut artikel de, setelah Aobh meninggal Lir menikahi saudarinya Aoife, yang karena cemburu mengubah anak-anak itu menjadi angsa; mereka harus mengembara 900 tahun sebelum kembali berwujud manusia.
long_description.en: Lir is the central figure of The Children of Lir, though it is unclear whether he is the same as Manannán's father. In that tale Lir is Bodb Dearg's rival for the kingship of the Tuatha Dé Danann; to appease him Bodb gives him his daughter Aeb, who bears Fionnuala, Aed and the twins Fiachra and Conn. According to the de article, after Aobh dies Lir marries her sister Aoife, who out of jealousy turns the children into swans; they must wander for 900 years before regaining human shape.

short_description.id: Lludd Llaw Eraint ("Lludd of the Silver Hand"), putra Beli Mawr, adalah pahlawan legenda mitologi Wales, raja Britania dalam kisah Lludd and Llefelys.
short_description.en: Son of Beli Mawr and called Lludd of the Silver Hand, this Welsh legendary hero is king of Britain in the tale of Lludd and Llefelys.

long_description.id: Lludd Llaw Ereint ("Lludd of the Silver Hand", Lludd bertangan perak), putra Beli Mawr, adalah pahlawan legenda dari mitologi Wales (Welsh). Sebagai Nudd Llaw Ereint, bentuk lebih tua namanya yang sekerabat dengan Nuada Airgetlám dari Irlandia (Irish) dan berasal dari dewa Kelt (Celtic) pra-Romawi Nodens, ia ayah Gwyn ap Nudd. Ia kemungkinan sumber raja Lud dalam History of the Kings of Britain karya Geoffrey of Monmouth. Dalam kisah Mabinogion Lludd and Llefelys, ia penguasa Britania (Britain) sementara saudaranya Llefelys memerintah Galia (Gaul), dan Lludd meminta Llefelys membebaskan Britania dari tiga wabah.
long_description.en: A legendary hero of Welsh myth, Lludd Llaw Ereint, 'of the Silver Hand', was a son of Beli Mawr. As Nudd Llaw Ereint, the older form of his name, akin to the Irish Nuada Airgetlám and rooted in the pre-Roman Celtic god Nodens, he is Gwyn ap Nudd's father. King Lud, as told by Geoffrey of Monmouth in his History of the Kings of Britain, probably derives from him. In the Mabinogion tale of Lludd and Llefelys he rules Britain while his brother Llefelys rules Gaul, and Lludd asks Llefelys to rid Britain of three plagues.

long_description.id: Wabah pertama adalah Coranians, bangsa kerdil "dari Asia" yang mungkin mewakili bangsa Romawi. Wabah kedua adalah naga putih dan naga merah, yang mewakili bangsa Briton dan penyerbu Anglo-Saxon; pada malam May Day keduanya bertarung dan jeritan naga merah membuat negeri mandul. Wabah itu diatasi dengan menangkap kedua naga di Oxford, pusat pulau itu, dan menguburkan mereka di lubang batu di Dinas Emrys, Snowdonia. Menurut artikel de, Lludd dianggap pendiri legendaris London (Caer Lludd, Llundain), dan putrinya Creiddylad menjadi teladan bagi Cordelia karya Shakespeare.
long_description.en: The first plague was the Coranians, a race of dwarfs 'from Asia' who may stand for the Romans. The second was the white and red dragons, standing for the Brythons and the Anglo-Saxon invaders; on May Day eve they fought and the red dragon's scream left the land barren. The plague ended when both dragons were caught at Oxford, the island's centre, and buried in a rock pit at Dinas Emrys in Snowdonia. According to the de article Lludd is held to be the legendary founder of London (Caer Lludd, Llundain), and his daughter Creiddylad was the model for Shakespeare's Cordelia.

Kisah menyebut ia tenggelam di Sungai Luo dan menjadi roh sungai tersebut. Museum Allen menjelaskan puisi Cao Zhi sebagai pertemuan cinta yang tidak tercapai dengan dewi sungai.
long_description.en: Traditions identify her with several different historical figures. One version calls her Fufei, Fuxi's daughter, while another identifies her as Fuxi's consort. The tale says she drowns in the Luo River and becomes its spirit. The Allen Museum explains Cao Zhi’s poem as a star-crossed encounter with a beautiful river goddess.

short_description.id: Maahes adalah dewa perang berkepala singa dalam agama Mesir.
short_description.en: Maahes is a lion-headed war god in Egyptian religion.

long_description.id: Maahes adalah dewa perang berkepala singa dalam agama Mesir. Gelarnya mencakup Penguasa Pembantaian dan Pemegang Pisau.
long_description.en: Maahes is a lion-headed war god in Egyptian religion. His titles include Lord of Slaughter and Wielder of the Knife.

long_description.id: Rujukan tertua yang dicatat artikel berasal dari Kerajaan Baru. Ia dianggap putra Ra dengan Bastet atau Sekhmet. Ia digambarkan memegang pisau dan bunga teratai. Orang Yunani menghubungkan Maahes dengan Furies karena watak pembalasannya.
long_description.en: The earliest reference cited by the article dates to the New Kingdom. He is regarded as a son of Ra with Bastet or Sekhmet. He is shown holding a knife and lotus flowers. The Greeks associate Maahes with the Furies because of his vengeful nature.

sources.title: Egyptian Gods - The Complete List - World History Encyclopedia

claims.quote: was an ancient Egyptian lion-headed god of war

statement.id: Maahes adalah dewa perang berkepala singa dalam agama Mesir.
statement.en: Maahes is a lion-headed war god in Egyptian religion.

claims.quote: The name of Maahes begins with the hieroglyphs for the male lion, although in isolation it also means (one who can) see in front. Some of the titles of Maahes were Lord of Slaughter, Wielder of the Knife, and The Scarlet Lord.

statement.id: Gelarnya mencakup Penguasa Pembantaian dan Pemegang Pisau.
statement.en: His titles include Lord of Slaughter and Wielder of the Knife.

claims.quote: The first recorded reference to Maahes is from the New Kingdom. Some Egyptologists have suggested that Maahes was of foreign origin; indeed there is some evidence that he may have been identical with the lion-god Apedemak worshipped in Nubia and Egypt's Western Desert.

statement.id: Rujukan tertua yang dicatat artikel berasal dari Kerajaan Baru.
statement.en: The earliest reference cited by the article dates to the New Kingdom.

claims.quote: Maahes was considered the son of Ra with the feline goddess Bastet, or of another feline goddess, Sekhmet. He was sometimes identified with another son of Sekhmet, Nefertum. Maahes was said to fight Ra's archenemy, the serpent Apep, during Ra's nightly voyage.

statement.id: Ia dianggap putra Ra dengan Bastet atau Sekhmet.
statement.en: He is regarded as a son of Ra with Bastet or Sekhmet.

claims.quote: Maahes was pictured as a man with the head of a male lion, sometimes holding a knife and a bouquet of lotus flowers, referring to his connection with Nefertum, who was symbolized by the lotus.

statement.id: Ia digambarkan memegang pisau dan bunga teratai.
statement.en: He is shown holding a knife and lotus flowers.

claims.quote: Linked by the Greeks with the Furies because of his vengeful nature.

statement.id: Orang Yunani menghubungkan Maahes dengan Furies karena watak pembalasannya.
statement.en: The Greeks associate Maahes with the Furies because of his vengeful nature.

short_description.id: Macrâle adalah penyihir perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Wallonia, Flandria, dan Ardennes, yang dituduh mendatangkan musim dingin, banjir, dan wabah.
short_description.en: The macrâle is a witch of the folklore of Wallonia, Flanders and the Ardennes, blamed for bringing winter, floods and epidemics.

long_description.id: Macrâle, dari kata Walloon Liège dan Luxembourg untuk penyihir perempuan, adalah sosok penyihir dalam cerita rakyat Wallonia, Flandria, dan Ardennes. Menurut Pierre Dubois ia campuran elf dan penyihir yang menyukai sabat dan berkeliling pada malam hari menebar kutukan. Ia dituduh mendatangkan musim dingin, banjir, dan wabah, dan menghuni hutan seperti nuton dan sottai.
long_description.en: The macrâle, from a Liège and Luxembourg Walloon word for a witch, is a witch figure of the folklore of Wallonia, Flanders and the Ardennes. Pierre Dubois calls her a mix of elf and witch who loves sabbaths and goes about at night spreading curses. She is blamed for bringing winter, floods and epidemics, and dwells in the forests like the nutons and sottai.

long_description.id: Kini banyak kelompok folklor memerankan macrâle dalam sabat dan pawai, misalnya di Haccourt, Vielsalm, dan Ellezelles. Kelompok Macralles du val de Salm di Vielsalm didirikan pada 1955 untuk mengenang legenda tokoh nyata Gustine Maka.
long_description.en: Today many folklore groups play macrâles in sabbaths and parades, for example at Haccourt, Vielsalm and Ellezelles. The Macralles du val de Salm group at Vielsalm was set up in 1955 to recall a legend about the real Gustine Maka.

who.en: A folklore witch.

role.en: Blamed for disasters.

famous_for.id: Sabat kelompok folklor macrâle.
famous_for.en: The sabbaths of macrâle folklore groups.

description.id: Tempat kelompok folklor Macralles du val de Salm, didirikan 1955.
description.en: Home of the Macralles du val de Salm folklore group, founded in 1955.

claims.quote: La macrâle, makrâlle, macralle, macrale (ou makralle en flamand) désigne une sorcière en Wallonie, en Flandre et dans les Ardennes.

statement.id: Macrâle (juga makrâlle, macralle, macrale, atau makralle dalam bahasa Flam) adalah sebutan untuk penyihir perempuan di Wallonia, Flandria, dan Ardennes.
statement.en: The macrâle (also makrâlle, macralle, macrale, or makralle in Flemish) is the name for a witch in Wallonia, Flanders and the Ardennes.

claims.quote: Le terme macrâle provient du wallon liégeois et luxembourgeois et a comme masculin le terme macrê qui quant à lui signifie sorcier.

statement.id: Istilah macrâle berasal dari bahasa Walloon Liège dan Luxembourg; bentuk maskulinnya, macrê, berarti penyihir laki-laki.
statement.en: The term macrâle comes from the Walloon of Liège and Luxembourg; its masculine form, macrê, means a male sorcerer.

claims.quote: Selon Pierre Dubois, la macrâle est un mélange d'elfe et de sorcière qui affectionne les sabbats, et se promène durant la nuit en lançant un florilège de maléfices.

statement.id: Menurut Pierre Dubois, macrâle adalah campuran elf dan penyihir yang menyukai sabat dan berkeliaran pada malam hari sambil melontarkan berbagai kutukan.
statement.en: According to Pierre Dubois, the macrâle is a mix of elf and witch who loves sabbaths and roams at night casting a host of curses.

claims.quote: La macrâle est accusée d'être responsable de bien des maux, tels que la venue de l'hiver, des inondations et des épidémies. Elles peuplent les forêts comme d'autres créatures du folklore belge et ardennais (nutons, sottai, Bayard).

statement.id: Macrâle dituduh menyebabkan banyak bencana seperti datangnya musim dingin, banjir, dan wabah; mereka menghuni hutan seperti makhluk lain dalam cerita rakyat Belgia dan Ardennes (nuton, sottai, Bayard).
statement.en: The macrâle is blamed for many ills such as the coming of winter, floods and epidemics; they people the forests like other creatures of Belgian and Ardennes folklore (nutons, sottai, Bayard).

claims.quote: De nombreux groupes folkloriques représentent des macrales et sorcières, notamment dans les sabbats de Haccourt, Vielsalm, Ellezelles (où elles sont appelées "chorchîles")

statement.id: Banyak kelompok folklor memerankan macrâle dan penyihir, antara lain dalam sabat di Haccourt, Vielsalm, dan Ellezelles (tempat mereka disebut chorchîles).
statement.en: Many folklore groups portray macrâles and witches, notably in the sabbaths of Haccourt, Vielsalm and Ellezelles (where they are called chorchîles).

claims.quote: Les Macralles du val de Salm (ou de Vielsam) est un groupe folklorique fondé en 1955 et qui a été créé en l'honneur d'une légende locale, autour de la personnalité bien réelle de Marie-Joseph-Augustine Lemoine dite Gustine Maka.

statement.id: Kelompok folklor Macralles du val de Salm di Vielsalm didirikan pada 1955 untuk menghormati legenda setempat tentang tokoh nyata Marie-Joseph-Augustine Lemoine, yang dijuluki Gustine Maka.
statement.en: The folklore group Macralles du val de Salm at Vielsalm was founded in 1955 in honour of a local legend about the real person Marie-Joseph-Augustine Lemoine, called Gustine Maka.

claims.quote: De makrallen in het Vlaams, les macrâles, macralles ou makrâlles in het Waals, komt van een Luiks-Waals woord voor heks.

statement.id: Artikel bahasa Belanda juga menyebut makrallen (Flam) atau macrâles (Walloon) berasal dari kata Walloon Liège untuk penyihir perempuan.
statement.en: The Dutch article likewise says makrallen (Flemish) or macrâles (Walloon) comes from a Liège Walloon word for witch.

short_description.id: Mama 'e su Sole adalah perempuan cantik dalam cerita rakyat Sardinia yang muncul pada siang terpanas musim panas dan membuat anak yang bermain di luar terserang demam.
short_description.en: Mama 'e su Sole is a beautiful woman of Sardinian folklore who appears in the hottest summer afternoons and gives fever to children playing outdoors.

long_description.id: Mama 'e su Sole, "Ibu Matahari", dikenal hampir di seluruh Sardinia. Ia perempuan sangat cantik yang muncul pada musim panas dari tengah hari sampai sekitar pukul 16. Bila bertemu anak yang bermain di jalan tanpa izin orang tuanya, ia mengejarnya, menyentuh dahinya hingga berbekas, dan anak itu terserang demam halentura beberapa hari.
long_description.en: Mama 'e su Sole, 'Mother of the Sun', is known almost all over Sardinia. She is a very beautiful woman who appears in summer from noon until about 16:00. If she meets a child playing in the street without its parents' leave, she runs it down, marks its brow with a touch, and the child falls ill with halentura fever for days.

long_description.id: Ia dipakai untuk menakuti anak agar tidak keluar saat terik dan juga menjelaskan demam akibat sengatan matahari, mirip uomo nero atau gatto mammone. Di beberapa desa ia punya saudari musim dingin, sa Mama 'e su Frittu, serta sosok sejenis untuk api dan angin.
long_description.en: She was used to keep children indoors in the heat and also explained fever from sunstroke, much like the uomo nero or gatto mammone. Some villages give her a winter sister, sa Mama 'e su Frittu, and similar figures for fire and wind.

who.en: A beautiful bogey woman.

role.en: Keeps children out of the midday sun.

note.en: Her sister and winter counterpart.
A similar bogey figure.

claims.quote: Mama 'e su Sole è una creatura tipica del folklore sardo, nata per mettere in guardia i bambini dal rischio di restare al sole nelle ore più calde della giornata.

statement.id: Mama 'e su Sole adalah makhluk khas cerita rakyat Sardinia yang muncul untuk memperingatkan anak-anak akan bahaya berada di bawah matahari pada jam-jam terpanas.
statement.en: Mama 'e su Sole is a creature typical of Sardinian folklore, born to warn children against staying in the sun in the hottest hours of the day.

claims.quote: Concettualmente è simile all'uomo nero o al gatto mammone.

statement.id: Secara konsep ia mirip uomo nero atau gatto mammone.
statement.en: Conceptually it resembles the uomo nero or the gatto mammone.

claims.quote: (la Madre del Sole) è identificata con una donna bellissima che appare d'estate, dopo mezzogiorno fino circa alle 16 del pomeriggio (le ore più calde della giornata).

statement.id: Sa Mama 'e su Sole (Ibu Matahari) diidentikkan dengan perempuan sangat cantik yang muncul pada musim panas, dari tengah hari sampai sekitar pukul 16, jam-jam terpanas.
statement.en: Sa Mama 'e su Sole (the Mother of the Sun) is identified with a very beautiful woman who appears in summer from noon until about 16:00, the hottest hours.

claims.quote: La leggenda dice che se la Mama 'e su Sole incontra un bambino per strada a giocare, disubbidendo ai genitori, lo rincorreva fino a raggiungerlo, gli tocca la fronte lasciandogli un segno e subito il bambino viene assalito da una febbre (halentura), che dura alcuni giorni.

statement.id: Menurut legenda, bila ia menemukan anak yang bermain di jalan karena tidak menuruti orang tuanya, ia mengejarnya, menyentuh dahinya hingga meninggalkan tanda, dan anak itu segera terserang demam (halentura) selama beberapa hari.
statement.en: The legend says that if she meets a child playing in the street against its parents' wishes, she chases it down, touches its forehead leaving a mark, and the child is at once seized by a fever (halentura) lasting some days.

claims.quote: Venne creato questo personaggio, anche per spiegare il fenomeno della febbre, dovuta in seguito a una prolungata esposizione al sole in un periodo di forte canicola.

statement.id: Tokoh ini juga diciptakan untuk menjelaskan demam akibat terlalu lama terpapar matahari pada masa panas terik.
statement.en: The figure was also created to explain fever caused by long exposure to the sun during a heatwave.

claims.quote: si narra che esistesse anche sa Mama 'e su Frittu [pron. sa Mamma 'e su Vrittu] (la Madre del Freddo), sua sorella e controparte invernale.

statement.id: Di beberapa desa Sardinia diceritakan pula adanya sa Mama 'e su Frittu (Ibu Dingin), saudarinya dan padanannya pada musim dingin.
statement.en: In some Sardinian villages there is said also to be sa Mama 'e su Frittu (the Mother of the Cold), her sister and winter counterpart.

claims.quote: Poi c'erano sa Mama 'e su Fogu [pron. sa Mamma 'e su Vógu] (la Madre del Fuoco), per spiegare ai bimbi il fenomeno degli incendi, e sa Mama 'e su Ventu [pron. sa Mamma 'e su Ventu] (la Madre del Vento), la quale appariva quando soffiavano il forte Maestrale o la Tramontana.

statement.id: Ada pula sa Mama 'e su Fogu (Ibu Api) untuk menjelaskan kebakaran kepada anak-anak, dan sa Mama 'e su Ventu (Ibu Angin) yang muncul saat angin Maestrale atau Tramontana bertiup kencang.
statement.en: There were also sa Mama 'e su Fogu (the Mother of Fire), to explain fires to children, and sa Mama 'e su Ventu (the Mother of the Wind), who appeared when the strong Maestrale or Tramontana blew.

claims.quote: Custa paristoria fit connotta in cada bidda peri tottu sa Sardigna.

statement.id: Artikel bahasa Sardinia menyebut kisah ini dikenal di setiap desa di seluruh Sardinia.
statement.en: The Sardinian-language article says this tale was known in every village throughout Sardinia.

short_description.id: Manasa adalah dewi ular dalam Hindu.
short_description.en: Manasa is a Hindu snake goddess.

long_description.id: Manasa adalah dewi ular dalam Hindu. Ia dipuja untuk mencegah dan menyembuhkan gigitan ular serta memohon kesuburan dan kemakmuran.
long_description.en: Manasa is a Hindu snake goddess. She is worshipped for preventing and curing snakebite and for fertility and prosperity.

long_description.id: Teks Hindu menyebutnya saudari Vasuki dan istri resi Jaratkaru. Astika disebut sebagai putranya. Versi Purana menyebut Manasa sebagai putri Kashyapa yang lahir dari pikiran. Koleksi Cleveland mencatat lukisan Manasa dewi ular dari Kalighat di Kolkata sekitar 1890.
long_description.en: Hindu texts call her Vasuki's sister and sage Jaratkaru's wife. Astika is called her son. The Puranic version calls Manasa Kashyapa's mind born daughter. The Cleveland collection records a Manasa snake goddess painting from Kalighat in Kolkata around 1890.

note.en: Manasa's brother in the texts.

short_description.id: Manat adalah dewi Arab pra-Islam yang dipuja di Jazirah Arab.
short_description.en: Manat is a pre-Islamic Arabian goddess worshipped on the Arabian Peninsula.

long_description.id: Manat adalah dewi Arab pra-Islam yang dipuja di Jazirah Arab. Manat dihubungkan dengan nasib, keberuntungan, waktu, dan takdir.
long_description.en: Manat is a pre-Islamic Arabian goddess worshipped on the Arabian Peninsula. Manat is associated with fate, fortune, time, and destiny.

long_description.id: Kuil utama Manat yang telah hilang berada di antara Mekah dan Madinah di pesisir Laut Merah. Aws dan Khazraj termasuk suku yang sangat memuja Manat. Para peziarah yang dibahas menganggap perjalanan belum lengkap tanpa mengunjungi arca Manat. Al-Qur’an 53:20 menyebut Manat sebagai dewi ketiga dalam rangkaian tersebut.
long_description.en: Manat’s lost main shrine stood between Mecca and Medina on the Red Sea coast. The Aws and Khazraj are among Manat’s devoted worshippers. The pilgrims described regard visiting Manat’s idol as necessary to complete their pilgrimage. Quran 53:20 mentions Manat as the third deity in that sequence.

short_description.id: Manibhadra adalah salah satu yaksha utama dan dewa populer di India kuno.
short_description.en: Manibhadra is a major yaksha and a popular deity in ancient India.

long_description.id: Manibhadra adalah salah satu yaksha utama dan dewa populer di India kuno. Nama Manibhadra diterangkan berarti seunggul permata.
long_description.en: Manibhadra is a major yaksha and a popular deity in ancient India. The name Manibhadra is explained as excellent as a jewel.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah Buddha, ia dikatakan menghuni Manimalachaitya di Magadha. Sastra Jain menyebutnya pemimpin yaksha utara, sementara Purnabhadra memimpin selatan. Di kalangan Jain Gujarat ia dipuja dengan tunggangan Airavata, gajah bergading banyak. Mackenzie mencatat Manibhadra dipuja oleh para pelancong dan menyerupai dewa kekayaan Kuvera.
long_description.en: In Buddhist accounts he is said to dwell at Manimalachaitya in Magadha. Jain literature calls him leader of northern yakshas while Purnabhadra leads the south. Among Gujarat Jains he is worshipped with Airavata, a multi tusked elephant mount. Mackenzie records Manibhadra being worshipped by travelers and resembling Kuvera, the god of wealth.

note.en: A comparison in Mackenzie's retelling.

short_description.id: Margot la fée adalah nama umum peri bumi Bretagne dan Mayenne, kemungkinan turunan Morgana, yang dapat menghilang, berubah wujud, menguji manusia dengan emas, dan menculik anak.
short_description.en: Margot the fairy is the generic name of the earthly fairies of Brittany and the Mayenne, probably descended from Morgana, who can vanish, shapeshift, test humans with gold and steal children.

long_description.id: Margot la fée adalah nama umum peri bumi dalam tradisi Bretagne dan Mayenne, paling dikenal di Côtes-d'Armor. Mereka kemungkinan berasal dari Morgana dan sebelumnya dari Ibu Bumi; namanya pun mungkin pelesetan Morgana. Mereka dapat menghilang, berubah wujud, dan mengubah orang lain, menari dengan indah, menyimpan harta di bawah tanah, dan dipercaya membangun monumen.
long_description.en: Margot the fairy is the generic name of the earthly fairies of Brittany and the Mayenne, best known in the Côtes-d'Armor. They probably descend from Morgana and before her from Mother Earth; even the name may distort Morgana's. They can vanish, shapeshift and transform others, dance beautifully, hoard treasure underground and are thought to have built monuments.

long_description.id: Mereka menguji manusia dengan emas, memberi hadiah kepada orang benar, menghukum yang serakah, menculik anak dan menggantinya, serta menjadi ibu baptis bayi. Banyak megalit dianggap rumah atau perabot mereka, dan sampai akhir abad ke-19 orang mempersembahkan hewan kepada mereka, terutama di gua Margot.
long_description.en: They test humans with gold, reward the just, punish the greedy, steal children and leave changelings, and stand godmother to babies. Many megaliths are thought to be their homes or furniture, and until the end of the 19th century people sacrificed animals to them, especially at the Margot cave.

literal_meaning.en: a distortion of the fairy Morgana's name

who.en: Earthly fairies of Brittany.

role.en: Test humans with gifts.

famous_for.id: Megalit yang dianggap rumah mereka.
famous_for.en: Megaliths thought to be their homes.

description.id: Tempat pemujaan peri Margot.
description.en: A cult site of the Margot fairies.

note.id: Peri Arthur yang mungkin menjadi asal mereka.
note.en: The Arthurian fairy they may descend from.

claims.quote: Margot the fairy is, in the traditions of Brittany and the Mayenne, the generic name for certain earthly fairies. They are best known in Central Brittany, particularly in the Côtes-d'Armor.

statement.id: Margot la fée adalah nama umum untuk sejumlah peri bumi dalam tradisi Bretagne dan Mayenne, paling dikenal di Bretagne Tengah, terutama Côtes-d'Armor.
statement.en: Margot the fairy is, in the traditions of Brittany and the Mayenne, the generic name of certain earthly fairies, best known in central Brittany, especially the Côtes-d'Armor.

claims.quote: Presumably descended from the fairy Morgana and before her from an aspect of Mother Earth, the Margot fairies are quite powerful. They can make themselves invisible, metamorphose and transform others.

statement.id: Kemungkinan berasal dari peri Morgana dan sebelumnya dari satu aspek Ibu Bumi, peri Margot sangat kuat: mereka dapat menghilang, berubah wujud, dan mengubah orang lain.
statement.en: Probably descended from the fairy Morgana and, before her, from an aspect of Mother Earth, the Margot fairies are powerful: they can turn invisible, change shape and transform others.

claims.quote: Reputed to be excellent dancers, often generous and sometimes cruel, they take pleasure in testing humans by giving them gold and objects. They are believed to have built several monuments, and to possess immense treasures hidden under the earth. They have animals, often cattle.

statement.id: Mereka penari ulung, sering murah hati dan kadang kejam, senang menguji manusia dengan memberi emas dan benda, dipercaya membangun sejumlah monumen, menyimpan harta besar di bawah tanah, dan memelihara hewan, sering ternak.
statement.en: They are fine dancers, often generous and sometimes cruel, who enjoy testing humans with gifts of gold and objects, are believed to have built several monuments and to hide great treasure underground, and keep animals, often cattle.

claims.quote: Tales and myths tell of the habits of these fairies, who kidnap human children to replace them with their own and become the godmothers of babies whom they name and cover with more or less convenient gifts.

statement.id: Dongeng menceritakan mereka menculik anak manusia dan menggantinya dengan anak mereka sendiri, serta menjadi ibu baptis bayi yang mereka beri nama dan hadiah yang kadang merepotkan.
statement.en: Tales tell how they steal human children, leaving their own in their place, and become godmothers of babies whom they name and endow with more or less useful gifts.

claims.quote: They reward the righteous and punish those who harm them, are greedy or indiscreet towards them. They sometimes show themselves to be thieves.

statement.id: Mereka memberi hadiah kepada orang benar dan menghukum yang menyakiti, serakah, atau lancang terhadap mereka, dan kadang mencuri.
statement.en: They reward the righteous and punish those who harm them or are greedy or indiscreet with them, and sometimes steal.

claims.quote: De nombreux mégalithes et rochers seraient les demeures de ces fées, ou bien leurs meubles et leurs outils : table, fuseau, chambre, sabot, fauteuil, berceau…

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, banyak megalit dan batu besar dianggap rumah peri-peri ini atau perabot dan perkakas mereka: meja, alat pintal, kamar, sabot, kursi, dan buaian.
statement.en: According to the French article, many megaliths and rocks are said to be these fairies' homes or their furniture and tools: table, spindle, room, clog, armchair, cradle.

claims.quote: They were the object of cults and beliefs, in particular at the Margot cave. These beliefs, until the end of the 19th century, led many people to offer them animals in sacrifice and to search for their supposed treasures.

statement.id: Mereka menjadi sasaran pemujaan, terutama di gua Margot; sampai akhir abad ke-19 kepercayaan ini membuat banyak orang mempersembahkan hewan kepada mereka dan mencari harta mereka.
statement.en: They were the object of cults, especially at the Margot cave; until the end of the 19th century these beliefs led many people to sacrifice animals to them and hunt for their treasures.

claims.quote: The name probably comes from a distortion of the name of Morgana, the famous fairy of the Arthurian myth. They were originally called "Morgana" in Lower Brittany.

statement.id: Namanya mungkin pelesetan nama Morgana, peri terkenal mitos Arthur; di Bretagne Bawah mereka semula disebut Morgana.
statement.en: The name probably distorts that of Morgana, the famous fairy of Arthurian myth; in Lower Brittany they were first called Morgana.

claims.quote: Roger Sherman Loomis sees a relationship between the fairies of Upper Brittany and the "Morgain" of the Arthurian romances.

statement.id: Roger Sherman Loomis melihat hubungan antara peri Bretagne Atas dan Morgain dalam roman Arthur.
statement.en: Roger Sherman Loomis sees a link between the fairies of Upper Brittany and the Morgain of the Arthurian romances.

claims.quote: El hada Margot (en francés, Margot la fée) es, en las tradiciones de Bretaña y Mayenne, el nombre genérico de algunas hadas terrestres.

statement.id: Artikel bahasa Spanyol juga menyebut peri Margot nama umum sejumlah peri bumi dalam tradisi Bretagne dan Mayenne.
statement.en: The Spanish article also calls Margot the fairy the generic name of certain earthly fairies in the traditions of Brittany and the Mayenne.
