short_description.en: Fravashi is a powerful supernatural being whose concept blends with the urvan in early Zoroastrianism.

long_description.id: Fravashi adalah makhluk gaib kuat yang konsepnya menyatu dengan urvan atau jiwa dalam Zoroastrianisme awal. Fravashi dibayangkan sebagai kumpulan sangat besar, berjumlah ratusan hingga puluhan ribu.
long_description.en: Fravashi is a powerful supernatural being whose concept blends with the urvan in early Zoroastrianism. Fravashis are imagined as a vast host numbering hundreds, thousands, and tens of thousands.

long_description.id: Yasht menggambarkan fravashi membantu Ahura Mazda menata dunia. Fravashi dihubungkan dengan pemeliharaan air, tumbuhan, dan perlindungan anak dalam kandungan. Fravashi berusaha memperoleh air bagi keluarga, permukiman, suku, dan negeri masing-masing. Mihr Yasht menyebut fravashi kaum beriman memberikan keturunan yang berbudi.
long_description.en: Their Yasht depicts fravashis helping Ahura Mazda order the world and maintaining it. Fravashis are associated with nurturing waters and plants and protecting children in the womb. Fravashis strive to obtain water for their family, settlement, tribe, and country. The Mihr Yasht describes the faithful’s fravashis as granting virtuous offspring.

short_description.id: Guhyaka adalah golongan makhluk supernatural Hindu yang melayani Kubera dan menjaga kekayaan tersembunyinya.
short_description.en: Guhyakas are a class of Hindu supernatural beings serving Kubera and guarding his hidden wealth.

long_description.id: Guhyaka adalah golongan makhluk supernatural Hindu yang melayani Kubera dan menjaga kekayaan tersembunyinya. Nama mereka berarti yang tersembunyi, dikaitkan dengan tempat tinggal di gua gunung.
long_description.en: Guhyakas are a class of Hindu supernatural beings serving Kubera and guarding his hidden wealth. Their name means hidden ones and is associated with dwelling in mountain caves.

long_description.id: Hopkins menafsirkan mereka mungkin sebutan umum roh penyembunyian, sedangkan sebagian teks membedakannya dari yaksha. Mereka menjalankan tugas penting dan menjadi utusan Kubera. Markandeya Purana menuturkan Surya menetapkan Revanta sebagai pemimpin guhyaka. Dalam doa Yudhishthira kepada matahari, guhyaka bersama makhluk lain mengikuti kereta dewa untuk mencari anugerah.
long_description.en: Hopkins interprets them as possibly a general term for spirits of concealment while some texts distinguish them from yakshas. They carry out important tasks and act as Kubera's messengers. The Markandeya Purana recounts Surya appointing Revanta as chief of the guhyakas. In Yudhishthira's prayer to the sun guhyakas follow the deity's chariot with other beings seeking boons.

note.en: Servants guarding Kubera's wealth.

sources.title: The Mahabharata, Vana Parva, Part I

long_description.en: In the quoted commentary, Ifrit offers to bring the throne before Solomon rises. In that commentary, Ifrit asserts his strength. In that commentary, Solomon asks for something faster. The same commentary distinguishes the honest Ashif ibn Barkhiya, who offers another method, from Ifrit. short_description.id: Ksatria Angsa adalah pahlawan legendaris abad pertengahan yang datang dengan perahu ditarik angsa untuk membela seorang gadis dengan syarat namanya tak boleh ditanyakan, kisah yang kelak menjadi opera Lohengrin.
short_description.en: The Knight of the Swan is a legendary medieval hero who arrives in a swan-drawn boat to defend a damsel on condition his name is never asked, a tale that became the opera Lohengrin.

long_description.id: Ksatria Angsa adalah penyelamat misterius yang datang dengan perahu ditarik angsa untuk membela seorang gadis, dengan syarat namanya tidak boleh ditanyakan; setelah mendapat tanah dan istri, ia pergi bersama angsanya. Legenda yang tercatat sejak abad ke-12 ini berasal dari Belanda Burgundia, dan siklus Perang Salib Prancis menjadikannya leluhur Godefroy dari Bouillon.
long_description.en: The Knight of the Swan is a mysterious rescuer who arrives in a swan-drawn boat to defend a damsel on condition that his name is never asked; after winning land and a wife he leaves with his swan. Recorded from the 12th century, the legend comes from the Burgundian Netherlands, and the French Crusade cycle made him an ancestor of Godfrey of Bouillon.

long_description.id: Wolfram von Eschenbach menamainya Loherangrin dalam Parzival, Konrad von Würzburg menggubah Der Schwanritter, dan keduanya menjadi dasar opera Lohengrin karya Richard Wagner (1850). Kisah anak-anak angsa yang terkait mirip dongeng The Six Swans.
long_description.en: Wolfram von Eschenbach called him Loherangrin in Parzival, Konrad von Würzburg wrote Der Schwanritter, and both underlie Richard Wagner's opera Lohengrin (1850). The related Swan Children tale resembles The Six Swans.

statement.en: The earliest versions, in John of Alta Silva's Dolopathos, give the knight no identity, but the Old French Crusade cycle of chansons de geste made the Swan Knight (Le Chevalier au Cigne, first version c. 1192) the legendary ancestor of Godfrey of Bouillon.

claims.quote: At a later time, the German poet Wolfram von Eschenbach incorporated the swan knight Loherangrin into his Matter of Britain epic Parzival (first quarter of the 13th century).

statement.id: Kemudian penyair Jerman Wolfram von Eschenbach memasukkan ksatria angsa Loherangrin ke dalam epos Parzival pada awal abad ke-13.
statement.en: Later the German poet Wolfram von Eschenbach brought the swan knight Loherangrin into his epic Parzival in the early 13th century.

statement.en: Wolfram's and Konrad von Würzburg's texts were used for the libretto of Richard Wagner's opera Lohengrin (Weimar, 1850).

claims.quote: It also bears resemblance to the fairy tale The Six Swans, where brothers transformed into birds are rescued by the efforts of their sister.

statement.en: The related Swan Children tale resembles The Six Swans, in which brothers turned into birds are saved by their sister.

claims.quote: Die Schwanenrittersage ist eine in mehreren Varianten überlieferte mittelalterliche Sage aus den Burgundischen Niederlanden. Sie erhielt unterschiedliche Ausformungen in der Literatur (so die Verserzählung „Der Schwanritter“ von Konrad von Würzburg) und diente einigen Herrscherhäusern am Niederrhein als genealogische Ursprungssage.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, legenda Ksatria Angsa berasal dari Belanda Burgundia, digubah antara lain dalam syair Der Schwanritter karya Konrad von Würzburg, dan menjadi legenda asal-usul beberapa wangsa di Rhein Hilir.
statement.en: According to the German article, the Swan Knight legend comes from the Burgundian Netherlands, was retold in works such as Konrad von Würzburg's verse tale Der Schwanritter, and served several Lower Rhine dynasties as an origin legend.

claims.quote: Dans la version la plus condensée de l’histoire, un inconnu en armes aborde sur un rivage dans une barque remorquée par un cygne. L'inconnu fait preuve de vaillance et obtient en récompense un fief et une épouse, avec qui il a des enfants. Un jour, le cygne réapparaît : l’inconnu saute dans la barque qui est aussitôt entraînée au large par l’oiseau et disparaît comme il était venu.

statement.en: According to the French article, in the shortest version an armed stranger lands in a swan-towed boat, proves his valour, wins a fief and a wife, and one day, when the swan returns, leaps into the boat and vanishes as he came.

short_description.id: Lempo adalah iblis dalam cerita rakyat dan mitologi Finlandia yang dikaitkan dengan cinta dan api, dan kemudian disamakan dengan Iblis oleh Kekristenan.
short_description.en: Lempo is a demon of Finnish folklore and mythology linked with love and fire, later identified with the Devil by Christianity.

long_description.id: Lempo adalah iblis dalam cerita rakyat dan mitologi Finlandia. Namanya dikaitkan dengan Lemmes, Lemmas, Lemmätär, dan Lemmetär ("Nyonya Cinta"), serta dengan tema cinta dan api. Nama berakhiran -tär bersifat perempuan, tetapi Lempo kadang juga dipahami sebagai iblis laki-laki. Dalam kepercayaan kuno Finlandia ia makhluk kepercayaan atau dewa yang oleh Kekristenan disamakan dengan Iblis.
long_description.en: Finnish folklore and myth know Lempo as a demon. The name is linked to Lemmes, Lemmas, Lemmätär and Lemmetär ("Lady Love") and to the themes of love and fire. The -tär names are feminine, yet Lempo has at times been seen as a male demon. In old Finnish belief Lempo was a being or god whom Christianity equated with the Devil.

long_description.id: Christfried Ganander menyebut Lempo roh jahat yang terbang dan menempa panah-panah jahat yang terbang. Matthias Castrén mengaitkan nama itu dengan kata lempi, "cinta erotis"; dalam mantra cinta, Lempi bisa menjadi perasaan liar yang mengamuk, sehingga Castrén menduga dewa cinta dapat berubah menjadi dewa jahat. Elias Lönnrot mengaitkannya dengan kata Swedia slem, "buruk". Umpatan ringan "Lempo soikoon!" semula adalah seruan kepada Lempo.
long_description.en: In Christfried Ganander's account Lempo was an airborne spirit of evil who made wicked arrows that flew. Matthias Castrén linked the name to lempi, "erotic love"; in love spells Lempi could be a wild, raging feeling, so Castrén thought a love god could have turned into an evil one. Elias Lönnrot connected it with the Swedish slem, "lousy". The mild curse "Lempo soikoon!" was originally an appeal to Lempo.

long_description.en: Ōtakemaru is a supernatural figure in Japanese folklore. His dwelling is the Suzuka Mountains between Ise and Ōmi. His legendary opponent is Sakanoue no Tamuramaro in Kanmu’s reign.

long_description.id: Ia dikisahkan mengendalikan badai, petir, dan awan yang menghujankan api. Kisah belakangan menyebutnya kijin, sekaligus iblis dan dewa. Uraian belakangan mencatat bahwa sebagian peringkat menggantikannya dengan Sutoku Tennō.

short_description.id: Piru adalah iblis atau setan dalam mitologi Finlandia, sering tampil sebagai roh hutan jahat yang beradu akal dengan manusia.
short_description.en: A piru is a fiend or demon of Finnish mythology, often appearing as a nasty forest spirit who matches wits with people.

long_description.id: Piru adalah iblis atau setan dalam mitologi Finlandia. Kata ini diwarisi dari bahasa Proto-Finnik *piru, "setan, iblis", yang berkerabat dengan kata dalam bahasa Karelia, Ingria, dan Estonia; asal-usul akhirnya tidak diketahui. Dalam cerita rakyat, piru sering tampil sebagai roh hutan jahat yang diajak beradu akal oleh orang cerdik, dengan taruhan yang dimenangkan atau dikalahkan.
long_description.en: Finnish myth calls a fiend or demon a piru. The word goes back to Proto-Finnic *piru, "devil, demon", with relatives in Karelian, Ingrian and Estonian, though its deeper origin is unknown. Folk tales often cast the piru as a mean forest spirit whom a quick-witted person outsmarts, or loses to, in a contest with a forfeit at stake.

long_description.id: Gejala poltergeist dan rumah berhantu sering disebut ulah piru, dan Iblis sendiri dapat disebut Piru atau Pääpiru, "piru utama". Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Finlandia, piru bisa pelayan Iblis atau makhluk jahat yang lebih rendah, atau Iblis itu sendiri. Mereka dapat merasuki manusia sehingga orang itu berperilaku aneh, jatuh sakit, atau berubah kepribadian, dan rasukan itu dapat diusir oleh pengusir setan. Kini piru juga kata makian ringan dalam bahasa Finlandia.
long_description.en: Poltergeists and hauntings are often blamed on pirus, and the Devil himself may be called Piru or Pääpiru, "the chief piru". In Finnish folk belief a piru may serve the Devil, be a lesser evil being, or be the Devil himself. Pirus can possess people, making them act strangely, fall ill or change personality, and an exorcist can drive them out. Today piru is also a mild Finnish swearword.

short_description.id: Poroniec adalah iblis jahat dalam mitologi Slavia yang dipercaya muncul dari janin yang lahir mati atau jasad bayi yang tidak dikuburkan dengan benar.
short_description.en: A poroniec is a hostile demon of Slavic mythology believed to arise from a stillborn fetus or an improperly buried infant.

long_description.id: Dalam kepercayaan Slavia, poroniec (jamak porońce) adalah iblis jahat yang memusuhi manusia. Ia dipercaya lahir dari janin yang mati dalam kandungan, juga dari jasad bayi yang meninggal dan tidak dikuburkan sesuai adat. Porońce dianggap sangat kuat karena membawa potensi kehidupan yang tidak sempat terwujud.
long_description.en: Slavic belief knows the poroniec (plural porońce) as a malicious demon hostile to people. It was thought to come from stillborn fetuses and from the remains of babies who died young and were not buried by custom. Porońce were held to be very powerful because of the unlived life they carried.

long_description.id: Kepercayaan ini melahirkan banyak pantangan bagi perempuan hamil dan yang baru melahirkan, seperti menimba air dari sumur, membawa bayi keluar rumah, atau berhubungan badan. Janin yang dikuburkan di bawah ambang pintu rumah tidak menjadi poroniec, melainkan kłobuk, roh pelindung rumah. Poroniec mirip myling dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia.
long_description.en: The belief gave rise to many taboos for pregnant women and new mothers, such as drawing water from a well, taking a baby outdoors or having sex. A fetus buried under the house threshold did not become a poroniec but a kłobuk, a protective house spirit. The poroniec resembles the myling of Scandinavian folklore.

short_description.id: Sea Mither adalah makhluk mitos cerita rakyat Orkney yang tinggal di laut pada musim panas, mengurung nuckelavee, dan setiap musim semi berperang dengan Teran, roh badai musim dingin.
short_description.en: Sea Mither is a mythical being of Orcadian folklore who lives in the sea in summer, confines the nuckelavee, and each spring battles Teran, spirit of winter storms.

long_description.id: Sea Mither, atau Mither of the Sea, adalah makhluk mitos cerita rakyat Orkney (Orcadian folklore) yang tinggal di laut pada musim panas, ketika ia mengurung nuckelavee yang jahat di kedalaman laut. Setiap musim semi ia bertarung dengan musuh bebuyutannya Teran, roh legenda Orkney yang dapat menimbulkan badai musim dingin hebat, untuk menguasai laut dan cuaca. Akhirnya ia mengalahkan Teran dan mengirimnya ke dasar laut, tetapi usaha itu melelahkannya hingga pada musim gugur Teran merebut kendali lagi. Kisah Sea Mither dan Teran termasuk legenda tertua Orkney, mungkin diciptakan untuk menjelaskan perubahan cuaca.
long_description.en: In the folklore of Orkney, Sea Mither (the Mither of the Sea) is a spirit who lives in the sea through the summer, when she keeps the demonic nuckelavee bound in the ocean depths. Every spring she fights her arch-enemy Teran, another Orkney spirit able to raise fierce winter storms, for mastery of sea and weather. In the end she beats Teran and banishes him to the deep, but the effort wears her out until in autumn Teran seizes control again. Tales of Sea Mither and Teran are among Orkney's oldest legends, perhaps devised to explain the whims of the weather.

long_description.id: Di Shetland, para nelayan memohon perlindungan Sea Mither dari Iblis. Mither adalah varian Skotlandia (Scots) untuk "mother", dan nama Teran dalam dialek Orkney berarti "amarah besar". Keduanya tak terlihat oleh manusia; pertarungan musim semi mereka, yang disebut "Vore tullye", menimbulkan angin kencang dan laut bergolak. Selama musim panas ia juga memberi makhluk laut kemampuan berkembang biak dan menghangatkan serta menenangkan laut. Menurut artikel ru, kisah Sea Mither dan Teran termasuk legenda Orkney tertua yang diketahui.
long_description.en: In Shetland, fishermen ask Sea Mither to protect them from the Devil. Mither is the Scots form of 'mother', and Teran in Orkney dialect means 'furious anger'. Both are invisible to people; their spring struggle, the 'Vore tullye', brings gales and heaving seas. Through the summer she also gives sea creatures the power to breed and warms and calms the waters. According to the ru article the tales of Sea Mither and Teran are among the oldest known Orkney legends.

short_description.id: Seonaidh (Shony) adalah roh air di Pulau Lewis, Skotlandia, menurut Martin Martin, yang diberi persembahan ale agar mengirim rumput laut.
short_description.en: The Seonaidh (Shony) was a water spirit of Lewis in Scotland, per Martin Martin, offered ale in return for seaweed.

long_description.id: Seonaidh (dibakukan dalam bahasa Inggris sebagai Shony atau Shoney) adalah roh air di Lewis menurut Martin Martin. Kamus Dwelly mendefinisikan bentuk terkait seonadh sebagai "tenung, sihir" dan "Druidisme". Penduduk Lewis berkumpul di gereja St. Mulway (Mael rubha), setiap keluarga menyumbang sekantong malt, dan semuanya diseduh menjadi ale.
long_description.en: The Seonaidh (anglicised Shony or Shoney) was a water spirit of Lewis according to Martin Martin. Dwelly's dictionary glosses the related form seonadh as 'augury, sorcery' and 'Druidism'. The people of Lewis would gather at the church of St. Mulway (Mael rubha), each family giving a bag of malt, which was all brewed into ale.

long_description.id: Seorang dipilih untuk berjalan ke laut sampai sepinggang membawa secawan ale, lalu berseru memohon Seonaidh mengirim banyak rumput laut untuk menyuburkan tanah, dan menuangkan ale ke laut; upacara ini dilakukan malam hari. Kemungkinan Seonaidh semula semacam dewa yang pemujaannya sedikit dikristenkan, atau namanya, bentuk Gaelik Skotlandia untuk Johnny, merujuk pada salah satu Santo Yohanes.
long_description.en: One man was picked to wade waist-deep into the sea with a cup of ale, call on Seonaidh to send plenty of seaweed to enrich the land, and pour the ale into the waves, all done at night. Seonaidh may once have been a god whose cult was lightly Christianised, or the name, the Scottish Gaelic form of Johnny, may point to one of the Saints John.

short_description.id: Skuld adalah putri dalam legenda Skandinavia, saudari tiri Raja Denmark Hrólfr Kraki dan istri pembunuhnya, Hjörvarðr; dalam saga ia penyihir.
short_description.en: Skuld is a princess of Scandinavian legend, half-sister of the Danish king Hrólfr Kraki and wife of his killer Hjörvarðr; the sagas make her a sorceress.

long_description.id: Skuld (juga Sculd, Skulde atau Skulda) adalah putri dalam legenda Skandinavia, saudari atau saudari tiri Raja Denmark legendaris Hrólfr Kraki dan istri pembunuh Hrólfr, Hjörvarðr. Dalam beberapa sumber, seperti Hrólfs saga kraka, ia menghasut suaminya untuk menggulingkan raja. Namanya, sama dengan Skuld salah satu norn, berasal dari kata kerja Norse Kuno skulla, "harus/akan". Menurut saga itu, ia putri Helgi dengan perempuan elf.
long_description.en: Skuld (also Sculd, Skulde or Skulda) is a princess in Scandinavian legend; she was a full or half sister of Hrólfr Kraki, the legendary Danish king, and married Hjörvarðr, the man who killed him. Several sources, among them Hrólfs saga kraka, have her urge her husband to topple the king. Her name, shared with Skuld the norn, comes from the Old Norse verb skulla, 'shall, ought to be'. In that saga she is Helgi's daughter by an elf-woman.

long_description.id: Skuld mengumpulkan pasukan besar berisi prajurit kuat, penjahat, elf dan norn, dan memakai seiðr (sihir) untuk menyembunyikannya dari Hrólfr. Mereka menyerang Lejre saat Yule; Skuld merapal mantra terkuat untuk membangkitkan prajuritnya yang gugur, hingga Hrólfr dan sebelas jagoannya tewas. Ia menjadi Ratu Denmark tetapi memerintah buruk dan singkat, sebelum ditangkap pasukan Swedia dan disiksa hingga mati sebagai balasan.
long_description.en: Skuld raised a great army of strong warriors, outlaws, elves and norns and used seiðr, sorcery, to hide it from Hrólfr. They fell on Lejre at Yule; Skuld cast her mightiest spell to raise her fallen warriors, until Hrólfr and eleven of his champions died. She became Queen of Denmark but ruled badly and briefly before a Swedish force seized her and she was tortured to death in revenge.

famous_for.en: Brief Queen of Denmark.

short_description.id: Takhayul orang Rusia adalah kumpulan kepercayaan dan kebiasaan sehari-hari, seperti duduk sejenak sebelum bepergian atau tidak bersiul di dalam rumah.
short_description.en: The superstitions of Russians are a body of everyday beliefs and habits, such as sitting a moment before a journey or not whistling indoors.

long_description.id: Banyak takhayul orang Rusia menjadi bagian kehidupan sehari-hari, dan sebagian bahkan dianggap etiket sosial biasa. Pengaruhnya berbeda-beda menurut daerah dan usia. Contohnya, sebelum perjalanan jauh, pelancong dan pengantarnya duduk sejenak dalam diam sebelum meninggalkan rumah.
long_description.en: Many Russian superstitions are part of everyday life, and some are even treated as ordinary social etiquette. Their influence varies by region and age. For example, before a long journey travellers and those seeing them off sit for a moment in silence before leaving the house.

long_description.id: Takhayul lain melarang bersiul di dalam rumah karena mendatangkan kesulitan uang, berjabat tangan atau memberi barang di ambang pintu, dan meletakkan botol kosong di meja; botol kosong harus ditaruh di lantai. Bila diberi hewan, orang membayar uang simbolis seperti satu rubel.
long_description.en: Other superstitions forbid whistling indoors, which brings money trouble, shaking hands or handing things over on the threshold, and putting an empty bottle back on the table; it must go on the floor. When given an animal, people pay a symbolic sum such as one rouble.

who.id: Ini kumpulan takhayul sehari-hari orang Rusia.
who.en: This is a body of everyday Russian superstitions.

origin.id: Takhayul ini berasal dari tradisi Rusia.
origin.en: These superstitions come from Russian tradition.

role.en: They govern everyday habits.

famous_for.id: Contoh terkenal adalah duduk sejenak sebelum bepergian.
famous_for.en: A well-known example is sitting a moment before a journey.

did_you_know.id: Dalam takhayul Rusia, botol kosong harus diletakkan di lantai, bukan di meja.
did_you_know.en: In Russian superstition an empty bottle must go on the floor, not the table.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa sebagian takhayul berubah menjadi etiket sosial?
learning_questions.en: Why do some superstitions turn into social etiquette?

claims.quote: Many superstition of Russians are staples of everyday life, and some are even considered common social etiquette despite being rooted in superstition. The influence of these traditions and superstitions varies, and their perceived importance depends on factors such as region and age.

statement.id: Banyak takhayul orang Rusia menjadi bagian kehidupan sehari-hari, sebagian bahkan dianggap etiket sosial biasa walaupun berakar pada takhayul; pengaruh dan pentingnya bergantung pada faktor seperti daerah dan usia.
statement.en: Many Russian superstitions are staples of everyday life, some even treated as ordinary social etiquette despite their roots in superstition; their influence and perceived importance depend on factors such as region and age.

claims.quote: Before leaving for a long journey, travelers, and all those who are seeing them off, must sit for a moment in silence before leaving the house. It is often seen as a time to sit and think of anything one may have forgotten.

statement.id: Sebelum berangkat ke perjalanan jauh, pelancong dan semua yang mengantarnya harus duduk sejenak dalam diam sebelum meninggalkan rumah, yang sering dianggap waktu untuk memikirkan apa saja yang mungkin terlupa.
statement.en: Before leaving on a long journey, travellers and everyone seeing them off must sit for a moment in silence before leaving the house, often seen as a moment to think of anything forgotten.

claims.quote: Ne sifflez jamais dans un appartement, sinon vous aurez des problèmes d'argent et le propriétaire de l'appartement aussi.

statement.id: Jangan pernah bersiul di dalam rumah, karena Anda dan pemilik rumah akan kesulitan uang.
statement.en: Never whistle indoors, or you and the owner of the flat will have money problems.

claims.quote: Ne pas serrer la main de quelqu'un ou donner quelque chose en se tenant sur le seuil de la porte.

statement.id: Jangan berjabat tangan atau memberikan sesuatu sambil berdiri di ambang pintu.
statement.en: Do not shake hands or hand something over while standing on the threshold.

claims.quote: Dès qu'une bouteille est vide, ne la reposez pas sur la table mais sur le sol.

statement.id: Begitu botol kosong, jangan diletakkan kembali di meja, tetapi di lantai.
statement.en: Once a bottle is empty, do not put it back on the table but on the floor.

claims.quote: Quand un animal vous est offert, il faut donner une somme d'argent symbolique, par exemple un rouble.

statement.id: Bila diberi hewan, seseorang harus memberi uang simbolis, misalnya satu rubel.
statement.en: When given an animal, one should pay a symbolic sum, for example one rouble.

short_description.id: Peri gigi adalah tokoh masa kanak-kanak budaya Barat yang datang saat anak tidur dan menukar gigi susu di bawah bantal dengan uang, tercatat pertama kali pada 1908.
short_description.en: The tooth fairy is a Western childhood figure who comes while a child sleeps and swaps a milk tooth under the pillow for money, first recorded in 1908.

long_description.id: Peri gigi adalah tokoh masa kanak-kanak dalam budaya Barat: anak menaruh gigi susu yang tanggal di bawah bantal atau di meja samping ranjang, lalu peri gigi menggantinya dengan sedikit uang saat ia tidur. Catatan tertua tradisi ini berasal dari Chicago Daily Tribune tahun 1908. Takhayul lebih tua tentang gigi anak antara lain pembakaran gigi susu di Inggris dan ketakutan bahwa penyihir dapat menguasai orang lewat giginya.
long_description.en: The tooth fairy is a childhood figure of Western culture: a child puts a lost milk tooth under the pillow or on the bedside table, and the tooth fairy swaps it for a little money while the child sleeps. The earliest record of the tradition is in the Chicago Daily Tribune in 1908. Older superstitions about children's teeth include burning milk teeth in England and fear that witches could control people through their teeth.

long_description.id: Rupanya tidak tetap; kajian Rosemary Wells tahun 1984 menemukan sebagian besar orang membayangkannya perempuan. Padanannya di negeri lain antara lain la Petite Souris dan Ratoncito Pérez, sedangkan di Jepang gigi susu dilempar ke atap atau kolong lantai.
long_description.en: Its looks are not fixed; Rosemary Wells's 1984 study found most people imagine it female. Counterparts elsewhere include la Petite Souris and Ratoncito Pérez, while in Japan milk teeth are thrown onto the roof or under the floor.

role.en: Swaps teeth for money.

famous_for.id: Gigi di bawah bantal.

claims.quote: The tooth fairy is a folkloric figure of early childhood in Western and Western-influenced cultures. The folklore states that when children lose one of their baby teeth, they should place it underneath their pillow or on their bedside table; the tooth fairy will visit while they sleep, replacing the lost tooth with a small payment.

statement.id: Peri gigi adalah tokoh cerita rakyat masa kanak-kanak dalam budaya Barat dan yang terpengaruh Barat: anak yang tanggal gigi susunya menaruhnya di bawah bantal atau di meja samping ranjang, lalu peri gigi datang saat ia tidur dan menggantinya dengan sedikit uang.
statement.en: The tooth fairy is a childhood folklore figure in Western and Western-influenced cultures: a child who loses a milk tooth puts it under the pillow or on the bedside table, and the tooth fairy comes during sleep and replaces it with a small payment.

claims.quote: Children in England were instructed to burn their baby teeth, on pain of spending eternity searching for the baby teeth in the afterlife. Fear of witches was another reason to bury or burn teeth.

statement.en: In the Middle Ages English children were told to burn their milk teeth or spend eternity searching for them in the afterlife, and fear of witches was another reason to bury or burn teeth.

claims.quote: In medieval Europe, it was thought that a witch could assume total power over someone if they were to obtain one of their teeth.

statement.id: Di Eropa abad pertengahan, penyihir dipercaya dapat menguasai seseorang sepenuhnya bila memperoleh salah satu giginya.
statement.en: In medieval Europe a witch was thought to gain total power over someone by obtaining one of their teeth.

claims.quote: While these beliefs may have had an influence, the earliest known record of the tooth fairy tradition itself is a 1908 "Household Hints" item in the Chicago Daily Tribune

statement.id: Catatan tertua tradisi peri gigi sendiri adalah rubrik "Household Hints" tahun 1908 di Chicago Daily Tribune.
statement.en: The earliest known record of the tooth fairy tradition itself is a 1908 'Household Hints' item in the Chicago Daily Tribune.

claims.quote: Unlike Santa Claus and, to a lesser extent, the Easter Bunny, there are few details of the tooth fairy's appearance that are consistent in various versions of the myth.

statement.id: Berbeda dari Sinterklas dan Kelinci Paskah, hanya sedikit rincian rupa peri gigi yang sama di berbagai versi.
statement.en: Unlike Santa Claus and the Easter Bunny, few details of the tooth fairy's looks are consistent across versions.

claims.quote: A 1984 study conducted by Rosemary Wells revealed that most – 74% of those surveyed – believed the tooth fairy to be female, while 12% believed the tooth fairy to be neither male nor female, and 8% believed the tooth fairy could be either male or female.

statement.id: Kajian Rosemary Wells tahun 1984 menemukan 74% responden menganggap peri gigi perempuan, 12% bukan lelaki maupun perempuan, dan 8% bisa keduanya.
statement.en: A 1984 study by Rosemary Wells found 74% of respondents thought the tooth fairy female, 12% neither male nor female, and 8% either.

statement.en: According to the Indonesian article, leaving a tooth under the pillow for the tooth fairy is practised across the Anglosphere.

statement.en: According to the Japanese article, the tooth fairy (German Zahnfee, French la Petite Souris, Spanish Ratoncito Pérez) exchanges lost milk teeth for coins or gifts.

statement.en: In Japan a lost upper milk tooth is thrown under the floor and a lower one towards the roof from a veranda or window.

short_description.id: Topielec atau utopiec adalah roh air Slavia, jiwa orang yang mati tenggelam, yang menyeret manusia ke rawa dan danau.
short_description.en: Topielec or utopiec is a Slavic water spirit, the soul of someone who drowned, that drags people into swamps and lakes.

long_description.id: Topielec, juga disebut utopiec, vodník, atau topnik, adalah nama bagi roh air dalam kepercayaan Slavia. Utopce adalah jiwa manusia yang mati tenggelam dan tetap tinggal di air tempat mereka meninggal. Mereka dipercaya menyeret orang ke rawa dan danau serta membunuh hewan yang berdiri di dekat air tenang.
long_description.en: Topielec, also called utopiec, vodník or topnik, is a name for water spirits in Slavic belief. The utopce are the souls of people who drowned and remain in the water where they died. They are believed to drag people into swamps and lakes and to kill animals standing near still water.

long_description.id: Roh air orang tenggelam masih populer dalam cerita rakyat pedesaan Polandia pada pergantian abad ke-19 ke-20, seperti tampak dalam novel Chłopi karya Władysław Reymont yang meraih Hadiah Nobel.
long_description.en: Water spirits of the drowned were still popular in rural Polish folklore around the turn of the 19th to 20th century, as Władysław Reymont's Nobel-winning novel Chłopi shows.

claims.quote: Utopiec (plural Utopce), Vodník or Topnik is a name applied to Slavic spirits of water. The utopce are spirits of human souls that died drowning, residing in the element of their own demise. They are responsible for sucking people into swamps and lakes as well as killing the animals standing near the still waters.

statement.id: Utopiec (jamak utopce), Vodník, atau Topnik adalah nama roh air Slavia; utopce adalah jiwa manusia yang mati tenggelam dan tinggal di air tempat mereka mati, menyeret orang ke rawa dan danau serta membunuh hewan di dekat air tenang.
statement.en: Utopiec (plural utopce), Vodník or Topnik is a name for Slavic water spirits; the utopce are souls of the drowned living in the water where they died, sucking people into swamps and lakes and killing animals near still water.

claims.quote: O topielce são espíritos de almas humanas que morreram se afogando, residindo no elemento de seu próprio falecimento.

statement.en: The topielce are spirits of human souls who died by drowning, living in the element of their own death.

claims.quote: Slavonic water spirits of the drowned dead remained a popular element of rural Polish folklore at the turn of the 19th and 20th century, as shown by Władysław Reymont in his Nobel Prize-winning novel Chłopi (The Peasants).

statement.id: Roh air Slavia dari orang yang mati tenggelam tetap populer dalam cerita rakyat pedesaan Polandia pada pergantian abad ke-19 dan ke-20 (19th, 20th), seperti ditunjukkan Władysław Reymont dalam novel Chłopi (Para Petani) yang meraih Hadiah Nobel.
statement.en: Slavic water spirits of the drowned remained popular in rural Polish folklore at the turn of the 19th and 20th century, as Władysław Reymont showed in his Nobel Prize-winning novel Chłopi (The Peasants).

claims.quote: A more recent example of the utopiec in Polish popular culture is the comic book series Lil and Put, where the two titular characters are constantly at odds with an Utopiec living in a pond next to their village.

statement.id: Contoh utopiec dalam budaya populer Polandia yang lebih baru adalah serial komik Lil dan Put (Lil i Put), yang dua tokoh utamanya terus berselisih dengan utopiec di kolam dekat desa mereka.
statement.en: A more recent example in Polish popular culture is the comic series Lil and Put (Lil i Put), whose two title characters are constantly at odds with an utopiec in a pond next to their village.

selection_criteria: computeFillStatus must be lengkap-informasi: complete, valid research without an approved image.
No active editorial artwork and no permanent artwork exclusion.
The accepted research entry is embedded unchanged; the image may only depict what its claims document.
Creatures an earlier batch left out keep that reason as catatan_sebelumnya; the generator may decline them with status tidak-digambar.

user_policy.fidelity: Do not invent. Every bodily feature, attribute and the scene must follow the documented claims of this research entry.
user_policy.presence: The being must not read as an ordinary human or an ordinary animal. Use its documented distinguishing traits, plus pose, expression, gaze, scale, setting from its stories and natural lighting, so the feel of the tradition comes through. Add no undocumented anatomy.
user_policy.aura: Character presence through pose, expression, framing, scale, atmosphere and natural lighting. No generic glowing envelope, neon outline, energy ribbons or luminous coloured mist. Magical effects only when documented, and restrained. Frightening beings get an appropriate horror atmosphere; benevolent beings stay appropriate to their tradition.
user_policy.style: Same house style as the existing 1,000 illustrations: square premium painterly naturalistic illustration, no text, labels, logo, border or watermark.
